title: Feature request: Allow additional text in function @template block
process scripts not part of a package
description:
There used to be a package called  [document](https://cran.r-project.org/package=document)  on CRAN and on [gitlab](https://gitlab.com/fvafrCU/document) that, given an R script with roxygen markup, would produce pdf, html and txt reference manuals.  It provided an easy path to developing a package since the same scripts could later be incorporated into an eventual package. It called the the roxygen2 package to perform the actual documentation.  That package was recently removed from CRAN.

It would be useful if this functionality were incorporated into roxygen2 itself or it could be a separate package that used roxygen2. There are likely many more people who write scripts than write packages and this would likely make roxygen2 more widely used.  Also it would provide an easy path from writing a script to an eventual package.

There still exists the [docstrings](https://cran.r-project.org/package=docstrings) package on CRAN which supports python-like docstrings within functions using roxygen markup. Like python docstrings it expects the markup to be in the function itself rather than before it and generates interactive help rather than manuals.  It has not been updated for many years.  This is actually quite a good idea and it might be nice if roxygen2 also supported docstrings.  The advantage of this is that since the roxygen is within the function the docstrings help system can find it if the function is loaded given only the function without knowing what script it came from.

There is also the [box](https://cran.r-project.org/package=box) package on CRAN which can be used for generating interactive help from roxygen markup but its focus is on modules rather than documentation and like docstrings it does not generate manuals.  

There are really several possible features here:
- generate reference manual from script
- an interactive help command that given an roxygen documented function from a script shows the help
- allow docstrings as an alternative to the existing way roxygen works and possibly have a conversion function to go back and forth.

title: Conditional cross-references of `Suggest`ed packages
description:
There are times when I want to cross-reference a help page in another package but I don't necessarily need my users to have that package installed, e.g., because the package's functions are used no where else in my package and the cross-reference is just to provide users with additional (optional) information. This suggests the package should be in my package's `Suggests`. However, CRAN requires that a package can be built without packages in `Suggests`; normally this would create a failure if the cross-referenced package is only in `Suggests` and not `Imports`. To avoid this problem, I use conditional cross-references in my packages that don't use `roxygen2`. This works using the following Rd syntax:

```
\ifelse{\Sexpr[results=rd,stage=render]{requireNamespace("foo", quietly = TRUE)}}{\code{\link[foo:bar]{foo::bar()}}}{\code{foo::bar()}}
```

So, when package `foo` is installed, this expands to `\code{\link[foo:bar]{foo::bar()}}`, a cross-reference to `foo::bar` with text that appears like `foo::bar()`, and when `foo` isn't installed, this expands to `\code{foo::bar()}`, text that appears like `foo::bar()` without a cross-reference. Because I set `stage=render`, the cross-references are checked and activated whenever the help page is loaded.

I am wondering if `roxygen2` could implement such an expansion when using, e.g., `[foo::bar()]`. For `Import`ed packages, this doesn't change anything because the package is installed. For `Suggest`ed packages, this creates a failsafe against improper cross-references to packages not installed while ensuring the correct cross-reference when the package is installed. This keeps the installation of the package lean (i.e., `foo` can be `Suggest`ed and doesn't need to be installed), staisfies CRAN's requirements for the package to be able to be built without `Suggest`ed packages installed, and still provides the user with the potential for a helpful cross-reference. In this way, it functions similarly to the `@examplesif` tag.

In my packages, I use the following macro to create `\pkgfun{}{}`, which implements the conditional cross-reference above.
```
\newcommand{\pkgfun}{\ifelse{\Sexpr[results=rd,stage=render]{requireNamespace("#1", quietly = TRUE)}}{\code{\link[#1:#2]{#1::#2()}}}{\code{#1::#2()}}}
```

I'm hoping something like this could be implemented in `roxygen2`. Thank you for considering my suggestion.

title: inheritParams does not find doc'ed multi-params
description:
When multiple parameters are documented in a single `@param` or `\arguments{ \item{a, b}{} }`, the referent documentation does not include the documentation of that parameter.

### Minimal example

```r
#' test function
#' This is a test function
#' @return A message
#'
#' @inheritParams testing
#'
#' @export
test <- function(b) {
    message("This is a test")
}


#' Another test function
#' @param a,b character(1) A letter, either lowercase or uppercase
#' @return Another message
#'
#' @export
testing <- function(a, b) {
    message("This is also a test")
}
```

The `test` function does not get any generated documentation for argument `b` even though it inherits the arguments of the `testing` function which are documented.

### Expected behavior

`test.Rd` should have the following included:

```Rd
\arguments{
\item{b}{character(1) A letter, either lowercase or uppercase}
}
```

### Observed behavior

The `\arguments` section is missing from the `test.Rd`.

### Roxygen version

`RoxygenNote: 7.2.1` 

### Example repository

https://github.com/Link-NY/testPkg

cc: @hadley

title: @describeIn throws error when used with S4 methods.
description:
I thought a perfect example of a use of `@describeIn` was describing generic functions and methods in a class definition.

So here is a code snippet which I thought would work:
```#' Class \code{"MongoRec"}
#'
#'
#' This is a lightweight class meant to be extended.  It contains a
#' single field for a mongo identifier, which can be accessed using
#' the `m_id()` method.  It is meant to store something that is a
#' record in a mongo collection, where `_id` is the mongo identifier.
#'
#'
#'
#' @name MongoRec-class
#' @aliases MongoRec-class m_id,MongoRec-method m_id<-,MongoRec-method
#' as.jlist,MongoRec,list-method as.json,MongoRec-method
#' @docType class
#' @section Objects from the Class:
#'
#' Objects can be created by calls to the \code{\link{MongoRec}()} function.
#' @author Russell G. Almond
#' @seealso \code{\link{MongoRec}()} --- constructor
#' \code{\link{as.json}},
#' \code{\link{parseObject}}, \code{\link{saveRec}}, \code{\link{getOneRec}}
#' @keywords classes
#' @examples
#'
#' showClass("MongoRec")
#'
#' @exportClass("MongoRec")
setClass("MongoRec",
         slots=c("_id"="character"    #Mongo ID
                 ))
#' @describeIn MongoRec Accessor for Mongo id.
setGeneric("m_id",function(x) standardGeneric("m_id"))

#' @describeIn MongoRec Accessor for Mongo id.
setGeneric("m_id<-",function(x, value) standardGeneric("m_id<-"))

#' @describeIn MongoRec Accessor for Mongo id.
setMethod("m_id","MongoRec", function(x) x@"_id")

#' @describeIn MongoRec  Accessor for Mongo id.
setMethod("m_id<-","MongoRec", function(x,value) {
  names(value) <- "oid"
  x@"_id" <- value
  x})
```
However, I get
```
Error in merge.rd_section_minidesc(self$get_section(type), section) : 
  identical(x$value$type, y$value$type) is not TRUE
```
(This is the same error referenced in my previous issue, about there not being sufficient context information with the error).

However, I think this should be a case where `@describeIn` works (or at least it needs better documentation as to what works and why).  

Note, I get a similiar error, if I move the documentation to the `m_id` generic function and try to use `@describeIn m_id` for the other generic and the two methods.

title: Create a list of the supported @tags
description:
As per the discussion in #1079, the roxygen2 documentation is currently missing a comprehensive overview list of the supported `@tags`. Most (but not all!) tags are currently [documented in the “rd” vignette](https://roxygen2.r-lib.org/articles/rd.html). However, that vignette also does not include a list overview of the supported tags, and searching for a suitable tag is not always trivial if the user does not know its exact name. I suggest either having a separate page or a “table of contents” like list at the beginning of the “rd” vignette, which lists all supported tags with hyperlinks to the documents/sections where they are explained. For reference, here is a list of the tags that seem to be currently undocumented.
Undocumented @tags * `@author` * `@docType` * `@encoding` * `@evalNamespace` * `@exportClass` * `@exportMethod` * `@exportPattern` * `@exportS3Method` * `@import` * `@importClassesFrom` * `@importFrom` * `@importMethodsFrom` * `@include` * `@inheritDotParams` * `@md` * `@noMd` * `@noRd` * `@note` * `@rawNamespace` * `@rawRd` * `@returns` * `@usage` * `@useDynLib`
Code to generate the list ```r tags = sub('.*\\.roxy_tag_', '', as.character(methods('roxy_tag_parse')))[-1L] vignette_file = system.file(file.path('doc', vignette('rd')$PDF), package = 'roxygen2') vignette = paste(readLines(vignette_file), collapse = '') missing = vapply(paste0('@', tags, '\\b'), Negate(grepl), logical(1L), vignette) tags[missing] ```

title: Inherit the same section from multiple functions
description:
Reprex: 

```r
temp_pkg <- file.path(tempdir(), "test")
usethis::create_package(temp_pkg, open = FALSE)

source <- "
#' Function f
#'
#' @examples
#' f()
f <- function() {
  message('I am f')
}
#' Function g
#' 
#' @examples
#' g()
g <- function() {
  message('I am g')
}
#' Function h
#' 
#' @inherit f examples
#' @inherit g examples
h <- function() {
  message('I am h')
}
"

write(source, file.path(temp_pkg, "R", "test.R"))

roxygen2::roxygenise(temp_pkg)

file.show(file.path(temp_pkg, "man", "h.Rd"))
```

In `h.Rd`, I would like to see 

```
\examples{
f()
g()
}
```

instead of 

```
\examples{
f()
}
```

In other words, when the same section is inherited from multiple functions, the result should be concatenated to create the new section.

This would be particularly useful to gather references from multiple functions in a single place.

title: Failures with inline R code in multiline @param tags
description: Consider the following `@param` tag: ```r #' @param some_param Some dynamically generated parameter documentation whose last 2 static #' chars are swallowed and instead contains a spurious ")'" at the end: 12`r paste0("test")` ``` When roxygen2 (latest 7.1.1.9001) renders this to `.Rd`, it **swallows the last two "static" characters** (`12`) **and outputs two additional characters** (``)` ``) at the end of the parsed inline R code which shouldn't be there: ```rd \item{some_param}{Some dynamically generated parameter documentation whose last 2 static chars are swallowed and instead contains a spurious ")'" at the end: test)`} ``` Instead, it should actually produce this `.Rd`: ```rd \item{some_param}{Some dynamically generated parameter documentation whose last 2 static chars are swallowed and instead contains a spurious ")'" at the end: 12test} ``` The underlying issue looks like some "off-by-two"-error. The inline R code ``` ... at the end: 12`r paste0("test")` ``` should be parsed to: ``` ... at the end: 12test ``` but wrongly becomes: ``` ... at the end: test)` ``` I simplified the inline R code in the above example as much as possible, thus it doesn't make much sense. What I was originally trying to do is auto-generate some doc in pkgsnip like this: ```r #' @param snippet The name of a snippet. Possible values include: #' `r paste0('- ``"', ls_file_snips()$name, '"``')` ```

title: New namespace vignette content formerly in R packages
description:
### S3  {#export-s3}

If you want others to be able to create instances of an S3 class, `@export` the constructor function. S3 generics are just regular R functions, you can `@export` them like functions. 

S3 methods represent the most complicated case because there are four different scenarios:

* A method for an exported generic: export every method.

* A method for an internal generic: technically, you don't need to export
  these methods. However, I recommend exporting every S3 method you write
  because it's simpler and makes it less likely that you'll introduce hard to 
  find bugs. Use `devtools::missing_s3()` to list all S3 methods that 
  you've forgotten to export.

* A method for a generic in a required package. You'll need to import the
  generic (see below), and export the method.

* A method for a generic in a suggested package. Namespace directives must
  refer to available functions, so they can not reference suggested packages. 
  It's possible to use package hooks and code to add this at run-time,
  but this is sufficiently complicated that I currently wouldn't recommend it.
  Instead, you'll have to design your package dependencies in a way that avoids this 
  scenario.

### S4 {#export-s4}

S4 classes: if you want others to be able to extend your class, `@export` it.
If you want others to create instances of your class but not to extend it,
`@export` the constructor function, not the class.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Can extend and create with new("A", ...)
#' @export
setClass("A")

# Can extend and create with new("B", ...). You can use B()
# to construct instances in your own code, but others can not
#' @export
B <- setClass("B")

# Can create with C(...) and new("C", ...), but can't create
# a subclass that extends C
#' @export C
C <- setClass("C")

# Can extend and create with D(...) or new("D", ...)
#' @export D
#' @exportClass D
D <- setClass("D")
```

S4 generics: `@export` if you want the generic to be publicly usable.

S4 methods: you only need to `@export` methods for generics that you did not define. But I think it's a good idea to `@export` every method: that way you don't need to remember whether or not you created the generic.

### RC {#export-rc}

The principles used for S4 classes apply here. Note that due to the way that RC is currently implemented, it's typically impossible for your classes to be extended outside of your package.

### Data {#export-data}

As you'll learn about in [data](#data), files that live in `data/` don't use the usual namespace mechanism and don't need to be exported.

title: Clarify version needed for dynamic R code
description:
## Introduction

I am trying to use for the first time markdown inline code markup to evaluate R code and insert its output into the manual page, as described here: https://roxygen2.r-lib.org/articles/rd-formatting.html#dynamic-r-code.

The real context is in a package but I am putting here a minimal working example as requested in the support guidelines, i.e., using reprex and `roc_proc_text()`.

So the problem is that the inline R code does not evaluate. In my package I have added the line `Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE)` to `DESCRIPTION`.

## MWE
``` r
doc <- "
#' dummy
#'
#' Roxygen created this manual page on `r Sys.Date()` using R version
#' `r getRversion()`.
#'
#' # Custom section
#' ## Custom subsection
#' The `iris` data set has `r ncol(iris)` columns:
#' `r paste0('``', colnames(iris), '``', collapse = ', ')`.
#'
#' @name dummy
#'
NULL
"

library(roxygen2)
roc_proc_text(rd_roclet(), doc)
#> $dummy.Rd
#> % Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
#> % Please edit documentation in ./<text>
#> \name{dummy}
#> \alias{dummy}
#> \title{dummy}
#> \description{
#> Roxygen created this manual page on `r Sys.Date()` using R version
#> `r getRversion()`.
#> }
#> \details{
#> # Custom section
#> ## Custom subsection
#> The `iris` data set has `r ncol(iris)` columns:
#> `r paste0('``', colnames(iris), '``', collapse = ', ')`.
#> }
packageVersion('roxygen2')
#> [1] '7.0.2'
R.version.string
#> [1] "R version 3.6.0 (2019-04-26)"
```

<sup>Created on 2020-04-24 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

title: Export S4 class generator function
description:
The documentation for [`setClass`](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/methods/versions/3.6.2/topics/setClass) explains that the function returns a class generator object, which can be invoked like `new`, but since it's an actual function it can be accessed via the `::` operator, and therefore offers safety and convenience to users. BioConductor do something like this by defining their own constructor functions, but I see the return value of `setClass` as R's convenient, built-in version of that.

Unfortunately, though, roxygen2 doesn't allow you to export this generator function automatically. If you add an `@export` to the `setClass` statement, it only exports the class itself, via `exportClass`:
`R/my_class.R`:
```R
#' @export
MyClass = setClass('MyClass', representation(foo='numeric'))
```
`NAMESPACE`:
```
exportClasses(MyClass)
```

***

If try to later annotate an `@export` onto the return value, but separately from the `exportClass`, Roxygen generates a blank export statement:

`R/my_class.R`:
```R
#' @export
MyClass = setClass('MyClass', representation(foo='numeric'))

#' @export
MyClass
```
`NAMESPACE`:
```
export()
exportClasses(MyClass)
```

***

The `NAMESPACE` file that I actually want to be generated is 
```
export(MyClass)
exportClasses(MyClass)
```

As a package developer, I would appreciate a new tag (say `@exportConstructor`), to do this automatically, or else some kind of workaround that allows me to generate the above `NAMESPACE` using Roxygen, instead of adding it manually.

parse_package(
  path = ".",
  env = env_package(path),
  registry = default_tags(),
  global_options = list()
)
```

Within my projects, I follow a (slightly unorthodox) strategy when working with tidy evaluation semantics where I place the default values for input columns as a list of symbols in the signature, which may be overridden with `...`. 

I do this because I like that I don't need to perform redundant documentation of these defaults in the docstring, and convenient tidy semantics may be used if the schema changes. 

# Input

the signature of a typical function might be:

<details>
  <summary>Lengthy Code Block</summary>

```r
#' Combine the journey, diagnosis, and patient dataframes for analysis
#' 
#' Join dataframes with diagnostic and demographic information for the basis 
#' of analysis. 
#' Adds every column present from [journey_acs_trim_relevant], as well as 
#' `gender` and `age` from `patient`, and `icd10_class`, and 
#' `diagnosis_display_id`, as given by [diagnosis_collapse_icd10_groups].
#' 
#' Also adds `journey_sep_mode` and `journey_sep_comment` columns, 
#' corresponding to the `enc_seapration_mode`/`comment` entries for the last
#' encounter of each journey.
#' 
#' @param journeys the journey df as given by [journey_acs_trim_relevant]
#' @param patients the patient df
#' @param diagnosis_i2x the diagnosis df, with icd10 groups collapsed.
#' @param ... unquoted column names to override the schema set by 
#'        `.default_dots`
#' @inheritParams set_default_dots
#' @export
#' @family journeys
journey_analysis_base <- function(
  journeys, diagnosis_i2x, patients,
  .default_dots = rlang::exprs(
    journey_key = JOURNEY_KEY, 
    
    encntr_key = encntr_key, 
    
    person_key = person_key, 
    gender = gender, age = age,
    
    icd10_class = icd10_class,
    diagnosis_display_id = display_identifier_cap,
    enc_separation_mode = enc_separation_mode,
    enc_separation_comment = enc_separation_comment,
    admit_dttm = admit_dttm
  ), 
  ...
) {
  enstr <- rlang::as_name
  
  args <- set_default_dots(.default_dots, ...)
```

```r
#' Assign defaults to dotted inputs
#'
#' `...` is a list of arguments, usually coming from `...` passed directly to
#'  the function.
#' @param .default_dots a named list of (typically) expressions, that specify
#'        default values for args in `...` if they aren't given by `...`
#' @return the input `...`,  with any named args from `.default_dots`
#'         missing from `...` being set by `defaults`.
#' @export
#' @keywords internal
set_default_dots <- function(.default_dots, ...) {
  `%||%` <- rlang::`%||%`
  out <- rlang::enexprs(...)
  defaults <- .default_dots
  
  for (nm in names(defaults)) out[[nm]] <- out[[nm]] %||% defaults[[nm]]
  
  return(out)
}
```

</details>

---

# Output

## Current

Presently, the output looks like this:

```r
journey_analysis_base(
  journeys,
  diagnosis_i2x,
  patients,
  .default_dots = rlang::exprs(journey_key = JOURNEY_KEY, encntr_key = encntr_key,
    person_key = person_key, gender = gender, age = age, icd10_class = icd10_class,
    diagnosis_display_id = display_identifier_cap, enc_separation_mode =
    enc_separation_mode, enc_separation_comment = enc_separation_comment, admit_dttm =
    admit_dttm),
  ...
)
```

ideally, however, I'd really prefer to have the items in `.default_dots` get similar wrapping to top level arguments, or even to just be displayed the same way they were written, since I write these list items for readability when inspecting code

(Though in source code, I'm a bit more concerned with reducing line usage so the source is a little easier to navigate, it's less important to me in rendered docs, as an individual reference page will still be pretty short).

## Desired 

### "as-is"

```r
journey_analysis_base(
  journeys, 
  diagnosis_i2x, 
  patients,
  .default_dots = rlang::exprs(
    journey_key = JOURNEY_KEY, 
    
    encntr_key = encntr_key, 
    
    person_key = person_key, 
    gender = gender, age = age,
    
    icd10_class = icd10_class,
    diagnosis_display_id = display_identifier_cap,
    enc_separation_mode = enc_separation_mode,
    enc_separation_comment = enc_separation_comment,
    admit_dttm = admit_dttm
  ), 
  ...
)
```

### One Line Per Item

```r
journey_analysis_base(
  journeys, 
  diagnosis_i2x, 
  patients,
  .default_dots = rlang::exprs(
    journey_key = JOURNEY_KEY, 
    encntr_key = encntr_key, 
    person_key = person_key, 
    gender = gender,
    age = age,
    icd10_class = icd10_class,
    diagnosis_display_id = display_identifier_cap,
    enc_separation_mode = enc_separation_mode,
    enc_separation_comment = enc_separation_comment,
    admit_dttm = admit_dttm
  ), 
  ...
)
```

I wonder whether you would consider an extension of #820 , allowing: 
* an option for vector elements to be given the same treatment as top level params, 
  or alternatively 
* for function signatures that are not explictly overridden by `@usage` to be parsed/ rendered "as-is", 
  ie, the same way they were typed in the source

Does that sound feasible/ useful to include in roxygen2 ? I know my use-case is pretty specific, but I find myself wanting it very regularly.

title: Implement a better syntax for double dispatch
description:
## Double dispatch methods

```r
#' @method vec_cast.binned double
#' @export
vec_cast.binned.double <- function(x, y, ...) {
}
```

should become

```r
#' @export
vec_cast.binned.double <- function(x, y, ...) {
}
```

roxygen2 takes the *last* dot as the default separator for the method. A few downstream packages might need fixing.

## First-level dispatch

```r
#' @method vec_cast vctrs_percent
#' @export
#' @export vec_cast.vctrs_percent
vec_cast.vctrs_percent <- function(x, to, ...) {
} 
```

should become perhaps

```r
#' @ddexport
vec_cast.vctrs_percent <- function(x, to, ...) {
}
```

## Reference

https://vctrs.r-lib.org/articles/s3-vector.html#appendix-namespace-declarations

title: @describeIn fails when used on S3 method and other funs together
description:
This was already partially addressed #666. (It was probably only partially addressed because I had failed to provide a reprex).

As per #666 and the below test, you *can* now document other functions via `@describeIn` for generics:

https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/blob/b3053b694399416543af877837efb29e6ec34d1f/tests/testthat/test-rd-describe-in.R#L72-L82

However, this fallback isn't triggered when you `@describeIn` methods and other functions together:

```r
library(roxygen2)

  out <- roc_proc_text(rd_roclet(), "
  #' Generic
  # foo <- function(x) {}
  foo <- function(x) UseMethod('foo')

  #' @describeIn foo some method
  as.character.zap <- function(x) c('zap')
  
  #' @describeIn foo related function
  bar <- function(y) {}
")[[1]]
```

yields:

```
Error in merge.rd_section_minidesc(self$get_section(type), section) : 
  identical(x$value$type, y$value$type) is not TRUE
```

Whether the "parent" function (the function you're `@describeIn` *in*) is a normal function or a generic does not seem to matter.
You can trigger the same error with:

```r
library(roxygen2)

  out <- roc_proc_text(rd_roclet(), "
  #' Normal
  foo <- function(x) {}

  #' @describeIn foo some method
  as.character.zap <- function(x) c('zap')
  
  #' @describeIn foo related function
  bar <- function(y) {}
")[[1]]
```

---

#### Motivation

I think this scenario might sometimes happen when documenting new (S3) OO schemes.
For example, you might have a class, and wish to document some (say, print) methods with it, as well as some "normal" functions, such as a validator.


#### More Background

(Not necessary to debug this, but might be helpful to other people who run into this and are confused about the relationship to `vctrs::s3_register()`

You can also run into this problem if you wish to expand other generics (say, `knitr::knit_print()`, which you don't want to `@ImportFrom` (and therefore `Imports:` in your `DESCRIPTION`).
If you then place knitr in your `Suggests:` and dynamically `vctrs::s3_register()` `knit_print` in your `onLoad`, your newly minted method `knit_print.foo()` will then look (to roxygen anyway) as a *normal* function, and will therefore trigger the above error.

title: R6 class inheriting from unexported parent causes check() error
description:
Running `devtools::check()` on an internal package gives the following result:

```
> checking Rd cross-references ... WARNING
  Missing link or links in documentation object 'LiquiditySeekerStrategy.Rd': 
    '[algotrade:Strategy]{algotrade::Strategy}'

  Missing link or links in documentation object 'TWAPStrategy.Rd':
    '[algotrade:Strategy]{algotrade::Strategy}'

  See section 'Cross-references' in the 'Writing R Extensions' manual.        
```

The reason, as far as I can tell, is because my exported `TWAPStrategy` and `LiquiditySeekerStrategy` classes inherit from a parent `Strategy` class, which is private. My documentation markup for the exported classes doesn't include any explicit links to `Strategy`, but it appears that roxygen2 inserts them anyway.

Some sample markup:

```r
#' TWAP strategy class
#'
#' @description
#' This class emulates the TWAP trading stategy.
#' @details
#' The TWAP strategy is the simplest strategy in use. (...)
#' @export
TWAPStrategy <- R6::R6Class("TWAPStrategy", inherit=Strategy, ...)
```

And the start of the corresponding .Rd file:

```
% Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
% Please edit documentation in R/TWAPStrategy.R
\name{TWAPStrategy}
\alias{TWAPStrategy}
\title{TWAP strategy class}
\description{
This class emulates the TWAP trading stategy.
}
\details{
The TWAP strategy is the simplest strategy in use. (...)
}
\section{Super class}{
\code{\link[algotrade:Strategy]{algotrade::Strategy}} -> \code{TWAPStrategy}
}
```
Notice the link to the Strategy class, which `check()` complains about. Should this link be there for an unexported class?

title: Enable non-R knitr engines
description:
I'm trying to include a TikZ image in the docs of a package of mine. While looking at my options, i was delighted to see that `roxygen2` supports `knitr` code chunks. Combined with the `tikz` engine support of `knitr` I thought I had all I needed to make this work. Unfortunately, currently there is a quite restrictive check in place for what is considered a `knitr` code chunk

https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/blob/c73def498f29783044fe50865f22c2482f80942d/R/markdown.R#L73-L77

Playing around with this a bit, I was seamlessly able to generate my TikZ image from code simply by relaxing this check a bit by including other `knitr` engines as reported by `knitr::knit_engines$get()`.

```r
markdown_engine_regexp <- function() {
  opts <- c("r", names(knitr::knit_engines$get()))
  paste0("^\\{(", paste(opts, collapse = "|"), ")[, \\}]")
}

is_markdown_code_node <- function(x) {
  info <- xml_attr(x, "info")
  regx <- markdown_engine_regexp()
  str_sub(xml_text(x), 1, 2) == "r " ||
    (!is.na(info) && grepl(regx, info))
}
```
See also: https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/compare/master...nbenn:master

While I realize that `knitr` support in `roxygen2` is a new and somewhat experimental addition, I was wondering whether you are open to expanding this powerful feature by allowing non-R language engines to be run. I'm happy to submit a PR if this is the case.

It feels like `vignette("vignette-or-article-name")` could get better treatment by roxygen2. For pkgdown reasons (and perhaps just in general), this is the preferred way to refer to a vignette from Rd. And on pkgdown, it's a hyperlink. Could it become a hyperlink in Rd too?

The example that motivated me to open this was an *article*, so there's no local hope of viewing anyway, i.e. you have to read it on the pkgdown site. So executing `vignette("article-name")` locally wouldn't achieve anything but a hyperlink would.

title: R Code that returns character vector is treated differently
description:
Previously we had something similar to: 
```r
#' @description
#' `r c("a", "b")`
add = function(a, b) a + b
```

where `"a"` and `"b"` appeared on individual lines, i.e. were combined using something like`paste(..., collapse = "\n")`

With the latest roxygen 7.2.0 release, this behaviour changed and now pastes the vectors with `", "` instead of `"\n"`

title: CRAN Warning when Non-breaking space in default function argument value
description:
Hi,

Thanks for your time and work on the roxygen2 package. It makes developing R packages much more convenient to me.

I have a function that takes a string with a default value that contains non-breaking spaces. When I use `devtools::document()` and afterwards `devtools::check()` I get a WARNING pointing out a mismatch between my code and the help page.

A minimal function with roxygen documentation that gives the WARNING:

```r
#' A dummy function
#'
#' @param str_with_nbsp A string, potentially with non-breaking spaces
#'
#' @return Not relevant
#' @export
#'
myfun <- function(str_with_nbsp = "x\u00a0=\u00a04") {print(str_with_nbsp)}
```

You can find a minimal package that includes this function, with github actions set up here: https://github.com/zeehio/testnbsp


The CRAN WARNING (not that helpful to read given that the regular space and the non-breaking space look the same...)

```
   Codoc mismatches from documentation object 'myfun':
   myfun
     Code: function(str_with_nbsp = "x = 4")
     Docs: function(str_with_nbsp = "x = 4")
     Mismatches in argument default values:
       Name: 'str_with_nbsp' Code: "x = 4" Docs: "x = 4"
```

Here is some reproducible example that could be easily converted into a unit test for this bug:

``` r
myfun <- function(str_with_nbsp = "x\u00a0=\u00a04") {print(str_with_nbsp)}
# The wrap_usage function replaces all my nbsp characters by regular characters
fun_usage <- roxygen2:::wrap_usage("myfun", identity, formals = formals(myfun))
fun_usage
#> <rd> myfun(str_with_nbsp = "x = 4")
# The nbsp 00a0 character was replaced by regular spaces:
grepl(pattern = "\u00a0", as.character(fun_usage)) # I expected this to be TRUE
#> [1] FALSE
```

<sup>Created on 2022-05-02 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

After looking at the code, I have been able to see that the replacement happens here: https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/blob/630ab47cff290e94380e0bfa57d6de964c722af3/R/rd-usage.R#L145

It feels like first roxygen2 introduces: `\u{A0}=\u{A0}` (in `args_string`). Afterwards it replaces all nbsp with regular spaces. A simple solution would be change the final search and replace so instead of `out <- gsub("\u{A0}", " ", out, useBytes = TRUE)` it becomes `out <- gsub("\u{A0}=\u{A0}", "=", out, useBytes = TRUE)`, so it would replace the non breaking spaces that roxygen adds, but not the ones that were present before.

However I don't know if `\u{A0}` and other UTF-8 characters are still problematic on some Windows locales or not... maybe with the recent changes in Windows support many of these workarounds can now be simplified...

Any help will be very much appreciated :pray:

title: unknown macro '\item' on @inheritDotParams
description:
When I try to use `@inheritDotParams glue::glue_data`,  `devtools::check(pkg)` throws a warning about `unknown macro \item`. My best guess is it comes from `roxygen2` but it could be from `devtools::document()`, `tools::parse_Rd()` or it could be with how it was written in `glue`.

I looks to be an issue in this section re: `.open` and `.close`. `\\\` becomes `\\`, probably because something interpreted it as a character escape

```diff
glue|        \item{.open}{[\code{character(1)}: \sQuote{\\\{}]\cr The opening delimiter...
mine| \item{\code{.open}}{[\code{character(1)}: \sQuote{\\{}]\cr The opening delimiter...
                                                        ^^^^^

glue|        \item{.close}{[\code{character(1)}: \sQuote{\\\}}]\cr The closing delimiter...
mine| \item{\code{.close}}{[\code{character(1)}: \sQuote{\\}}]\cr The closing delimiter...
                                                         ^^^^^
```

| pkg  | R        | Rd        |
|---   |---       |---        |
|glue  | [glue_r] | [glue_rd] |
|mine  | [my_r]   | [my_rd]   |

```r
# create tmp package
tmp <- tempdir()
pkg <- file.path(tmp, "test")
devtools::create(path = pkg)

# add R code
writeLines(
  con = file.path(pkg, "R/test.R"),
  text = 
    "#' does some stuff
    #' @inheritDotParams glue::glue_data
    foo <- function(...) glue_data(...)"
)

# document is ok
devtools::document(pkg) 

# warning: prepare_Rd: ./man/foo.Rd:20: unknown macro '\item'
devtools::check(pkg)

# also throws warning
pkgdown::build_reference(pkg)
# In tools::parse_Rd(path, macros = macros, encoding = "UTF-8") :
#   C:/Users/jake/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpYxG5C2/test/man/foo.Rd:20: unknown macro '\item'

# remove temp directory
unlink(tmp, recursive = TRUE)
```


[glue_r]: https://github.com/tidyverse/glue/blob/d47d6c7701f738f8647b951df418cfd5e6a7bf76/R/glue.R#L15-L18

title: 7.2.0 Confusing error message thrown by `tokenize_file()`
description:
Dear all,

there seems not to be an issue related to this 'problem' yet, I hope I have not overlooked anything.

**Problem/Issue:** After updating my system (Ubuntu `20.04`, R Version `4.2.0`, roxygen2 `7.2.0`) I encountered an confusing error message when documenting my package due to a syntax error in the roxygen comments. The error message:

* `Error: invalid version specification ‘0.68’`

**Origin:** I was able to track it down to `roxygen2:::tokenize_file()` (`roxygenize()` -> `parse_package()` -> `parse_file()` -> `tokenize_file()`). I could not find out where `0.68` originates from but was able to reproduce the problem with a small minimal:

* GIST: <https://gist.github.com/retostauffer/fdaca37ad1ea2f6b9aabbd509feafdb2>

The minimal writes four minimal `.R` scripts with roxygen documentation and a demo function. (1) is correct, (2) returns an readable error message, (3 & 4) return the error shown above.

Not a bug as the problem lies on my side, but the error message is confusing and it took me a while to find the issue (did not happen with R `4.1.0`; cannot tell which roxygen version I was using).

Thanks a lot!

description:
This may be intentional, but I want to check.

In `devtools::check_mac_release()` and `devtools::check_win()`, we have:

``` r
#' @inheritParams pkgbuild::build

<snip, snip>

check_mac_release <- function(pkg = ".", dep_pkgs = character(), args = NULL, manual = TRUE, quiet = FALSE, ...) { ... }
```

The intent and what was happening prior to roxygen2 7.2.0 is that these devtools functions would inherit the docs for `manual` from `pkgbuild::build()`, which look like:

```
#' @param vignettes,manual For source packages: if `FALSE`, don't build PDF
#'   vignettes (`--no-build-vignettes`) or manual (`--no-manual`).
```

That no longer happens (https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/commit/647db331c40e34697bfbf069a4a7d8b18b25cc12).

Is this a known breakage due to the response to #950 and devtools just can't inherit the documentation for `manual` from pkgbuild?

description: If you try and document dplyr with the dev version of roxygen2, I get something like this. It looks like the reexport links are being replicated to the length of the number of functions you are reexporting from that package (i.e. there are 13 tibble reexports and it shows 13 times)

title: Circular warning when inheriting params from `pkgA::foo()` that links back to `pkgB::bar()`
description:
If you document dplyr, you'll see warnings that look like this:

```r
> devtools::document()
ℹ Updating dplyr documentation
ℹ Loading dplyr
Writing NAMESPACE
Warning: Link to unknown topic in inherited text: dplyr::pull
Warning: Link to unknown topic in inherited text: dplyr::pull
Writing NAMESPACE
```

I've tracked this down to the fact that `pull()` has `@inheritParams tidyselect::vars_pull` to get docs for `var`, but then in the docs for `vars_pull()`, we link back to `dplyr::pull()` in two places (hence, two warnings). 

https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/blob/8c55a20823a394f4eba8a53f25f82871dce1cd8e/R/pull.R#L8
https://github.com/r-lib/tidyselect/blob/e2c51de4ada765efa22b620f7766fcac68d88a7f/R/vars-pull.R#L3
https://github.com/r-lib/tidyselect/blob/e2c51de4ada765efa22b620f7766fcac68d88a7f/R/vars-pull.R#L21

I've managed to reproduce this in a minimal way here:

https://github.com/DavisVaughan/testinherit
https://github.com/DavisVaughan/testinheritfrom

If you `devtools::install_github("DavisVaughan/testinheritfrom")` then fork and locally clone {testinherit}, then running `devtools::document()` with {testinherit} should show the same warnings as what we see in dplyr.

The weird part is that we are inheriting parameters, but the warnings are related to the fact that there is a link back to `pull()` in the `@description` and `@seealso` sections of `vars_pull()` (i.e. in theory those aren't related to the parameter docs)

title: Use hyperlink in `warn_roxy_tag()` + `warn_roxy_block()`
HTML5 fixes
description:
From Kurt Hornik * the (new) warnings about " attribute "align" not allowed for HTML5" are typically from roxygen2 doing ``` ./R/object-defaults.R: fig <- "\\if{html}{\\figure{logo.png}{options: align='right' alt='logo' width='120'}}" ``` This can easily be fixed by changing align='right' to ``` style='text-align: right;' ``` * another group of problems is from putting R code in examples into a div. One test case is `keras/man/timeseries_dataset_from_array.Rd` which has ``` Consider an array \code{data} of scalar values, of shape \code{(steps)}. To generate a dataset that uses the past 10 timesteps to predict the next timestep, you would use:\if{html}{\out{
}}\preformatted{steps <- 100 ``` which does not work "as intended", as `\preformatted` will add a `

` to close the preceding paragraph but *after* the inserted `
`. Afaict, we don't have a way to force closing a paragraph other than adding an empty line, so changing the generated Rd to ``` Consider an array \code{data} of scalar values, of shape \code{(steps)}. To generate a dataset that uses the past 10 timesteps to predict the next timestep, you would use:\if{html}{ \out{
}}\preformatted{steps <- 100 ``` will "work" (and also not add an extra line in the LaTeX version): could you please change roxygen2 accordingly? * Finally, most warnings are from generating methods lists for R6 classes. E.g., for webmockr/man/Adapter.Rd we get inherited methods entries like ```html

  • webmockr::Adapter$disable()

    • ``` where the span starts outside the p but is closed inside the p. I don't see a "simple" fix for this, but the code in rd-r6.R is ``` c("\\if{html}{", paste0("\\out{", details, "}"), "\\itemize{", sprintf( paste0( "\\item \\out{}", "\\href{../../%s/html/%s.html#method-%s}{\\code{%s::%s$%s()}}", "\\out{}" ), super_meth$package, super_meth$classname, super_meth$name, super_meth$package, super_meth$classname, super_meth$name, super_meth$package, super_meth$classname, super_meth$name ), "}", "\\out{}", "}" ) } ``` so perhaps instead of calling `\href` (which will start the p inside the span) you could simply `\out` the a hyperlink directly?

title: remove duplicated authors in aliases
description:
Whenever you use a single page for multiple functions (using `@rdname`), the authors automatically stack.

However, especially with aliases, it seems quite unlikely that there are different authors using the same documentation page.

Shouldn't duplicates be removed from this field?

I'm not sure how multi-author statements can be managed though (last example).

Here is a reproducible example:

```r

title: use knit_print methods for inline R
description:
Update: On further inspection, the below is a feature request, not a bug report, I think. Reworded accordingly. --- It would be great if inline dynamic R code would respect the `knitr::knit_print()` method, which in turn [can have special behavior for `inline=TRUE`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/knitr/vignettes/knit_print.html). I don't think it currently does. Here's a reprex: ```r #' Reprex #' @inheritParams knitr::knit_print #' @param inline logical flag, whether print method is used from inside inline or a chunk. #' @export #' @section Let's test the print method: #' #' Setting things up: #' ```{r} #' library(knitr) #' x <- structure("I'm the default printing method.", class = "foo") #' ``` #' #' Here's the chunk output: #' #' ```{r} #' x #' ``` #' #' And inline with manual invocation: `r knitr::knit_print(x, inline = TRUE)`. #' #' And inline without manual invocation: `r x`. knit_print.foo <- function(x, inline = FALSE, ...) { out <- ifelse(inline, "I'm inline R output", "I'm an R chunk output") knitr::asis_output(out) } ``` And the resulting `knit_print.foo.Rd`: ``` % Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand % Please edit documentation in R/reprex.R \name{knit_print.foo} \alias{knit_print.foo} \title{Reprex} \usage{ \method{knit_print}{foo}(x, inline = FALSE, ...) } \arguments{ \item{x}{An R object to be printed} \item{inline}{logical flag, whether print method is used from inside inline or a chunk.} \item{...}{Additional arguments passed to the S3 method. Currently ignored, except two optional arguments \code{options} and \code{inline}; see the references below.} } \description{ Reprex } \section{Let's test the print method}{ Setting things up:\if{html}{\out{

}}\preformatted{x }\if{html}{\out{
}} I'm an R chunk output And inline with manual invocation: I'm inline R output. title: Use cli for feedback to user
Using @export on a S3 method registers it and does not export it
description:
Adding `#'@export` to a function such as `predict.myclass()` adds `S3method(predict, myclass)` to the NAMESPACE file of the package **{foo}**. However it does not add `export(predict.myclass)`.

The result is that `foo::predict.myclass` does not exist (only  `foo:::predict.myclass`).

That can create problem.

For example, if a package **{bar}** makes no call to `foo::fn` but only to the generic `stats::predict()`, then the dispatch won't work.
This is because the **foo** namespace will not be present in the search path (even if package is listed in Imports).

We can go around this problem by e.g. using `requireNamespace("foo")` inside **bar**, but this is not elegant.

Also it is sometimes nice to refer, in internal code at least, directly to the function used so as not to obfuscate where functions come from.
(Another good reason for this is that CMD won't fault if **foo** is not declared in Imports if `stats::predict()` is used).

Perhaps you had a good reason not to create `export(predict.myclass)` on top of `S3method(predict, myclass)`, but I think that `#'@export` suggests to the package developer that the function will be exported while in fact what happens now is that the function is *registered* but not *exported*.

If that does not cause problems I don't anticipate, I would thus recommend that  `#'@export` should generate the export statement in the NAMESPACE file (in addition to the registration).

title: @exportS3Method fails when package not imported or already in global namespace
description:
With the move to R 4.0.0, I've come across an issue with one of my packages where I wanted to include S3 methods without introducing a dependency on the package that defines the generic. I'd previously done this by `@export`ing the function without an `@importFrom`, which meant that an `export` rather than `S3method` directive was written to NAMESPACE. However, now that R 4.0.0 doesn't look in the global namespace for S3 methods, this no longer worked.

As per duckmayr's answer to my [StackOverflow question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61482561/whats-the-preferred-means-for-defining-an-s3-method-in-an-r-package-without-int), the answer comes from using `@exportS3Method package::generic_function` without an `@importFrom`. However, this fails unless the relevant package has already been loaded into the global namespace before a call to `roxygen2::roxygenise`. Within RStudio, this means that the Document option in the Build pane fails. Is there any chance of modifying the check that leads to the error `@exportS3Method` and `@exportS3Method generic` must be used with an S3 method' and therefore fails to include the relevant lines in NAMESPACE?

title: Allow Manual Avoidance of Usage Section
description:
A popular documentation design used in the Bioconductor community for S4 classes is:

- Title
- Description
- Details
- Constructor
- Summary (i.e. the `show` method)
- Accessors

I notice that the core packages all use manually-written Rd files (e.g. [GRanges-class.Rd](https://github.com/Bioconductor/GenomicRanges/blob/master/man/GRanges-class.Rd)) to achieve this and I am trying to recreate the style using Roxygen2. But, whenever I use `@export` or `@exportMethod`, this automatically creates a Usage section, which I would like to be able to avoid, since I'm trying to copy the structure of having Constructor, Summary, Accessor sections and I want the constructor function to be in Constructor (and I don't want the S4 generic to appear in Usage, either. It could have less parameters than any defined S4 method for it).

title: bug: `@inheritDotParams` doesn't handle escaped characters well
description:
I'm writing a package which uses the `glue` package. One of the functions effectively wraps `glue::glue_data`, so it has an ellipsis for all the `glue_data` arguments which should be documented with `@inheritDotParams glue::glue_data`.

As a reprex, I simply compiled a package with this function:
```r
# foo.R

#' foo
#'
#' @inheritDotParams glue::glue_data
#' @export
f <- function(...) {
  print(1)
}
```

At a glance this seems to work well, with roxygen2 compiling the .Rd files without a hitch. However, when I build and check the package, I get an odd warning about an unexpected `\item`.

I've realized the problem is in `glue_data`'s `.open` and `.close` arguments.

These are defined as:

```r
# glue.R

#' @param .open \[`character(1)`: \sQuote{\\\{}]\cr The opening delimiter. Doubling the
#'   full delimiter escapes it.
#' @param .close \[`character(1)`: \sQuote{\\\}}]\cr The closing delimiter. Doubling the
#'   full delimiter escapes it.
```

which gets compiled as:

```latex
% glue.Rd

\item{.open}{[\code{character(1)}: \sQuote{\\\{}]\cr The opening delimiter. Doubling the
full delimiter escapes it.}

\item{.close}{[\code{character(1)}: \sQuote{\\\}}]\cr The closing delimiter. Doubling the
full delimiter escapes it.}
```

In both files, we get `\sQuote{\\\{}`, that's three backslashes (two to render a backslash and one to escape the bracket), so that the rendered output is `'\{'`.

However, when I run roxygen2 on `foo.R`, the generated .Rd file has the following definitions of `.open` and `.close`:

```latex
% foo.Rd

    \item{\code{.open}}{[\code{character(1)}: \sQuote{\\{}]\cr The opening delimiter. Doubling the
full delimiter escapes it.}
    \item{\code{.close}}{[\code{character(1)}: \sQuote{\\}}]\cr The closing delimiter. Doubling the
full delimiter escapes it.}
```

They both have `\sQuote{\\{}`, with only two backslashes! So we get a rendered backslash but then the bracket is interpreted as code, which messes the parser up and throws a warning when building and checking the package.

description:
Say we have this block in package A: ```r #' Internal #' #' @section Example section: #' #' ```{r} #' letters #' ``` #' #' @name internal NULL ``` And the same block in package B: ```r #' External #' #' @section Example section: #' #' ```{r} #' letters #' ``` #' #' @name external NULL ``` Then in package A we inherit the section from both the internal and external topics: ```r #' Foo #' @inheritSection internal Example section #' @name foo NULL #' Bar #' @inheritSection issueInheritSectionExporter::external Example section #' @name bar NULL ``` foo.Rd is generated as: ```Rd \section{Example section}{ \if{html}{\out{
}}\preformatted{letters }\if{html}{\out{
}}\preformatted{## [1] "a" "b" "c" "d" "e" "f" "g" "h" "i" "j" "k" "l" "m" "n" "o" "p" "q" "r" "s" ## [20] "t" "u" "v" "w" "x" "y" "z" } ``` But in bar.Rd the curly brackets of the `\if` arguments are rewrapped: ```Rd \section{Example section}{ \if{{html}{\out{

If one has a DOI like <doi:10.1175/1520-0469(1981)038<1179:TSLROA>2.0.CO;2> in the package DESCRIPTION one needs to URLencode it for R CMD check to pass. I.e. "doi:10.1175/1520-0469(1981)038%3C1179:TSLROA%3E2.0.CO;2"

title: Usage section does not contain a linebreak as expected when a default argument is a function itself with a long return value
Bad wrapping of argument names
description:
This seems to be related to #21, but wasn't fixed when that bug was fixed. An argument with long names can have those names split with "\n" in the \usage block, and generate a "Mismatches in argument default values" warning in R CMD check.

## R code
```
#' Compare images
#'
#' @param x,y,match,batch_size,match_defaults,info Description here
compare_images <- function(x, y, match = NULL, batch_size = 100L, 
                           match_defaults = c(`Match` = TRUE, 
                                              `Likely match` = TRUE, 
                                              `Possible match` = FALSE,
                                              `No match` = FALSE), 
                           info = NULL, ...) {
  NULL
}
```

## \usage section
```
\usage{
compare_images(
  x,
  y,
  match = NULL,
  batch_size = 100L,
  match_defaults = c(Match = TRUE, `Likely match` = TRUE, `Possible match` = FALSE, `No
    match` = FALSE),
  info = NULL,
  ...
)
}
```
(There is no explicit "\n" in the \usage block, but the line wraps after the "No" in `No match`.)

## R CMD check excerpt
```
Codoc mismatches from documentation object 'compare_images':
  compare_images
    Code: function(x, y, match = NULL, batch_size = 100L, match_defaults
                   = c(Match = TRUE, "Likely match" = TRUE, "Possible
                   match" = FALSE, "No match" = FALSE), info = NULL, ...)
    Docs: function(x, y, match = NULL, batch_size = 100L, match_defaults
                   = c(Match = TRUE, "Likely match" = TRUE, "Possible
                   match" = FALSE, "No\n match" = FALSE), info = NULL,
                   ...)
    Mismatches in argument default values:
      Name: 'match_defaults'
      Code: c(Match = TRUE, `Likely match` = TRUE, `Possible match` = FALSE, 
            `No match` = FALSE)
      Docs: c(Match = TRUE, `Likely match` = TRUE, `Possible match` = FALSE, 
            `No\n    match` = FALSE)
```
Now the newline shows up, and causes the warning.

title: Struggling with `{{` links
Allow `Roxygen: list()` to include a vector of tags that are exempted from markdown parsing
description: Package authors may define macros different from the 'official' tags listed here (https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/blob/master/R/markdown-escaping.R#L38) for which it may also be desirable to avoid markdown parsing. Case in point, the `mathjaxr` package (https://github.com/wviechtb/mathjaxr) provides an easy way for package authors to include equations in their documentation that are parsed via MathJax in the html help files. The package provides several macros such as `\mjeqn` and `\mjdeqn` for this purpose. Unfortunately, markdown parsing (e.g., when there is an underline/underscore for a subscript) can happen within these tags (see: https://github.com/wviechtb/mathjaxr/issues/7). A possible solution would be to allow the specification of additional tags via `Roxygen: list()` in `DESCRIPTION` that are also exempted from markdown parsing (in essence, these just need to be appended to `escaped_for_md`). Would there be interest in adding such an option to `roxygen2`?

title: Failures in a file included with `@includeRmd` will nuke the NAMESPACE
description:
If you include a file with `@includeRmd` that fails during `roxygenise()`, then your NAMESPACE will be (mostly) nuked, which often puts you in a state where you can't even `roxygenise()` again to fix it. You end up having to revert the changes made to the NAMESPACE manually, fix the Rmd (or whatever made it fail), and then redocument. (This has bitten the tidymodels team, and me in vctrs quite a few times)

I have a somewhat minimal example here, where this commit changed an Rmd to make it fail, I redocumented, and now the exported function `fn()` is no longer part of NAMESPACE
https://github.com/DavisVaughan/testfailingroxygen2/commit/ad6f49fd34073758c9d69fb88089673051f920e1

The way this occurs is:
- [`roclet_preprocess()`](https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/blob/6c1e42f061e9435a14bd3a0e01c7f08fc7aa9160/R/roxygenize.R#L73) has a namespace method that inserts partial information into the NAMESPACE file. It seems to insert information about imports only.
- [`roclet_process()`](https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/blob/6c1e42f061e9435a14bd3a0e01c7f08fc7aa9160/R/roxygenize.R#L80) will then run, and the Rd method for that is where the Rmd is rendered and subsequently fails.
- [`roclet_output()`](https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/blob/6c1e42f061e9435a14bd3a0e01c7f08fc7aa9160/R/roxygenize.R#L88) never gets to run, which is where the NAMESPACE is finalized, so we end up with the broken partial NAMESPACE that `roclet_preprocess()` wrote.

I see two potential solutions:
- `roxy_tag_rd.roxy_tag_includeRmd()` could `tryCatch()` the `rmarkdown::render()` call? Or maybe pass something to `render()` to make it not fail.
- More generally, I'm not entirely sure why `roclet_preprocess.roclet_namespace()` exists. It seems like the process and output methods for roclet_namespace will basically do the same thing, just with `import_only = FALSE`. If the preprocess method wasn't run, it seems like we wouldn't get into that problematic state from above because we would never write a partial NAMESPACE to disk. I'm probably missing something though https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/blob/6c1e42f061e9435a14bd3a0e01c7f08fc7aa9160/R/namespace.R#L34-L63.

title: Add tags  to automatically add links to S4-methods,S4-generics,S4-superclasses and S4-subclasses
description:
Given an S4-generic function, it is possible to find the methods a package provides for it. 
Similarly, subclasses and superclasses of an S4 class can be found automatically by introspection. 
It is even possible to find out if a given class appears in a given s4-method implemented by the package.

Imagine the following  hypothetical tags:
- @s4methods 
  - in the documentation of a generic function it would trigger the creation of
    - a page for every S4-method of this generic provided in the package.
    - a section in the documentation of the generic with links to all the methods.
  - In the documentation of an S4-class it would trigger links to methods that have an argument of this class in their signature

- @s4generics
 - in the documentation of an S4-method it would trigger the creation of a link to the documentation of the generic. 
 - In the documentation of an S4-class it would trigger the creation of a section of links to generics that provide methods with the  
   class in their signature. 

- @s4subclasses
  In the documentation of an S4-class, this would create a section of links to all subclasses.

- @s4superclasses 
  In the documentation of an S4-class, this would create a section of links to all superclasses.
  
I have implemented all these tags and found them very useful to make this information automatically visible in the documentation.
While developing, automatically collecting and linking methods and subclasses makes it much easier to get/keep an overview of what methods are already available. I found myself using the creation of this linked documentation almost like a compile step and progress report.

Hadley closed the pull request https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/pull/1146 because it adds too much code at once and suggested starting with an issue to allow a discussion about the proposed changes. 
I hope for this discussion not least because I used this functionality to document a rather big package and in the long run do not want to maintain a separate branch of roxygen just to update the documentation ...
So comments are very welcome and useful.

title: @inheritParams separates parameters originally documented on the same line
description:
Consider for example:

```r
#' Foo
#' @inheritParams bar
foo <- function(a, b) a

#' Bar
#' @param a,b Parameters documented together.
bar <- function(a, b) b
```

This generates a single line of documentation for `a, b` in `?bar`, but two separate lines for `a` and `b` in `?foo` with the documentation text duplicated. Should the inherited lines in `?foo` match the original in `?bar`?

Suggestion: Tag to include source code in documentation
description:
Working on analytical packages in a business-context, I make pretty heavy use of `roxygen2`/`pkgdown` to document the projects I work on. As such I find that sometimes it's handy to include the source-code for a function (including comments) in its own documentation, particularly as `pkgdown` will then autolink to other functions that get called in the function body. My suggestion is to include a tag that will do this automatically, e.g. `@source_code function_name`. I'd be happy to submit a PR if you'd be willing to include such a feature in the package, though I understand it may be somewhat out of scope.

NB, the utility function I currently use to do this works like this:
```
#' `r include_source_code(fun = "name_of_current_function", file = "name_of_current_file")`
```
Thanks for all the hard work on this fantastic package :)

title: Request: inheritParams with different names
description:
Hi devs,

In some specific cases, it makes sense to name a parameter differently in two functions although the parameter serves the same purpose.

In these cases, `@inheritParams` will not work and this may cause code duplication.

A `key=value` syntax would be a nice workaround for this limitation, would that be manageable?

```r
#' Foo
#' @param a This is the first argument
foo <- function(a) a + 10

#' Bar
#' @param b This is the second argument
#' @inheritParams foo bar_a=a
bar <- function(bar_a, b) {
    foo(a=bar_a) * 10
}
```

title: multiple lines latex equation
roxygenize deletes Rdfiles
description:
On my new setup, `roxygenize` works the first time, but then later deletes the Rd files.  
I tracked it down to roclet_output.roclet_rd <https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/blob/7b706c9f7f2e4227c98928a67c5dcb51d88ec15d/R/rd.R#L69>
which should be empty but isn't.  
`dir(man, full.names = TRUE`) returns "C:/path/pack/man/fun1.Rd",  "C:/R/pack/man/fun2.Rd" etc  
while `paths`, coming from `file.path(man, names(results))` is "C:\\\\path\\\\pack\\\\man/fun1.Rd" etc with double backslashes as path separators. (Bitten again. Why on earth did Windows choose this?!)

`man` comes from  `man <- normalizePath(file.path(base_path, "man"))` and the `base_path` input argument already had backslashes instead of normal slashes.

Basically, dir() should use double backslashes as path separator but uses forward and then roxygen fails.

title: XML error in interactive sessions
description:
Documenting works in non-interactive sessions but fails in interactive ones with:

```r
devtools::document()
#> ℹ Updating rlang documentation
#> ℹ Loading rlang
#> Error in `read_xml.raw()`:
#> ! PCDATA invalid Char value 27 [9]

rlang::last_trace()
#> <error/rlang_error>
#> Error in `read_xml.raw()`:
#> ! PCDATA invalid Char value 27 [9]
#> Backtrace:
#>      ▆
#>   1. └─devtools::document()
#>   2.   └─roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg$path, roclets) at devtools/R/document.R:32:2
#>   3.     └─roxygen2::parse_package(base_path, env = NULL)
#>   4.       └─base::lapply(files, tokenize_file)
#>   5.         └─roxygen2 FUN(X[[i]], ...)
#>   6.           └─purrr::pmap(...)
#>   7.             └─roxygen2 .f(...)
#>   8.               └─roxygen2:::parse_tags(tokens)
#>   9.                 ├─roxygen2::roxy_tag_parse(tokens[[i]])
#>  10.                 └─roxygen2:::roxy_tag_parse.roxy_tag_section(tokens[[i]])
#>  11.                   └─roxygen2::tag_markdown(x)
#>  12.                     └─roxygen2:::markdown_if_active(x$raw, x)
#>  13.                       └─roxygen2:::markdown(text, tag, sections)
#>  14.                         └─roxygen2:::markdown_pass2(escaped_text, tag = tag, sections = sections)
#>  15.                           └─roxygen2:::md_to_mdxml(esc_text_linkrefs)
#>  16.                             ├─xml2::read_xml(md)
#>  17.                             └─xml2:::read_xml.character(md)
#>  18.                               └─xml2:::read_xml.raw(...)
```

~It also fails in interactive sessions when I disable Rprofile.~
Edit: `document()` doesn't fail when I disable Rprofile, only the reprex below does which makes sense since it has ANSI codes.

Here is a reprex:

```r
x <- "Splicing a list of arguments:

Take a function like [base::rbind()] that takes data in `...`. This
sort of functions takes a variable number of arguments.

```r
df1 <- data.frame(x = 1)
df2 <- data.frame(x = 2)

rbind(df1, df2)
#>   x
#> 1 1
#> 2 2
```

Passing individual arguments is only possible for a fixed amount of
arguments. When the arguments are in a list whose length is
variable (and potentially very large), we need a programmatic
approach like the splicing syntax `!!!`:

```r
dfs <- list(df1, df2)

inject(rbind(!!!dfs))
#>   x
#> 1 1
#> 2 2
```

Because `rbind()` is a base function we used [inject()] to
explicitly enable `!!!`. However, many functions implement [dynamic
dots][list2] with `!!!` implicitly enabled out of the box.


```r
tidyr::expand_grid(x = 1:2, y = c("a", "b"))
#> \033[38;5;246m# A tibble: 4 × 2\033[39m
#>       x y    
#>   \033[3m\033[38;5;246m<int>\033[39m\033[23m \033[3m\033[38;5;246m<chr>\033[39m\033[23m
#> \033[38;5;250m1\033[39m     1 a    
#> \033[38;5;250m2\033[39m     1 b    
#> \033[38;5;250m3\033[39m     2 a    
#> \033[38;5;250m4\033[39m     2 b

xs <- list(x = 1:2, y = c("a", "b"))
tidyr::expand_grid(!!!xs)
#> \033[38;5;246m# A tibble: 4 × 2\033[39m
#>       x y    
#>   \033[3m\033[38;5;246m<int>\033[39m\033[23m \033[3m\033[38;5;246m<chr>\033[39m\033[23m
#> \033[38;5;250m1\033[39m     1 a    
#> \033[38;5;250m2\033[39m     1 b    
#> \033[38;5;250m3\033[39m     2 a    
#> \033[38;5;250m4\033[39m     2 b
```

Note how the expanded grid has the right column names. That's
because we spliced a _named_ list. Splicing causes each name of the
list to become an argument name.

```r
tidyr::expand_grid(!!!set_names(xs, toupper))
#> \033[38;5;246m# A tibble: 4 × 2\033[39m
#>       X Y    
#>   \033[3m\033[38;5;246m<int>\033[39m\033[23m \033[3m\033[38;5;246m<chr>\033[39m\033[23m
#> \033[38;5;250m1\033[39m     1 a    
#> \033[38;5;250m2\033[39m     1 b    
#> \033[38;5;250m3\033[39m     2 a    
#> \033[38;5;250m4\033[39m     2 b
```



[base::rbind()]: R:base::rbind()
[inject()]: R:inject()
[list2]: R:list2
"
md <- commonmark::markdown_xml(x, hardbreaks = TRUE, extensions = "table")
xml2::read_xml(md)
```

Not sure if roxygen generates invalid input or if there is bug in commonmark or xml2.

description:

I am working for a time now on the documentation of a large package I wrote. I am struggling with a certain issue:

The generic is documented as follows:

```
I searched a lot on stackoverflow, but did not find an answer to this question I have. What is my error here? 

Any help is welcome.

title: Automatic delayed S3 method registrations for R 3.6.0?
description:
I just got the following email from Kurt Hornik (regarding my dendextend package):

> Dear maintainer,
> 
> Apparently your package has S3 methods it does not register via
> NAMESPACE and instead exports, so that these methods can only be found
> on the search path.  The CRAN run time tests find at least
> 
>     S3 method lookup found 'as.phylo.dendrogram' on search path 
> 
> there may be more.
> 
> Presumably, you did not register the methods as this requires the
> generic to be imported, and hence the namespace of the generic and all
> its dependencies to be loaded, which maintainers often prefer to avoid
> for S3 methods which are really only needed when the namespace of their
> generic is loaded.
> 
> For the current development version of R, we have recently added a
> simple mechanism for delayed S3 registration: using 
> 
>    if(getRversion() >= "3.6.0") {
>        S3method(pkg::gen, cls)
>    }
> 
> will register 'gen.cls' as S3 method for class 'cls' and generic 'gen'
> from package 'pkg' only when the namespace of 'pkg' is loaded.
> (Similarly, one can use
> 
>    if(getRversion() >= "3.6.0") {
>        S3method(pkg::gen, cls, fun)
>    }
> 
> in case the method is named 'fun' and not 'gen.cls'.)
> 
> Can you please add the necessary delayed S3 method registrations to your
> NAMESPACE, and submit a new version of your package as quickly as 
> possible?
> 


I wrote to him that I use @export to get the S3 method registered (see here: https://github.com/talgalili/dendextend/blob/c0885f64686a1a7ff86eb06dde8b12e1233549cd/R/ape.R#L24 ), and that I cannot manually edit NAMESPACE since it is managed automatically via roxygen2.

What should be a solution for this?

One option is that roxygen2 will move to using 
```
 if(getRversion() >= "3.6.0") {
      S3method(pkg::gen, cls)
 }

```

Another is to allow some areas of the NAMESPACE to have manual parts, and the rest will be auto-generated (is this already possible now?!).
Any other thoughts?

Thanks.

title: rd_roclet does not respect exports in hand-written NAMESPACE
description:
When `NAMESPACE` is generated by hand, `rd_roclet` (and hence`roxygen2::roxygenise`, `devtools::document` etc.) generate documentation for functions that are not exported.

To reproduce, `mkdir rot ; cd rot ; R`:

```
> packageVersion("roxygen2")
[1] ‘7.1.1’
> usethis::create_package(".")
```

Add `R/foo.R` with the contents:

```R
#' This is an internal function and shouldn't be exported or documented.
.Foo <- function() {}

#' This function should be exported.
#' @export
Bar <- function() {}
```

From R:

```
devtools::document()
ℹ Updating rot documentation
ℹ Loading rot
Writing NAMESPACE
Writing NAMESPACE
Writing Bar.Rd
```

This is working as expected so far.  However, now lets provide a custom NAMESPACE:

```
# Generated by hand.  Stay away, roxygen2.
export(Bar)
```

Clear out old things: `rm -rf man`, then

```
> roxygen2::roxygenise()
First time using roxygen2. Upgrading automatically...
ℹ Loading rot
Warning: The existing 'NAMESPACE' file was not generated by roxygen2, and will not be overwritten.
Writing dot-Foo.Rd
Writing Bar.Rd
```

roxygen2 should not generate `dot-Foo.Rd`, because `.Foo` was not explicitly exported.

title: inheritDotParams includes duplicate param definitions if param already documented
S3 method false negative?
description:
If I provide an S3 method for the primitive function `cos()` like this:
```r
#' @export
cos.my_class <- function(x) x
```
roxygen2 correctly adds it as an S3 method to NAMESPACE as:
> ```
> S3method(cos,my_class)
> ```

However when doing the same thing for another primitive function `cospi()`:
```r
#' @export
cospi.my_class <- function(x) x
```
roxygen2 doesn't detect that it should be exported as an S3 method, and exports it as another function:
> ```
> export(cospi.my_class)
> ```

It does the same thing as `cospi()` for the following functions: `sinpi()`, `tanpi()`, `log10()`, and `log2()`. These are all primitives, so I can't see any reason they would behave differently than `cos()` and other primitives. I could well be missing something though - my knowledge of S3 dispatch and primitives is decidedly sketchy.

Manually editing NAMESPACE to add `S3method(cospi,my_class)` works, but is a pain - is there another way to force this to export as an S3 method in the current version of roxygen2? 

---

P.S. There's an example of this issue in the wild [here](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/blob/fd38cf89d00354b29fbb516f40cc24dbdc51859f/R/functions.R) and I have a minimal demo package I can push and link to if that would be useful.

title: Cannot create documentation for PackageC which depends on PackageB which calls a method from PackageA onLoad
description:
Please excuse the weird title. I am having troubles building documentation with roxygen2 when my package depends on another package that depends... consider the following example.

## PackageA
- Has a function `helloA()` which prints `"Hello, world, this is package A!"`
- Does `print("Hello, its package A")` in it's `.onLoad()`

## PackageB
- Depends on `PackageA`
- Does `print("Hello, its package B")` in it's `.onLoad()`
- Calls `helloA()` in it's `.onLoad()`

Creating documentation using roxygen2 for this package yields

```
==> devtools::document(roclets = c('rd', 'collate', 'namespace'))

i Updating PackageB documentation
i Loading PackageB
[1] "Hello, its package A"
[1] "Hello, its package B"
[1] "Hello, world, this is package A!"
Documentation completed
```

## PackageC
- Depends on `PackageB`
- Does `print("Hello, its package C")` in it's `.onLoad()`

Creating documentation using roxygen2 for this package fails:

```
==> devtools::document(roclets = c('rd', 'collate', 'namespace'))

i Updating PackageC documentation
[1] "Hello, its package B"
i Loading PackageC
Error: Dependency package(s) 'PackageB' not available.
Backtrace:
    x
 1. +-base::suppressPackageStartupMessages(...)
 2. | \-base::withCallingHandlers(expr, packageStartupMessage = function(c) tryInvokeRestart("muffleMessage"))
 3. \-devtools::document(roclets = c("rd", "collate", "namespace"))
 4.   \-roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg$path, roclets)
 5.     \-roxygen2:::load_code(base_path)
 6.       \-pkgload::load_all(path, helpers = FALSE, attach_testthat = FALSE)
 7.         \-pkgload:::load_depends(path)
 8.           \-pkgload:::abort_for_missing_packages(res, depends$package)
Warning message:
In (function (dep_name, dep_ver = "*")  :
  Dependency package 'PackageB' not available.
Execution halted

Exited with status 1.
```

So it first attaches packageB without attaching packageA, therefore, calling `helloA()` in `.onLoad()` of packageB fails. If I remove `helloA()` from the `.onLoad()` of packageB, the output is:

```
==> devtools::document(roclets = c('rd', 'collate', 'namespace'))

i Updating PackageC documentation
i Loading PackageC
[1] "Hello, its package B"
[1] "Hello, its package A"
[1] "Hello, its package C"
Documentation completed
```

We clearly see that packageA is loaded **after** packageB.
- Adding packageA to the Depends of PackageC does not help
```
Depends:
    PackageA,
    PackageB
```

At the same time, building documentation without roxygen works:

```
> devtools::document()
i Updating PackageC documentation
i Loading PackageC
[1] "Hello, its package C"
```

title: repeated test runs in same session may raise warnings
description:
As of https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/commit/b3053b694399416543af877837efb29e6ec34d1f, repeated tests with some failing tests in the same session may raise these warnings:

```
1: In .Internal(gc(verbose, reset, full)) :
  closing unused connection 7 (/var/folders/1f/9tm8hrm179b6qsv8mw9lbv580000gn/T//RtmpWHa5Ey/file92741d50bb5e)
2: In .Internal(gc(verbose, reset, full)) :
  closing unused connection 6 (/var/folders/1f/9tm8hrm179b6qsv8mw9lbv580000gn/T//RtmpWHa5Ey/file9274512de9cd)
3: In .Internal(gc(verbose, reset, full)) :
  closing unused connection 5 (/var/folders/1f/9tm8hrm179b6qsv8mw9lbv580000gn/T//RtmpWHa5Ey/file92746b389a99)
4: In .Internal(gc(verbose, reset, full)) :
  closing unused connection 4 (/var/folders/1f/9tm8hrm179b6qsv8mw9lbv580000gn/T//RtmpWHa5Ey/file92743e1b3129)
```

The exact number of closed unused connections varies somewhat.

To reproduce:

1. Introduce a failing test somewhere:
    ```r
     test_that("trigger unused connections warning",  testthat::fail())
    ```
2. Run the test at least twice:
    ```r
    devtools::test()
    devtools::test()
    ```

This isn't really a big problem, though it can get contributors off on the wrong path if their tests break during development.
(I thought I might must have somehow mishandled connections in https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/pull/1182).

Based on the paths, my guess would be that these warnings are caused by connections to `tempfile()`  in tests, which somehow may not be properly closed in time.

Maybe something like this:

https://github.com/r-lib/testthat/blob/f1dd05cbae2432c1ad8a3db53849ce01819f4172/tests/testthat/test-expect-known.R#L13-L20

description: When running document() one can get an error about missing dependency when that dependency is not missing. If "X" is the package that is reported to be missing then the output of requireNamespace("X") is generally more useful in diagnosing this than the message that comes from devtools which can be incorrect and it would be good if that message were output.

title: Unicode Remapping Causes Function-Documentation Mismatch
description:
This is related to #592.

I am trying to write a Unicode to ASCII simplifier which will map specific characters before doing a general mapping using `stringi`.  One of the characters that often shows up in my work is the Greek character lowercase mu.  There are two Unicode code points that typically have the same glyph but one is considered "Greek mu" and one is "micro sign".  These are `c("\u03bc", "\u00b5")`.

As I have learned more and more, operating system and locale are often important for this, and so this is on Windows 10 with the English/United States locale (full session info is in the reprex).

When I generated the documentation for these with `devtools::document()`, both of these were mapped to "\u00b5".  So, I got an error in Travis-CI:

```
* checking for code/documentation mismatches ... WARNING
Codoc mismatches from documentation object 'unicode_to_ascii':
unicode_to_ascii.character
  Code: function(x, verbose = FALSE, pattern = c("Î¼", "Âµ"), replacement
                 = c("u", "u"), general_conversion = TRUE, ...)
  Docs: function(x, verbose = FALSE, pattern = c("Âµ", "Âµ"), replacement
                 = c("u", "u"), general_conversion = TRUE, ...)
  Mismatches in argument default values:
    Name: 'pattern' Code: c("Î¼", "Âµ") Docs: c("Âµ", "Âµ")
```

Is there any way to prevent this Unicode remapping?

In the reprex below, the last 4 lines are the problem.  They should look like:

any(grepl(x=doc, pattern="\u03bc"))

  )
