title: error building PDF manual of roxygenized package
description:
In Hadley's R packages book in the chapter on checking he writes
​
> Occassionally you’ll get an error when building the PDF manual. This is usually because the pdf is built by latex and you’ve forgotten to escape something. Debugging this is painful - your best bet is to look up the latex logs and combined tex file and work back from there to .Rd files then back to a roxygen comment. I consider any such failure to be a bug in roxygen2, so please let me know.

I sent Hadley this example by email and he asked me to post my issue here. I’ve figured out the error in the .Rd syntax but maybe you think roxygen2 should handle it smarter. I’m attaching the minimal example source package as a [tarball](https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/files/2146945/examplePackage.tar.gz).

I roxygenized it with `devtools::document(".")` (maybe that’s not the recommended way?). (System and version info below).

Here is the (bad) roxygen block:

```
##' A boring function                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
##'                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
##' This function bores me but the documentation is exciting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
##'                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
##' \code{                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
##'   myfunction(x)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
##'                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
##'   # comment line code block following an empty line                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
##' }                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
##' @param x an argument                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
##' @return x again                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
##' @export                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
myfunction <- function(x) {
  x
}
```
(The problem is using `\code` instead of `\preformatted`, and the error also seems to require a comment line following an empty line.)

This results in the following .Rd file:

```
% Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
% Please edit documentation in R/myfunction.R                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
\name{myfunction}
\alias{myfunction}
\title{A boring function}
\usage{
myfunction(x)
}
\arguments{
\item{x}{an argument}
}
\value{
x again
}
\description{
This function bores me but the documentation is exciting.
}
\details{
\code{
  myfunction(x)

# comment line code block following an empty line
}
}
```

and then an error when making the PDF manual:

```
friedmab@rescomp1094:~/scr/packages % R CMD Rd2pdf examplePackage --no-clean
Hmm ... looks like a package
Converting Rd files to LaTeX
Creating pdf output from LaTeX ...
Error in texi2dvi(file = file, pdf = TRUE, clean = clean, quiet = quiet,  :
  Running 'texi2dvi' on 'Rd2.tex' failed.
LaTeX errors:
! Paragraph ended before \Rd@code was complete.
<to be read again>
                   \par
l.48

! Emergency stop.
<to be read again>
                   \par
l.48

!  ==> Fatal error occurred, no output PDF file produced!

...
```

Changing the `\code` directive to `\preformatted` fixes the problem.

title: Unclear warning of missing @description value
description:
When using the following R code as the whole content of a single hello.R file residing in the R folder of a default package structure (e.g. the test package from Rstudio) a warning "Warning: @description [hello.R#1]: requires a value" is generated, when running roxygen using `devtools::document(roclets=c('rd', 'collate', 'namespace')). ` 

```
#'
#' @name testClass
#' @title testClass
#'
#' @slot one character.
#' @slot two numeric.
#'
#' @export
setClass("testClass",
                      slots = c("one" = "character",
                                "two" = "numeric"),
                      prototype = c("one" = "fump",
                                    "two" = 6))
```

It is fixed by removing the first line of roxygen comment. The following code does not produce the warning:

```
#' @name testClass
#' @title testClass
#'
#' @slot one character.
#' @slot two numeric.
#'
#' @export
setClass("testClass",
                      slots = c("one" = "character",
                                "two" = "numeric"),
                      prototype = c("one" = "fump",
                                    "two" = 6))
```

It seems to me, that the warning is at least misleading. It maybe a bug, since the difference between the two coding blocks is not existant.

title: If a project defines a collation, but does not contain any include directives generation fails.
description:
This might be by design, however in https://github.com/r-lib/fs I originally had a include directive, then later removed it. This caused my `DESCRIPTION` to have a `Collate:` section, however roxygen could no longer manage it because there were no include directives.

Ideally it would do one of the following in this case.

1. Emit a warning about lack of include directives.
2. Update the collation with the default sorting for the locale.
3. Delete the collation section entirely.

2 and 3 could be problematic for packages that use a manually modified collation I guess, so likely 1 is the only one we could use.

title: Cryptic error when leaving @inheritDotParams unspecified.
description:
By mistake I left in a `@inheritDotParams` line, with no function specified from which to inherit. I did not notice for some time, since `devtools::load_all(".")` was working fine.

However, when building or checking the package it suddenly stopped early with the following error:

```
Updating phylopath documentation
Loading phylopath
Error: is.function(fun) is not TRUE
Execution halted

Exited with status 1.
```

It was not clear to me what was wrong. I traced the error as follows:

- I figured out that `devtools::document()` also wasn't working.
- `roxygen2::roxygenise` was failing.
- I used the debugger to step through:  `roxygenise`, `roc_out`, `roclet_process` and `topics_process_inherit` to find that `topics$apply(inherit_dot_params, env = env)` was failing.

Would it be possible to report the topic for which the error occured, or at least that some inheritance failed? That would make this much easier to pin down.

Thanks all for a massive time saver.

title: Add plain "-method" alias to documentation for S4 methods
description:
Use case: https://github.com/r-dbi/DBI/issues/162

Then, the package that defines a generic can use a `methodName-method` link to point users to all available implementations. Unfortunately, `R CMD check` then warns for the package that defines the generic that the link `methodName-method` points to nowhere. This can be alleviated by a reexports-like "landing page" for all such links.

Example:

- *DBI* defines a `dbConnect()` generic
    - In the documentation for that method, *roxygen2* creates a section "Implementations" that contains a link to `dbConnect-method`
    - A file `methods.Rd` is created, aliased to `dbConnect-method` (to satisfy `R CMD check`); a bullet point mentioning `dbConnect()` is created there, perhaps with relevant links. This file also contains a message like "if you see this page, you may need to load more packages"
- *RSQLite* implements a `dbConnect()` method
    - The help page for that method is aliased to `dbConnect-method`
    - In the documentation, *roxygen2* creates a section "Generic" that contains a link to `dbConnect`

title: New roxygen behavior around author
description:
I just noticed that the new release of roxygen2 introduces a new behavior for the handling of author fields. Specifically, it now draws author information from the DESCRIPTION and puts it into Rd files. This is, however, the wrong use of the `\author{}` field.

According to [Writing R Extensions](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Rd-format), this field refers to the author of the specific documentation file not the package:

> \author{…}
Information about the author(s) of the Rd file. Use \email{} without extra delimiters (such as ‘( )’ or ‘< >’) to specify email addresses, or \url{} or \href{}{} for web pointers.

As such this is incorrect behavior. Can you please revert? Thanks!

title: assignment of an object of class “call” is not valid for @‘.Data’ in an object of class “MethodDefinition”; is(value, "function") is not TRUE
description:
Hi all,

I have been stumbling into the same issue for a while now, when documenting packages that include S4 methods named like primitives of the `base` package. I have a kind of workaround (described further below), but I would like to learn if and what is the proper way of dealing with this kind of situation.

The issue is that Roxygen crashes with the following message. As a result, the `NAMESPACE` file is left with only `import*` directives, but none of the `export*` directives.

```
==> devtools::document(roclets=c('rd', 'collate', 'namespace'))

Updating unisets documentation
Writing NAMESPACE
Loading unisets
Error in (function (cl, name, valueClass)  : 
  assignment of an object of class “call” is not valid for @‘.Data’ in an object of class “MethodDefinition”; is(value, "function") is not TRUE
Calls: suppressPackageStartupMessages ... block_find_object -> object_from_call -> parser -> <Anonymous>
In addition: Warning message:
In asNamespace(ns, base.OK = FALSE) :
  operation not allowed on base namespace
Execution halted

Exited with status 1.
```

This crash happens when I document functions like `subset` or `c` like this:

```
#' @rdname BaseSets-methods
#' @aliases subset.BaseSets subset,BaseSets-method
#'
#' @param ... Additional arguments passed to and from other methods.
#'
#' @section Subsetting:
#'
#' `subset(object, subset, ..., drop=TRUE)` returns subsets of relations which meet conditions.
#' The `subset` argument should be a logical expression referring to any of `"element"`, `"set"`, and any available relation metadata indicating elements or rows to keep: missing values are taken as false.
#' The `drop` logical scalar controls whether elements and sets orphaned during the subsetting should be removed from the `elementData` and `setData` slots, respectively.

#'
#' @importFrom methods as
#' @importFrom BiocGenerics eval unique
#' @importFrom S4Vectors from to subset
#' @method subset BaseSets
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#'
#' bs1 <- subset(bs, set == "set1" | element == "E")
#' bs1
setMethod("subset", "BaseSets", function(x, ...) {
    .local <- function(x, subset, select, drop=TRUE, ...) {
        # Match code layout of the FuzzySets method
        table <- as.data.frame(x)
        i <- eval(substitute(subset), table)
        out <- x[i, drop=drop]
        # For derived subclasses, coerce back to the original
        as(out, class(x))
    }
    .local(x, ...)
})
```

I've tried the following too:

```
> roxygen2::roxygenize()
Loading unisets
Error in (function (cl, name, valueClass)  : 
  assignment of an object of class “call” is not valid for @‘.Data’ in an object of class “MethodDefinition”; is(value, "function") is not TRUE
In addition: Warning message:
In asNamespace(ns, base.OK = FALSE) :
  operation not allowed on base namespace
```

My current workaround is to define both an S3 an S4 functions, and to document the S3 only, like this:

```
#' @rdname BaseSets-methods
#' @aliases subset.BaseSets subset,BaseSets-method
#'
#' @param ... Additional arguments passed to and from other methods.
#'
#' @section Subsetting:
#'
#' `subset(object, subset, ..., drop=TRUE)` returns subsets of relations which meet conditions.
#' The `subset` argument should be a logical expression referring to any of `"element"`, `"set"`, and any available relation metadata indicating elements or rows to keep: missing values are taken as false.
#' The `drop` logical scalar controls whether elements and sets orphaned during the subsetting should be removed from the `elementData` and `setData` slots, respectively.

#'
#' @importFrom methods as
#' @importFrom BiocGenerics eval unique
#' @importFrom S4Vectors from to subset
#' @method subset BaseSets
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#'
#' bs1 <- subset(bs, set == "set1" | element == "E")
#' bs1
subset.BaseSets <- function(x, ...) subset(x, ...)

setMethod("subset", "BaseSets", function(x, ...) {
    .local <- function(x, subset, select, drop=TRUE, ...) {
        # Match code layout of the FuzzySets method
        table <- as.data.frame(x)
        i <- eval(substitute(subset), table)
        out <- x[i, drop=drop]
        # For derived subclasses, coerce back to the original
        as(out, class(x))
    }
    .local(x, ...)
})
```

Can anyone spot what I'm doing wrong?
The package source code is hosted here: https://github.com/kevinrue/unisets if anyone is willing to open a PR showing me the fix.

Thank you in advance!

title: devtools::document() Error in .f(.x[[i]], ...) : attempt to apply non-function
description:
I recently updated from `roxygen2` version 6.0.1 to 6.1.0. I went to document some newly added functions and received the following error message:  
```
> devtools::document()
Updating package documentation
Loading package
Error in .f(.x[[i]], ...) : attempt to apply non-function
```

title: New `@testthat` tag
description:
I really enjoy having documentation of a function at its definition. For a while I have wished for something similar for tests (not for all tests, but for some). What do you think of the idea of introducing a new `@testthat` that can generate [testthat](https://github.com/r-lib/testthat) tests automatically? E.g. for the `str_length` at this repo's `README`:

```
@testthat expect_equal(str_length(letters), nchar(letters))
@testthat expect_equal(nchar("roxygen"), 7)
```

I'm not sure if there should be multiple `@testthat`'s or just a single; this was just to illustrate the idea.

What do you think of something like that?

If `roxygen2` was extendable, i.e. a package could provide a new roclet, then I think that would make a neat little add-on package. But as far as I understand the `roxygen2` process, then that's not the case and additions like the one suggested above need to be implemented in `roxygen2` directly. Is that correct?

title: Consider making package load optional
description:
I usually call `roxygenize(roclets="rd")` (via [this script](https://github.com/eddelbuettel/littler/blob/master/inst/examples/roxy.r), usually) which worked fine for many years.  It uses `roxygenize` to translate markup from the `R/` directory into content in the `man/` directory.   This never touches `NAMESPACE` or `DESCRIPTION`.

Now, all of a sudden, the function decides to invoke `pkgload`, forcing a load/build I did not ask for, and seemingly running it with different flags (as I get compiler warnings I do not get otherwise).

I would like to suppress this package loading test.  Would you consider a PR to that effect?  Maybe skipping if `roclets` is equal to `"rd"` so that we do not need a new flag?

(And I checked that this did not happen with version 6.0.1.  The code in `R/roxygenize.R` appears to not have changed so this may be a side effect of other changes.)

title: Expose a file argument to roxygen2::roxygenize()
description:
Exposing an API for selected files only would be handy for two reasons:

* parallelization. Have not found any issue on that. Is this a priority?
* Ability to only run it on files that were changed, e.g. as part of a pre-commit hook. That would probably result in a significant speed up. Also, frameworks such as pre-commit.com have built-in parallelization over files, so currently in https://github.com/lorenzwalhtert/pre-commit-hooks, to roxygenize hook is run as many times as there are changed files (because it does not make use of the passed information about files).

Would you consider exporting such a function from the package? Or add a `files`  argument to `roxygen2::roxygenize()`?

title: Provide a way to concisely document the API of a package
description:
so that changes can be tracked and compared between releases.

According to https://principles.tidyverse.org/function-interface.html, the API consists of:

- (Function) name
- Inputs
- Output value
- Errors
- Side effects

The [API roclet](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgapi/blob/2464d224630c6bc1b7e68b5448096a0baebbe8ec/R/roclet.R) in {pkgapi} documents the first two items in a new `API` file. This format (one line per function) won't be sufficient if we consider output, errors and side effects, but it seems clear that {roxygen} is a good tool to create this.

Related to {vctrs} which provides ways to specify/check the type of an object.

We should strive for consistency with the [RDocTaskForce](https://github.com/RDocTaskForce) R Consortium project.

title: Uninformative error when leaving an empty @param
description:

Leaving an empty   `#' @param` in a roxygen comment leads to an error with no information at all to identify the problem:
`Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : index out of bound`

I believe it could be useful to specify in which comment the error occurs in such situations.

description:

    library(roxygen2)
    out <- roc_proc_text(rd_roclet(), "
      #' with escaped quotation mark
      #' @examples
      #' '34.00\''
      h <- function() {}
    ")
      ```

* If roxygen2 fails with an uninformative message, what's a strategy for winnowing your package down to reveal the problem.

title: allow customization of '@family' prefix
description:
When using e.g.

    #' @family foo

The documentation gets an entry in the seealso section as:

    Other foo: <...>

I'd like to be able to customize the prefix, so that I could just write e.g.

    #' @family Environment management

and just have a plain old:

    Environment management: <...>

ie, without the `Other:` prefix. Does that seem sensible?

tl;dr: "Other:" isn't always a great prefix and I'd like to customize that somehow.

title: Unbalanced backticks in Rd for a [link text][pkg::object]-style link
description:
This backtick behaviour: 

```
methods::`structure-class`
```

is inspired by how I would get help, e.g. by `` ?methods::`structure-class` ``

But the trailing backtick goes missing in the Rd docs.

I note that I got unstuck by *not* using backticks around `structure-class`. But it feels like these backticks should be tolerated / not mangled, since everything else in your experience suggests they are necessary or at least a good idea.

``` r
library(roxygen2)

roc_proc_text(
  rd_roclet(), "
    #' Title
    #'
    #' Description, see [`matrix`][methods::`structure-class`].
    #' @md
    foo <- function() {}"
)[[1]]
#> % Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
#> % Please edit documentation in RtmpiHM2q1/file13dc854fab817
#> \name{foo}
#> \alias{foo}
#> \title{Title}
#> \usage{
#> foo()
#> }
#> \description{
#> Description, see \code{\link[methods:`structure-class]
#> {matrix}}.
#> }
```

<sup>Created on 2018-10-23 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1)</sup>

This Rd leads to the [following WARNING on travis](https://travis-ci.org/tidyverse/tibble/jobs/444840369#L1271-L1275) but not for me locally (macOS) and I have no idea why.

```
❯ checking Rd cross-references ... WARNING
  Missing link or links in documentation object 'as_tibble.Rd':
    ‘[methods:`matrix-class]{matrix}’
  
  See section 'Cross-references' in the 'Writing R Extensions' manual.
```

title: Url containing %
description:

title: How to write tags and where to look for existing (non standard) ones?
description:
As a concrete project, I would like to extend the functionality of the documentation for R4 classes and methods a little bit, if only to document my own code.
 
Use cases are for example:
- a list of constructors for a  certain class automatically linked to the class
- automatic links to methods that are documented separately  both from the class and the generic
...
From a first glance at the roxygen2 code I assume that writing my own 'tags' would be a fairly nonintrusive way to achieve this. 
If this is indeed the case it seems reasonable that other people had similar ideas and wrote their own tags. But I could not find any. 
**Are there any resources about how to find or make one's own tags apart from the source code of the implemented tags?** 

Thanks for your time and the huge amount of work already done

title: exposing a command line interface using roxygen
description:
This is related to #858. The idea would be that using adding 
"@exposeas bar" to the roxygen comment lines would create a command line tool (in this case bar) that fulfills  the API specification of the documented function.  The wrapping tool could be called from a shell. This would be enable R functionality to be chained with other tools in a language agnostic way (I am thinking IO specification along the lines of [boutiques](https://boutiques.github.io), Common Workflow Language, or nipype interfaces).

Does this seem feasible? My impression is that currently, to create a command line tool one must right wrapping code that parses command arguments (using the likes of commandArgs,docopt, or argparse among others). This in effect forces one to specify the same interface in two different places. Using roxygen seems like a more elegant approach. 

Please correct me if I'm wrong as I currently need to create some command line tools for a project, and roxygen seems like the clear winner to me for documenting functionality in  a way that nicely integrates with the devtools/rstudio workflow

title: `rd.Rmd` vignette references wrong vignette for Markdown documentation
description: While reading the documentation, I noticed that Line 108 of the [rd.Rmd vignette](https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/blob/master/vignettes/rd.Rmd) refers to the [formatting vignette](https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/blob/master/vignettes/formatting.Rmd) for discussion of Markdown formatting. However, the formatting vignette does not mention Markdown. Perhaps Line 108 should simply be updated to refer to the [Markdown vignette](https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/blob/master/vignettes/markdown.Rmd) instead?

title: Support for optional text between arguments/parameters
description:
According to [Writing R Extensions](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Documenting-functions) section on Rd files, it is possible to include text between function arguments (parameters), for example to separate groups of related arguments:
> There may be optional text outside the \item entries, for example to give general information about groups of parameters.

Is there a way to support this in `roxygen2`? I understand it may be complicated, as this doesn't represent a name-description "tag"... If not, are there any other suggestions to achieve visual 'grouping' of parameters?

title: Warning: bad markup (extra space?) - automatic cut of line when @inheritParams
description:
I have a package in which there is this [argument description](
https://github.com/easystats/bayestestR/blob/de682e173484b2b11db3acbd3c2269f2144231dc/R/describe_posterior.R#L8):

`#' @param rope_range \href{https://easystats.github.io/bayestestR/rope}{ROPE's} lower and higher bounds. Should be a list of two values (e.g., \code{c(-0.1, 0.1)}) or \code{"default"}. If \code{"default"}, the bounds are set to \code{x +- 0.1*SD(response)}.`

The package documentation builds without problems. 

However, in another package, I [inherit this parameter from the first package](https://github.com/easystats/parameters/blob/df9bf9557f6d9ca47f437bfaf2b4c24573046b22/R/model_parameters.bayesian.R#L69). Then, upon compilation of this second package, I got the error:

`Warning: bad markup (extra space?)`

And when I look at the created documentation, it seems like roxygen cut the first part of the line, leaving only:

`c(-0.1, 0.1)) or "default". If "default", the bounds are set to x +- 0.1*SD(response).`

How can I address that? Thank you!

I have `roxygen2_6.1.1`.

title: NAMESPACE overwritten when externally authored
description:

The offending code seems to be in namespace.R, line 36.

title: Creating PDF version Warning: Replacing ... does not exist, replaced by a fixed one.
rdname fails if first character is a dot .
description:
`@rdname` does indeed require the Rd name, but roxygen replaces the initial `.` with the string `dot-` when generating (internal) documentation. I think it should accept either the original object name or documentation object `@name` or the `dot-` replaced version.
```
d <- "/tmp/rdnamedot"
dir.create(file.path(d, "R"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
cat(file = file.path(d, "R", "script.R"), "
#' Symbol internal to package
.j <- 1

#' @rdname .j
.k <- 1

#' @rdname dot-j
.k2 <- 1
")
cat(file = file.path(d, "DESCRIPTION"), 
    'Package: rdnamedot
Version: 0.1
Description: show rdname requires the file name, not the object from which it was derived
Authors@R: person(given = "Jack O. Wasey", role = "cre", email = "em@ail.com")
Encoding: UTF-8
')
roxygen2::roxygenize(d, roclets = "rd")
list.files(file.path(d, "man"))
cat(paste(readLines(file.path(d, "man", "dot-j.Rd")), collapse = "\n"))
```

title: Inheriting Roxygen2 documentation for multiple arguments doesn't work as expected
description:
This is kind of relevant to this [question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39762443/inherit-roxygen2-documentation-for-multiple-arguments-in-r-package), but not really.

If I have the same documentation, for multiple arguments, `roxygen2` takes care of this
```r
#' @rdname foo1
#' @param color,colour Color name to print.

foo1 <- function(color = NULL, colour) {
  color <- color %||% colour
  print(color)
}
```
and the `.Rd` file looks like the following-
```
\item{color, colour}{Color name to print.}
```
But inherit this documentation in another function, **this works** 
```r
#' @rdname foo2
#' @inheritParams foo1

foo2 <- function(color = NULL, colour) {
  foo1(color = color, colour = colour)
}
```
but produces duplication in the `.Rd` file-
```r
\item{color}{Color name to print.}
\item{colour}{Color name to print.}
```
Any way to avoid such duplication?

title: Wish: document infix-function with optional extra arguments, without usage-tags
description:
In a comment on [SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/8873514/documenting-setter-functions-with-roxygen), from 2012, I read "you should never need to use @usage - any time you do it is a bug in roxygen2 and you should file a bug report", so that's why I'm posting now, even though I think my problem is an edge-case.
And furthermore, I'm not sure if what I would ideally want is even possible, or that it violates documentation requirements. Anyway, my situation:

I've written an infix-function, with an optional extra argument:
````
`%mod%` <- function(x,y, tolerance = sqrt(.Machine$double.eps))
````
(This function calculates modulo, but with some tolerance for rounding error, so 9.1 %mod% .1 == 0 instead of (very nearly) .1, as 9.1 %% .1 gives).
I expect any users to rarely use the parameter "tolerance", which is why I made it an infix.
But it is there, and R cmd-check expects all arguments to be in the docs.
Ideally, I'd like my usage sections to read something like this:
````
x %mod% y
`%mod%`(x, y, tolerance = sqrt(.Machine$double.eps))
````

However, if I don't specify a @usage section, roxygen2 only documents `x %mod% y`
And devtools::check() then complains (rightfully so) that my argument "tolerance" is undocumented.
I've found the only way to get rid of this warning is using @usage, with the full parameter list.

So I have 2 questions:
1. Could roxygen2 handle this automatically, without @usage?
2. Is there any way to document the 2 different calling forms? With multiple lines of @usage, my docs look good to me, but then devtools::check() also complains. (although it's not really an roxygen2 issue, but maybe you could help me)

title: Allow to control order of useDynLib lines in NAMESPACE file
description:
When generating the NAMESPACE file, the useDynLib lines (created with @useDynLib)  are ordered lexically by the name of the shared object.
However, the order of  loading the shared objects matters if there are dependencies between the shared objects, such as when functions from external libraries need to be called.
There should be a way to control the order of these lines. Probably just not sorting them and recommend to place all the @useDynLib calls in the right order in one location.
( [See also:](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/53171756/)

title: Adding methods to another package's R6 class: how to document?
description:
R6 has a nifty feature where you can add new members to an existing class via `set()`. You can even do this to a class exported by a different package, which is very useful indeed.

For example, in package A:
```r
#' @export
myclass <- R6::R6Class("myclass",
    public=list(
        f=function(x) { ... }
))
```
And in package B:
```r
# modifying objects exported by another package must be done at runtime
.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname)
{
    A::myclass$set("public", "g", overwrite=TRUE,
        function(y) { ... }
}
```
Now you can do something like
```r
library(A)
library(B)
obj <- A::myclass$new(...)
obj$g(y=42)  # method defined by package B
```
How should we document the new method added by B?

title: Improve wrapping for usage sections
description:
When functions have many arguments, the default wrapping of their \usage section is hard to read. For example, `readr::read_delim` looks like:
```
read_delim(file, delim, quote = "\"", escape_backslash = FALSE,
  escape_double = TRUE, col_names = TRUE, col_types = NULL,
  locale = default_locale(), na = c("", "NA"), quoted_na = TRUE,
  comment = "", trim_ws = FALSE, skip = 0, n_max = Inf,
  guess_max = min(1000, n_max), progress = show_progress())
```

This saves vertical space, but makes it hard to spot argument names and to distinguish them from default values. It would sometimes be nicer to have one argument per row. For example, `lattice::xyplot` does

```
xyplot(x,
       data,
       allow.multiple = is.null(groups) || outer,
       outer = !is.null(groups),
       auto.key = FALSE,
       aspect = "fill",
       panel = lattice.getOption("panel.xyplot"),
       prepanel = NULL,
       scales = list(),
       strip = TRUE,
       groups = NULL,
       xlab,
       xlim,
       ylab,
       ylim,
       drop.unused.levels = lattice.getOption("drop.unused.levels"),
       ...,
       lattice.options = NULL,
       default.scales,
       default.prepanel = lattice.getOption("prepanel.default.xyplot"),
       subscripts = !is.null(groups),
       subset = TRUE)
```

The most flexible solution would be to have the usage laid out just as it is in the original code. At the moment, roxygen reformats usage sections.

title: roxygen2 6.1.0 discards latin1 packages
description:
The decision to soft-enforce `Encoding: UTF-8` has been made some time ago (#649) and has recently become effective with the release of **roxygen2** 6.1.0. I understand that supporting just one package encoding makes **roxygen2** much simpler to maintain. However, I would like to document three drawbacks of this change:

1. [Writing R extensions](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#The-DESCRIPTION-file) discourages the use of an Encoding field in the DESCRIPTION when it is actually not needed (#774)

> Do not specify an encoding unless one is actually needed: doing so makes the package *less* portable. If a package has a specified encoding, you should run `R CMD build` etc in a locale using that encoding.

2. Who knows how long UTF-8 will actually remain the dominant encoding? Maybe some of its (future) derivatives will take over? Having a **roxygen2** implementation which works with either encoding seems to be desirable in the long run.

3. **roxygen2** cannot be used by "latin1" packages anymore.

To quantify the importance of the last point, I have checked how many "latin1" packages on CRAN have actually used **roxygen2**:

```r
db <- tools::CRAN_package_db()
table(db$Encoding, exclude = NULL)
## latin1 latin2  UTF-8   <NA>
##    198      1   3116   9723

latin1pkgs <- subset(db, Encoding == "latin1")$Package

## how many of these "latin1" packages have used roxygen2?
## (pulling DESCRIPTION files from the github/cran mirror)
descdir <- file.path(tempdir(), "desc"); dir.create(descdir)
for (pkg in latin1pkgs) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(descdir, pkg)))
        next
    url <- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cran/", pkg, "/master/DESCRIPTION")
    ## or from CRAN:
    ## url <- paste0("https://CRAN.R-project.org/web/packages/", pkg, "/DESCRIPTION")
    try(download.file(url = url, destfile = file.path(descdir, pkg)))
}
setwd(descdir)
roxy <- sapply(list.files(descdir), read.dcf, fields = "RoxygenNote")
table(roxy, exclude = NULL)
## 5.0.1 6.0.1  <NA>
##     5    21   171
affected_pkgs <- names(which(!is.na(roxy)))
affected_maintainers <- unique(subset(db, Package %in% affected_pkgs)$Maintainer)
```

This results in **26 packages** of 22 different maintainers, who will either have to re-encode their package or stick to the previous version of **roxygen2** (for now). The affected packages are listed below. I have also mentioned the maintainers (if I could find a corresponding GitHub username) to make them aware of this regression in **roxygen2**:

[Barycenter](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=Barycenter), [bibliometrix](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=bibliometrix) (@massimoaria), [binomSamSize](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=binomSamSize) (@hoehleatsu), [DFIT](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=DFIT) (@herulor), [ecd](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ecd), [ExpDes](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ExpDes) (@EricBarba), [ExpDes.pt](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ExpDes.pt) (@EricBarba), [FKF](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=FKF) (@waternumbers), [GFA](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=GFA), [GFE](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=GFE), [ggseqlogo](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ggseqlogo) (@omarwagih), [INLABMA](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=INLABMA), [InterfaceqPCR](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=InterfaceqPCR), [ldhmm](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ldhmm), [lifecontingencies](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=lifecontingencies) (@spedygiorgio), [MatrixCorrelation](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=MatrixCorrelation) (@khliland), [microclass](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=microclass) (@larssnip), [mixlm](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=mixlm) (@khliland), [PGRdup](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=PGRdup) (@aravind-j), [plsgenomics](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=plsgenomics), [RcmdrPlugin.NMBU](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=RcmdrPlugin.NMBU) (@khliland), [REPPlab](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=REPPlab) (@fischuu), [surveillance](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=surveillance) (@bastistician), [TeachingSampling](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=TeachingSampling) (@psirusteam), [VTrack](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=VTrack) (@RossDwyer), [Xplortext](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=Xplortext)

Are there any plans for **roxygen2** to support non-UTF-8 packages again in the future? Is this even possible while still avoiding issue #592 on Windows?

title: Exporting `default_tags()` function

title: Roxygen thinks a function of mine is an S3 method, and so breaks upon installation of my package
description:
I'm using roxygen to create my own package. I have a function that's causing a problem:

```
##' extract.sig.metadata
##' @param foo bar
##' @author me
##' @export
extract.sig.metadata <- function(foo){
# does stuff
}
```

I've created my package skeleton (with create(my-package) from devtools), and I've used document() to process the roxygen tags. However, when I try to install my package, it fails:

...
**\* installing help indices
*\* building package indices
*\* testing if installed package can be loaded
Error : object 'extract' not found whilst loading namespace 'my-package'
Error: loading failed
Execution halted

I'm pretty sure that roxygen thinks that extract.sig.metadata is an S3 method, i.e. a specialized form of export(), but it's not finding the function export(), and so it's breaking. But this isn't an s3 method, it's just a function called extract.sig.metadata. If I look in the Rd code, the /usage tag looks weird:

```
\usage{
\method{extract}{sig.metadata}(spec.df, var = "product_name",
  ratio.cutoff = 0.001, prob.modifer = 3, frequency.cutoff = NA,
  verbose = F, assign.to.global.env = FALSE, use.bigrams = T, clean = T,
  ngram.dupe.n.cutoff = 0.1, max.obs = 10000)
}
```

If I do change the name to extractSigMetadata, the problem is technically fixed, and the .Rd code changes,

```
\usage{
 extractSigMetadata(foo)
}
```

But I would really like to not have to change the name of my function (there are tens of functions that have the same problem in my package, and they are used in a bunch of scripts - it would be a huge pain to change my naming schema not). 

---> Does anyone know how I can tell roxygen that this is just a normal function and not weird s3 method? I'm guessing it has something to do with the @method tag, but I don't know how to use it properly enough to make this work. Thanks!!!

title: Feature Proposal: Type Checking
description:
This proposal is to allow users to add type checking in their docs with a `@contract` tag.

I recently came across the python package [contract](https://github.com/AndreaCensi/contracts). From the description:

> PyContracts is a Python package that allows users to declare constraints on function parameters and return values. It supports a basic type system, variables binding, arithmetic constraints, and has several specialized contracts (notably for Numpy arrays).

So type hinting but actually doing things, pretty dang cool!

I was staring at the below example for a bit and thinking, "Gosh it would be very rad to have this in R"

```python
@contract
def my_function(a, b):
    """ Function description.
        :type a: int,>0
        :type b: list[N],N>0
        :rtype: list[N]
    """
    ...
```

Suddenly `TrianglesAndMathInMyFaceMeme.jpg` why can't we do that in roxygen???

```R
#' Function description.
#' @contract
#' @param a [int, min > 0] A very important number.
#' @param b [list, length > 0] A very important list.
#' @return [vector, type = numeric] A very important vector.
my_function = function(a, b){
...
}
```

I think the easiest way to do this would be to add a function to the users function. Though this sounds kind of invasive it would look something like

```R
#' Function description.
#' @contract
#' @param a [int, min > 0] A very important number.
#' @param b [list, length > 0] A very important list
#' @return [vector, type = numeric] A very important vector
my_function = function(a, b){
# adds type checking
contract_my_function()
}
```

The `contract_my_function()` would look into it's parents frame getting all function inputs. It could use something like [checkmate](https://github.com/mllg/checkmate) to then build the assertion rules to pass or fail functions.

idk if it would be better in roxygen or as it's own package, but either way would like like to know how the roxygen team feels about something like the above. It feels like a good idea, though adding stuff to peoples code seems a bit aggressive.

Thanks for reading!

title: Documenting R6 objects
description:
I asked this question on Stack Overflow about how to document R6 objects, but no answers yet after a week:  https://stackoverflow.com/questions/53750453/roxygen-r6-methods .  Wondering if someone here might have a suggestion.

(I know R6 documentation is an oft-desired topic, as shown in the uncompleted issues #388, #306, etc. - basically I'm trying to "punt" and not need Roxygen to know anything about R6; I'm just trying to use some existing Roxygen features like `@inheritParams` etc. and have `R CMD check` not yell at me.)

Question repeated here:

------------------------------

I'm trying to generate some reasonable documentation for R6 classes.  Here's an example:


    ##' GroveR class object
    ##' @importFrom R6 R6Class
    ##' @export
    GroveR <- R6Class(
      portable = FALSE,
      private = list(
        fileRoot = ".",
        artDefs = list(),
        memCache = list()
      )
    )

    .public  <- function(...) GroveR$set("public",  ...)

    #' Do a thing
    #'
    #' @name myMethod
    #' @usage
    #' myMethod(name, deps, create, retrieve, checkTime,
    #'          store, clobber=FALSE)
    #'
    #' @param name name of the artifact
    #' @param deps names of other artifacts this artifact depends on
    #' @param create function to create this artifact object from its dependency objects
    #' @param retrieve function to retrieve this artifact from cache
    #' @param checkTime function to fetch the time of last update for this artifact
    #' @param store function to store this artifact to cache
    #' @param clobber whether to allow redefinition of this artifact if it is already defined
    .public("myMethod", function(name, deps, create, retrieve, checkTime, store, clobber=FALSE) {
      # ...body...
    }

    #' Do a similar thing
    #'
    #' @name myOtherMethod
    #' myOtherMethod(name, deps, create, path, readFun=readRDS,
    #'               writeFun=saveRDS, ...)
    #'
    #' @inheritParams myMethod  // TODO Doesn't work yet
    #' @param path path to cached file
    #' @param readFun function to read file from disk
    #' @param writeFun function to write file to disk
    #' @param ... further arguments passed to \link{myMethod}
    .public("myOtherMethod", function(name, deps, create, path, readFun=readRDS, writeFun=saveRDS, ...) {
      # ...body...
    }

`.public()` is a helper function I've written for defining R6 methods.

There are several things not working here:

* The `@inheritParams` directive is not working, the `name` and `deps` and `create` argument for `myOtherMethod()` are not being inherited.  This generates `R CMD check` warnings like `Undocumented arguments in documentation object 'myOtherMethod'
  ‘name’ ‘deps’ ‘create’`
* I'm adding the `@usage` directive manually, because Roxygen can't figure out (quite reasonably) how to parse my method definitions.  Is there a better way to do this?
* In `R CMD check`, I get warnings about `Functions or methods with usage in documentation object 'myMethod' but not in code:
  myMethod `

Is there a more fruitful direction for me to go?  Should I try documenting a `NULL` object instead of my `.public` calls?  What would that look like?

title: warning: missing name/title. Skipping
description:
Often I want to create a copy of a function because I know that users might be confused about the exact spelling of the function (think `dplyr::summarise` and `dplyr::summarize`). In that case, I do something like the following-
```r

#' @name foo1
#' @title foo1
#' @export
foo1 <- function(x) {
   print(x)
}

#' @rdname foo2
#' @export

foo2 <- foo1
```

But this gives the following warning for `devtools::document()`-
```
Warning: foo2.Rd is missing name/title. Skipping
```

Is it possible in this case for `foo2` to inherit `foo1`'s `name` and `title` without me having to copy-paste the same thing, which will be more prone to error?

description:

```
==> devtools::document(roclets=c('rd', 'collate', 'namespace'))

Updating roxygen2 documentation
Loading roxygen2
Error in markdown_rparse(markdown_tags[[xml_name(xml)]](xml), markdown_tags = markdown_tags) : 
  attempt to apply non-function
Calls: suppressPackageStartupMessages ... markdown_rparse -> paste -> vapply -> FUN -> markdown_rparse

title: Issues with math latex formatting
description:
In the documentation for Roxygen2 it says that math equations can be made using standard Latex inside of \eqn{} or \deqn{}. This is no issue for simple equations, but I've been unable to use standard latex to make more specific math formatting in my documentation, like for example just trying to format an integral. For example, the simple latex integral from 0 to 4 in a roxygen comment:
 \deqn{$$\int_{0}^{4} x^2 dx$$}
doesn't provide an integral symbol, rather it just outputs the code inside of the brackets. 

The same is true if only one dollar sign is used, and if no dollar signs are used inside of the \deqn{} brackets. I have been unable to find a solution to this and was wondering if there was a way to use specific latex math formatting to present more attractive documentation of formulas.

title: Collate Section of DESCRIPTION Incorrectly Parsed in roxygen 6.1
description:
Documentation build no longer works with (some?) packages with a collate section in description (update: it seems to be packages that list one file per line in the collate field with indenting).  Here is an example against the current master of ggplot2, although I've seen the same thing with one of my packages:

```
> devtools::document()
Updating ggplot2 documentation
Loading ggplot2
Error in parse(text = lines, keep.source = TRUE, srcfile = srcfilecopy(file,  : 
  /Volumes/PERSONAL/repos/ggplot2/R:1:12: unexpected numeric constant
1: .          0
               ^
> sessionInfo()
R version 3.5.1 (2018-07-02)
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin15.6.0 (64-bit)
Running under: macOS High Sierra 10.13.6

Matrix products: default
BLAS: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.5/Resources/lib/libRblas.0.dylib
LAPACK: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.5/Resources/lib/libRlapack.dylib

locale:
[1] en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/C/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] ggplot2_3.0.0.9000

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] Rcpp_0.12.18        compiler_3.5.1      pillar_1.3.0.9000  
 [4] plyr_1.8.4          bindr_0.1.1         tools_3.5.1        
 [7] testthat_2.0.0      digest_0.6.15       memoise_1.1.0      
[10] tibble_1.4.99.9003  nlme_3.1-137        gtable_0.2.0       
[13] lattice_0.20-35     viridisLite_0.3.0   mgcv_1.8-24        
[16] pkgconfig_2.0.2     rlang_0.2.2         Matrix_1.2-14      
[19] commonmark_1.5      bindrcpp_0.2.2      withr_2.1.2        
[22] stringr_1.3.1       dplyr_0.7.6         roxygen2_6.1.0.9000
[25] xml2_1.2.0          desc_1.2.0          devtools_1.13.6    
[28] rprojroot_1.3-2     grid_3.5.1          tidyselect_0.2.4   
[31] glue_1.3.0          R6_2.2.2            purrr_0.2.5        
[34] reshape2_1.4.3      magrittr_1.5        backports_1.1.2    
[37] scales_0.5.0        MASS_7.3-50         assertthat_0.2.0   
[40] colorspace_1.3-2    stringi_1.2.3       lazyeval_0.2.1     
[43] munsell_0.5.0       crayon_1.3.4       
```
 I believe this can be traced to the [change to use `desc::desc`](https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/blame/a8ed64bf13b6de454760b2c5e41c1b51558b0c80/R/utils.R#L152).

I have a PR coming shortly that should fix the issue.

Fundamentally, the problem is that the new method of pulling the description does not trim whitespace.  The old method used `read.dcf`:

```
> read.dcf('DESCRIPTION')
     Package Title                                         
[1,] "fansi" "ANSI Control Sequence Aware String Functions"
... SNIP ....
     Collate                                                                                                                                                                            
[1,] "'constants.R'\n'fansi-package.R'\n'has.R'\n'internal.R'\n'load.R'\n'misc.R'\n'nchar.R'\n'strip.R'\n'strwrap.R'\n'strtrim.R'\n'strsplit.R'\n'substr2.R'\n'tohtml.R'\n'unhandled.R'"
``` 
The new method keeps the whitespace padding:
```
> roxygen2:::read.description('DESCRIPTION')
$Package
[1] "fansi"

$Title
[1] "ANSI Control Sequence Aware String Functions"

... SNIP ...

$Collate
[1] "'constants.R'\n    'fansi-package.R'\n    'has.R'\n    'internal.R'\n    'load.R'\n    'misc.R'\n    'nchar.R'\n    'strip.R'\n    'strwrap.R'\n    'strtrim.R'\n    'strsplit.R'\n    'substr2.R'\n    'tohtml.R'\n    'unhandled.R'"

```
Which then leads to this file listing:

```
debugging in: package_files(path)
debug: {
    desc <- read_pkg_description(path)
    all <- normalizePath(r_files(path))
    collate <- scan(text = desc$Collate %||% "", what = "", sep = " ", 
        quiet = TRUE, strip.white = TRUE)
    collate <- normalizePath(file.path(path, "R", collate))
    rfiles <- c(collate, setdiff(all, collate))
    ignore_files(rfiles, path)
}
Browse[2]> 
debug: desc <- read_pkg_description(path)
Browse[2]> 
debug: all <- normalizePath(r_files(path))
Browse[2]> 
debug: collate <- scan(text = desc$Collate %||% "", what = "", sep = " ", 
    quiet = TRUE, strip.white = TRUE)
Browse[2]> 
debug: collate <- normalizePath(file.path(path, "R", collate))
Browse[2]> collate
 [1] "constants.R"     ""                ""                ""               
 [5] ""                "fansi-package.R" ""                ""               
 [9] ""                ""                "has.R"           ""               
[13] ""                ""                ""                "internal.R"     
[17] ""                ""                ""                ""               
[21] "load.R"          ""                ""                ""               
[25] ""                "misc.R"          ""                ""               
[29] ""                ""                "nchar.R"         ""               
[33] ""                ""                ""                "strip.R"        
[37] ""                ""                ""                ""               
[41] "strwrap.R"       ""                ""                ""               
[45] ""                "strtrim.R"       ""                ""               
[49] ""                ""                "strsplit.R"      ""               
[53] ""                ""                ""                "substr2.R"      
[57] ""                ""                ""                ""               
[61] "tohtml.R"        ""                ""                ""               
[65] ""                "unhandled.R" 
```

which then causes the error when R tries to read the R directory as a file.

This is likely the source of #785 as well.

The only thing that gives me pause in all this is that there are not more reports of this issue here given how long 6.1 has been out, so maybe I am doing something wrong.

It is possible this was not caught because the tests use a "collate" field where the file names are all on one line and no indents (i.e. `tests/description-example.txt`).

title: Percentage sign '%' is not escaped in ```...``` code block.

#' ```R

#' %
#' \%
#' ```
```

The generated `.Rd` will be:

```latex
\preformatted{
generate_eventlog() %>% create_pmap() %>% render_pmap_file("test.svg", format = "svg")
%
\\%
}
```

\
```
I think this bug is similar to https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/issues/640, maybe there are other places or characters are needed to be escaped.

title: Multiple records in Authors@R causes roxygen to crash when using "_PACKAGE"
description:
Simple reproducible case.  Remove either the `"My Giant Company [cph]"` line from `DESCRIPTION` or the `"_PACKAGE"` line from `R/pkgname.R` and things work.  With both in place, things fail.

DESCRIPTION
> Package: test
> Type: Package
> Title: What the Package Does (Title Case)
> Version: 0.1.0
> Authors@R: as.person(c(
>     "package maintainer <yourself@somewhere.net> [aut, cre]",
>     "My Giant Company [cph]"
>     ))
> Description: More about what it does (maybe more than one line)
>     Use four spaces when indenting paragraphs within the Description.
> License: What license is it under?
> Encoding: UTF-8
> LazyData: true
> RoxygenNote: 6.0.1

R/pkgname.R
> #' My Package
> #'
> #' Does some stuff
> #'
> "_PACKAGE"

devtools::document(roclets=c('rd', 'collate', 'namespace', 'vignette'))
> Updating test documentation
> Loading test
> Error in vapply(unclass(authors), author_desc, character(1)) : 
>   values must be length 1,
>  but FUN(X[[1]]) result is length 2
> Calls: suppressPackageStartupMessages ... object_defaults.package -> package_authors -> vapply
> Execution halted

Changing 
> Authors@R: as.person(c(
>     "package maintainer <yourself@somewhere.net> [aut, cre]",
>     "My Giant Company [cph]"
>     ))
to
> Authors@R: c(
>     as.person("package maintainer <yourself@somewhere.net> [aut, cre]"),
>     as.person("My Giant Company [cph]")
>     )
produces the same failure

The root cause is the way `as.person()` translates `"three word name"` into a person object.  Instead of splitting it into `given`, `middle` & `family`, it sets the `given` field to a character vector of length 2, e.g. c("three" "word").

As `person(given = c("My", "First"), "Name")` is also valid, I think roxygen needs to handle this situation more gracefully than it does today.

PS before you ask, yes I am including `<>` around the email addresses above.  The characters are just being eaten by the GitHub markdown engine

title: S3 methods for S4 classes not properly documented
description:
Per the [methods manual](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/methods/html/Methods_for_S3.html) , the following construct should be used when creating S3 methods for S4 classes. This is eg needed when having a model framework in S4, but one needs to provide predict(), fitted(), coef() , ... methods.

```
setClass("uncased", contains = "character")
unique.uncased <- function(x, incomparables = FALSE, ...) nextMethod(tolower(x))
setMethod("unique", "uncased", unique.uncased)
```
And the namespace should contain

```
S3method(unique, uncased)
exportMethods(unique)
```

When I try the following : 
```
#' @rdname unique
#' @export
unique.uncased <- function(x, incomparables = FALSE, ...) nextMethod(tolower(x))
#' @rdname unique
#' @export
setMethod("unique", "uncased", unique.uncased)
```
Then : 
- in the namespace `export(unique.uncased)` is added.
- R CMD check gives a note about a possible S3 method being refered to in the manual with its full name.

> S3 methods shown with full name in documentation object 'unique':
>   'unique.uncased'
> The \usage entries for S3 methods should use the \method markup and not their full name.

If I use the (deprecated) tag `@S3method` instead, I have the correct entry in the namespace but still the same note in R CMD check.

title: Error after `devtools::document` when `#'` comments inside function
description:
I would say this is linked to a bad practice but as I took me some time to find the reason, I thought this could be good to be reported.  
I received a R code that I wanted to transform as a package. I remarked that if there are some comments inside a function that are commented with `#'`, there are used as the roxygen skeleton. Hence, when using `devtools::document()` the following function returns a warning and is **not** exported. This because `@export` is followed by multiple lines.
```
Warning: @export [mean.R#11]: may only span a single line
```
Example function:
```
#' Mean of a vector

#' @param x vector
#'
#' @return return mean of a vector without NA
#' @import magrittr
#' @importFrom stats na.omit
#' @examples 
#' my_mean(c(4,5))
#' @export

my_mean <- function(x){
  #' Remove NA
  x <- x %>% na.omit()
  #' Calculate mean
  sum(x)/length(x)
}
```

To see it differently, we can finish the roxygen skeleton with `@examples`. Usually, if this is empty, `document` returns a warning: `Warning: @examples [mean.R#9]: requires a value`. However, in the following case, comments written using `#'` are used as the content of examples with no errors or warnings.

```
#' Mean of a vector

#' @param x vector
#'
#' @return return mean of a vector without NA
#' @import magrittr
#' @importFrom stats na.omit
#' @export
#' @examples 

my_mean <- function(x){
  #' Remove NA
  x <- x %>% na.omit()
  #' Calculate mean
  sum(x)/length(x)
}
```
Look at the documentation produced.
![my_mean](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21193866/39714777-699c30e4-522b-11e8-86be-6756dd5789ba.png)

I think we are not supposed to include such kind of comments inside the function, but does roxygen not supposed to stop reading when calling `function` ? (Maybe it would not work with S3 methods or documented data ?)

Error reported here once is maybe linked:
https://github.com/STAT545-UBC/Discussion/issues/241
and reported here
https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/community/posts/205901678-Too-many-newlines-in-roxygen-comments

title: Selectively exclude package-internal docblocks from output
description:
Is there a way to mark some Roxygen docblocks "package-internal", and exclude them from the generated output?

To explain what I mean, this is a feature that's present in some similar `@tag` code documentation systems for other languages. For example, [JSDoc](http://usejsdoc.org/) for Javascript when rendering will exclude all docblocks marked with the `@private` tag, by default. A parameter allows you to change this behavior, so that you can generate developer documentation that includes all the internal methods.

As a recent newcomer to R, I'd assumed Roxygen did something similar, so I had been documenting all my functions, exported or not, using `#'` Roxygen docblocks. But then I noticed in the [tidyjson](https://github.com/jeremystan/tidyjson/issues/105) project the devs have done the same thing, and the result is that the end-user package helpfiles are made confusing by the presence of help docs for many functions the end-user is not meant to access.

I think under the current functionality, a workaround for this could be to use `@rdname` to move "internal" docblocks into a file named `internal.Rd`, and add that to `.Rbuildignore`, but I was wondering if I've missed a more obvious way to achieve this.

Cheers!

title: Markdown link text line wrapping removes whitespace
description:
Using the Markdown tag (`@md`) on a Roxygen block works as expected for links in the `[link text](link.url)` markup, except where `[link text]` breaks across lines due to text wrapping. In this case, whitespace at the end or beginning of lines is stripped and words are concatenated. So for example the following Roxygen block:

```
#'  Personal R packages are not an original idea of mine; I think I first heard
#'  about them on [Hilary Parker's 
#'   blog](https://hilaryparker.com/2013/04/03/personal-r-packages/), though
```

Produces a link of the format [Hilary Parker'sblog](https://hilaryparker.com/2013/04/03/personal-r-packages/). Note that this example contains both trailing and leading whitespace and both are stripped.

The current workaround is not to wrap the `[link text]`, so that:

```
#'  Personal R packages are not an original idea of mine; I think I first heard
#'  about them on [Hilary Parker's blog](https://hilaryparker.com/2013/04/03/personal-r-packages/),
#'  though
```

Works as desired/expected.

title: Documenting S4 methods
description:
I'm only learning roxygen, and I'm contemplating migrating some of my packages to this style documentation, as I'd like to keep docs next to code.  However, I'm getting stuck deciding where to document S4 generics and methods.

The typical structure is as follows for a silly example package "junk" for illustration purposes:

```shell
$ tree junk
junk
|-- DESCRIPTION
`-- R
    |-- AllGenerics.R
    |-- AllMethod.R
    `-- plotFoo.R
$ cat junk/R/AllGenerics.R
##' Methods for plotting
##'
##' @name plotFoo-methods
if (!isGeneric("plotFoo")) {
    setGeneric("plotFoo",
               function(x, y, ...) standardGeneric("plotFoo"))
}
$ cat junk/R/AllMethod.R
setMethod("plotFoo", signature(x="numeric", y="numeric"),
          function(x, y, time.lim=seq(0, 1, by=0.1),
                   depth.lim=seq(10), ...) {
              .plotFoo(time=x, depth=y, time.lim=time.lim,
                       depth.lim=depth.lim, ...)
          })

setMethod("plotFoo", signature(x="numeric", y="missing"),
          function(x, y, depth.lim, ...) {
              .plotFoo(time=x, depth=rev(x), depth.lim=depth.lim, ...)
          })
$ cat junk/R/plotFoo.R
###_ + Internal Function

".plotFoo" <- function(time, depth, time.lim=NULL, depth.lim=NULL, ...)
{
    plot(depth ~ time, xlim=time.lim, ylim=depth.lim, ...)
}
```

Of course, the real AllGenerics.R and AllMethod.R contain many more generics and methods, and there are several other files like plotFoo.R with other functions.  As implied, I'd like to show all plotFoo methods in a plotFoo-methods.Rd file.  The challenge is that the methods only handle some arguments before passing the correct arguments onto an internal function, so it's unclear where and how one documents all arguments?  Any tips welcome.

title: CRAN incompatible Rd files generated by S4 methods for classes with non-syntactic names.
description:
I know the title of this issue is a bit of a word salad, but bear with me on this... For example:

```
#' @rdname is.one.sided
#' @aliases is.one.sided,<--method
setMethod( 'is.one.sided', '<-', .is.one.sided )
```

Generates Rd files that are (at present) rejected by CRAN.  This is unlikely to change in the near future.
Kurt Hornik writes regarding the formula.tools package:

> 
> Thanks.  I see that this got auto-rejected, base on
> 
> * checking for code/documentation mismatches ... WARNING
> Functions or methods with usage in documentation object 'formula.parts' but not in code:
>   \S4method{lhs}{<-} \S4method{op}{<-} \S4method{rhs}{<-}
> 
> so I took a closer look.
> 
> The code for processing Rd S3/S4 method markup assumes that the names of
> the classes involved are syntactic names.  In your case, <- is not, and
> using
> 
>   \S4method{is.one.sided}{<-}
> 
> would not parse, which I guess is why you use
> 
>   \S4method{is.one.sided}{`<-`}
> 
> in your Rd file.  But this is not recognized as S4 method markup and
> hence not processed accordingly, hence the mismatch.
> 
> One could try to extend the markup processing to handle not syntactic
> names quoted by backticks, but we've had no need for this in many years,
> so I'd rather avoid the effort if possible.  Now, R-exts says
> 
>   If it is necessary or desired to provide an explicit function
>   declaration (in a '\usage' section) for an S4 method (e.g., if it has
>   "surprising arguments" to be mentioned explicitly), one can use the
>   special markup
> 
>      \S4method{GENERIC}{SIGNATURE_LIST}(ARGUMENT_LIST)
> 
> Afaics, your methods have not surprising arguments, so perhaps you could
> simply not provide \S4method entries and instead say in text which
> classes you provide the methods for?
> 
> Best

The solution is to omit usage entries for non-syntactic names.

title: Default @format is not overwritten when using a dummy documentation file
description:
When using a dummy documentation file to document two (or one) data sets, the default `@format` is not overwritten. However, when documenting the data from within data.R file, `@format` will overwrite the default. 

I encountered the issue when trying to combine documentation for multiple data sets into one file, but it appears the issue is more with the dummy file. 

**The following works, i.e., the default `@format` is overwritten:**
*data.R:*
```
#' Test data with shared description in this file
#'
#' Longer description for \code{t1} and \code{t2}
#'
#' @format Something besides the default format

"t1"

#' @rdname t1
"t2"
```


**While the following does not work, i.e., the default `@format` is not overwritten.** It results in format: An object of class `data.frame` with 10 rows and 2 columns.
*data.R:*
```
#' @rdname sharedDoc
"t3"

#' @rdname sharedDoc
"t4"
```
------
*doc.R:*
```
#' Test data with NULL documented
#'
#' Longer description for \code{t3} and \code{t4}
#'
#' @format A different format description that won't show up.
#' @name sharedDoc
NULL
```

The above continue to work/not work, even if only documenting one data set in each file.

If it helps at all, the minimum code is included in a skeleton package at https://github.com/rabutler/testBug

  b = NULL) #' description of argument b
{
  ret <- process_it(a, b)
  ret #' a character vector
}
```

would be equivalent to

``` r
#' Some function
#' @param a description of argument a
#' @param b description of argument b
#' @return a character vector
```

This came up on the @RDocTaskForce mailing list.

title: `roxygenise` fails when the `.Rbuildignore` file is empty
description:
When the `.Rbuildignore` file is empty, `roxygenise` throws an error with the message:

    !matches : invalid argument type

This is addressed in pull request #646.

title: Import only roclet
description:
When you add a new method to a generic defined in another package, you need to first import that generic. This makes it easy to get stuck in a state (e.g. https://github.com/ThierryO/testS4) that you can't easily get out without modifying the `NAMESPACE` by hand. 

One solution would be to have a separate roclet that works like `collate`. I think the translation from all the import directives is straightforward, so this should work. (But it can't do all namespace directives because `@export` definitely needs the loaded code)

title: generate roxygen from R code?
description:
It'd be nice if we could have something like `@evalRd`, but `@evalRoxygen`, which takes the output of some R function and treats it as though it were part of the current Roxygen block. For example, suppose you were documenting the same function multiple times, but it took different default arguments in different functions. It'd be nice to be able to write:

```
## function a
#' @eval roxygen_parameter(default = "foo")

## function b
#' @eval roxygen_parameter(default = "bar")
```

In this case, `roxygen_parameter()` is some function defined by the user in the package's namespace, and the output of that function is used to generate the documentation.

title: Using square brackets in back tips
description:
When using square brackets in back tips (e.g. \`X[i]\`) in the documentation, it produces some weird documentation.
Using the old-way with \code{X[i]} works fine.

title: allow 'inheritParams' + 'noRd' to work together
description:
Sometimes it's useful to have functions inherit documentation from a Roxygen block that itself shouldn't be written to a `.Rd` file, e.g.

```R
#' @param x A parameter.
#' @name docs
#' @noRd
NULL

#' @inheritParams docs
foo <- function(...) { ... }
```

Unfortunately, this doesn't work as `@noRd` completely wipes out the documentation object, so that `@inheritParams` now fails.

title: Better support for concepts
description:
* Check generated Rd
* Auto generate with family

title: Check file extension when identifying files in R to roxygenise
description: If a user does something silly like leave old documented code files in the R folder, but with the extension `.oldR`, `otheR`, etc. (such as I sometimes do when rewriting functions) Roxygen will still parse the Roxygen comments in those files, potentially leading to namespace weirdness. I'm guessing there's a regex call to blame that searches for `"r$"` rather than `"\.r$"`

title: Roxygen 5.0.1 clears DESCRIPTION file that was built with Roxygen 6.0.0 before
description:
I'm not sure whether I can reproduce this issue, but the steps were:

  * I updated packages on my Win Laptop, Roxygen was updated to 6.0.0
  * Later, when I used my Mac (R files synced via cloud), where I did not update packages and used Roxygen 5.x, the description-file was completely cleared when building my package (except for the RoxygenNote-line)

On both win and mac, I use R 3.3.2, RStudio 1.0.136 and use devtools to build packages.

title: don't underline parentheses for function links

description:
The following code throws a warning and does not produce a valid Description under roxygen 6.0.1

```

#'
#' `0.5\%`
#'
#' @md
#' @export
foobar <- function(){
  NULL
}
```

The following produce a valid description, but not as wanted:
```
#' 0.5\%     works (but is not verbatim text)
#' `0.5\\%`  produces verbatim 0.5\%  (so no error, but an unwanted extra backslash)
```

title: provide shorthand for roxygen templates + variables
description:
Rather than writing:

```R
#' @template foo
#' @templateVar x 1
#' @templateVar y 2
```

it would be nice if we could write:

```R
#' @template foo(x = 1, y = 2)
```

title: Templates and Markdown
description:
Template files in `man-roxygen` don't seem to respect Markdown mode: https://github.com/krlmlr/dplyr/commit/89b892f9aecd850d1484791c6f826b8e7e652a7b#commitcomment-20813612

CC @gaborcsardi.

title: Inherit examples
description: It seems there is currently no way to inherit the examples field. This would be useful for reexports.

description:
For instance, the following code produces an error:

```R

#' @return Density
wrapperDensity <- function(...) density(na.rm=TRUE, ...)
```

The error states:
`Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : object 'na.rm' not found`

title: @inherit Doesn't inherit description if not inheriting title
description:
This might be a feature rather than a bug, but the following doesn't seem to work as expected. Unless I include `@inherit title`, `@inherit description` doesn't work. 

Original function:
```
#' This is title
#' 
#' This is description
#'
#' @param x x
#' @param y y
#'
#' @return numeric vector
f1 <- function(x, y) x + y
```
Function that will inherit f1:

```
#' Different title
#'
#' @inherit f1 description 
#'
#' @inheritParams f1
#' @param z z
#'
#' @inherit f1 return
f2 <-function(x, y, z) x + y + z
```
This results in `\description{}` of f2 to be: "Different title". If I modify the title to `@inherit f1 title`, the `\description{}` of f2 is correctly inherited as "This is description"

title: @inherit causes an unexpected END_OF_INPUT warning
description:
Hi,

Consider this piece of code:
```R
#' @inherit base::file.path
catPath <- file.path
```
When I run `devtools::document()`, all goes well. However, if I then run `devtools::build()`, I get the following warning:

> Warning: [...]/man/catPath.Rd:34: unexpected END_OF_INPUT '

In the corresponding Rd file, I have:
```Rd
so as from \R 3.1.0 a trailing \code{/} or \code{\} is removed.
```

It seems like roxygen2 should have escaped the backslash to a double-backslash when processing the @inherit directive.

Cheers,
Florent

title: prompt becomes a question mark if Authors@R is NULL
description:
I am experiencing a problem when running devtools::document() with roxygen2 version 6.0.1 (version 5.0.1 seems unaffected).

My package is not using the Authors@R construct. When processing the package documentation file (with the "_PACKAGE" sentinel), eventually package_authors() is reached, which calls `parse(text = desc$`Authors@R`)`. My `desc` contains the following fields:
```
> names(desc)
 [1] "Package"     "Type"        "Title"       "Version"     "Date"       
 [6] "Author"      "Maintainer"  "Description" "License"     "URL"        
[11] "LazyLoad"    "Depends"     "Imports"     "LinkingTo"   "ByteCompile"
[16] "RoxygenNote"
```
So desc$`Authors@R` is NULL, hence parse() displays a `?` as prompt, which cannot be dismissed without an error.

Example of the roxygen comment: ```r #' Generate a request for the Sheets v4 API #' #' Generate a request, using some knowledge of the [Sheets v4 #' API](https://developers.google.com/sheets/api/reference/rest/). title: Documenting an object may corrupt Rd formatting
description:
I found that sfr is not formatted well by roxygen. (edzer/sfr#177)

Here is a minimal replex R file in [my repo for proof of concept](https://github.com/yutannihilation/roxygen2_NA_crs_test/blob/master/R/hello.R):

```r
#' Hello, world!
#'
#' This is an example function named 'hello'
#' which prints 'Hello, world!'.
#'
#' @name hello
# Exporting object seems not allowed.
hello <- "hello"

#' @rdname hello
#' @export
how_low <- function(x) UseMethod("how_low")

#' @rdname hello
#' @export
how_low.default <- function(x) "hello"

#' @rdname hello
#' @export
how_low.character <- function(x) "Nirvana"
```

This will result bellow with incorrect double backslashes:

```r
\usage{
hello

how_low(x)

\\method{how_low}{default}(x)

\\method{how_low}{character}(x)
}
```

I can't tell if this is a bug or intended behavior. Is this that roxygen2 does not allow us to document objects that is not a function or a dataset?
