title: output from tbl_df in code breaks read_lines_enc
description:
I think this was introduced in https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/pull/565

## Reproducible

```r
cat(paste(capture.output(tbl_df(mtcars)), collapse = "\n"), file="foo.txt")
con <- file("foo.txt")
head(readLines(con))
# Warning in readLines(con) : incomplete final line found on 'foo.txt'
# [1] "# A tibble: 32 × 11"                                                 
# [2] "     mpg   cyl  disp    hp  drat    wt  qsec    vs    am  gear  carb"
# [3] "*  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>"
# [4] "1   21.0     6 160.0   110  3.90 2.620 16.46     0     1     4     4"
# [5] "2   21.0     6 160.0   110  3.90 2.875 17.02     0     1     4     4"
# [6] "3   22.8     4 108.0    93  3.85 2.320 18.61     1     1     4     1"
con <- file("foo.txt", encoding = "UTF-8")
head(readLines(con))
# Warning: invalid input found on input connection 'foo.txt'
# Warning in readLines(con) : incomplete final line found on 'foo.txt'
# [1] "# A tibble: 32 "
```

Oddly enough:

```r
head(readLines("foo.txt", encoding = "UTF-8"))
# Warning in readLines("foo.txt", encoding = "UTF-8") :
#   incomplete final line found on 'foo.txt'
# [1] "# A tibble: 32 <d7> 11"                                              
# [2] "     mpg   cyl  disp    hp  drat    wt  qsec    vs    am  gear  carb"
# [3] "*  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>"
# [4] "1   21.0     6 160.0   110  3.90 2.620 16.46     0     1     4     4"
# [5] "2   21.0     6 160.0   110  3.90 2.875 17.02     0     1     4     4"
# [6] "3   22.8     4 108.0    93  3.85 2.320 18.61     1     1     4     1"
```

The errant line is: `# A tibble: 32 × 11`, where the problem is the `×` [multiplication character](http://www.fileformat.info/info/unicode/char/2715/index.htm). In the second code block, it shows this as `<d7>`.

Since `read_lines_enc` uses `con <- file(..., encoding)`, source files with console output from `dplyr` (for example) will fail:

```r
devtools::document("~/Projects/mypackage")
# Updating mypackage documentation
# Loading mypackage
# Loading required package: futile.logger
# Updating roxygen version in C:\Users\r2\Projects\mypackage/DESCRIPTION
# Warning: invalid input found on input connection 'C:\Users\r2\Projects\mypackage\R\mysource.R'
# Error in parse(text = lines, keep.source = TRUE, srcfile = srcfilecopy(file,  : 
#   C:\Users\r2\Projects\mypackage\R\mysource.R:537:0: unexpected end of input
# 535:   ###   ungroup()
# 536:   # # A tibble: 19,121 
#     ^
```

(My use case: I often include comments in my code that includes console representation of a mid-stage variable, either directly or from `str`, so that later debugging can see if/how the structure of the object has changed.)

Whether this is an underlying bug in R (or a nuisance "complaint" against `dplyr`) is a different issue. (I'd appreciate your thought on this, I'm not 100% certain.) Regardless, I suggest it might be useful to have some fallback mechanism in `roxygen2` in this situation. I have not found a way of reading this file correctly with `con <- file(...)` and `readLines(con)` without omitting `encoding`.

Side note:

```bash
$ file foo.txt
foo.txt: ISO-8859 text, with CRLF line terminators
```

Removing the multiplication symbol reverts it to ASCII, not surprising.

## Workaround

With just a global search/replace of that single character, both `readLines(..., encoding)` and `roxygenise()` succeed without warning.

```r
devtools::session_info()
# Session info -------------------------------------------------------------------
#  setting  value                       
#  version  R version 3.3.2 (2016-10-31)
#  system   x86_64, mingw32             
#  ui       RTerm                       
#  language (EN)                        
#  collate  English_United States.1252  
#  tz       America/Los_Angeles         
#  date     2017-02-06                  
# Packages -----------------------------------------------------------------------
#  package    * version    date       source                        
#  assertthat   0.1        2013-12-06 CRAN (R 3.3.0)                
#  backports    1.0.4      2016-10-24 CRAN (R 3.3.2)                
#  commonmark   1.1        2016-12-13 CRAN (R 3.3.2)                
#  DBI          0.5-13     2016-12-04 Github (rstats-db/DBI@238b676)
#  devtools     1.12.0     2016-06-24 CRAN (R 3.3.1)                
#  digest       0.6.12     2017-01-27 CRAN (R 3.3.2)                
#  dplyr      * 0.5.0.9000 2017-01-06 local                         
#  evaluate     0.10       2016-10-11 CRAN (R 3.3.2)                
#  htmltools    0.3.5      2016-03-21 CRAN (R 3.3.0)                
#  knitr        1.15.1     2016-11-22 CRAN (R 3.3.2)
```

title: Import and export are reordered, which prevents exports of imported objects from working
description:
I maintain the package DoE.base; I am currently working on removing an obstacle in my package that prevents the functionality from working if my package is not loaded and thus forces other packages to depend on the package. The issue below is concerned with how to enable roxygen users to obtain the namespace file in the form needed for my package to work without being depended upon.

My package heavily relies on objects (mainly orthogonal arrays) present in and exported from the package namespace. There are various functions in the package that rely on these objects being on the search path, and it would be a lot of work, sometimes probably also quite difficult, to locate and change all this code to explicitly refer to those objects in the unloaded package namespace. A straightforward solution is for users who want to make the functionality work from within their package but not depend on my package to export those crucial objects from their package namespace, after importing them from my package. 

This requires the namespace to import many objects from my package and *afterwards* export some of them; I am not an experienced roxygen2 user. When doing a small test package, I noticed that roxygen2 seems to move the imports after the exports, even if they are provided before the exports. Is there a way with roxygen2 to address a namespace requirement like the one outlined above?

Best regards,
Ulrike

title: Allow comments inside roxygen code
description:
I'd like to be able to have roxygen content that doesn't end up in the resulting Rd file. That is, a roxygen comment. (I know that roxygen already supports R comments in, e.g., the `examples` tag.)

My use case is for teaching people how to use roxygen, though it may be more widely useful for meta-documentation.

C-style comments are one option.

```r
#' /* Write the title */
#' ___
#' 
#' /* Write a description of the function */
#' ___
#' /* Add a parameter tag */
#' ___
#' /* Add a return tag */
#' ___
hypotenuse <- function(x, y) {
  x ^ 2 + y ^ 2
}
```

Full line comments starting hash + another character are another option.

```r
#% Write the title
#' ___
#' 
#% Write a description of the function
#' ___
#% Add a parameter tag
#' ___
#% Add a return tag
#' ___
hypotenuse <- function(x, y) {
  x ^ 2 + y ^ 2
}
```

I'd like to know if this sounds like a useful feature to anyone else, and if anyone has any opinions on the best syntax.

cc: @sumedh10 @machow @aimeegott

title: Add support for single files
description:
At the moment roxygen2 seems to only work for packages. However, not all code comes in the form of packages. Even though there’s an overwhelming consensus to use packages even for small analysis projects, it seems unnecessary to push this preference onto the user, since roxygen2 contains all the necessary functionality already, it just needs to expose it in its API.

There are at least two concrete use-cases for this (the second being relevant for me):
- [Single-file one-off Markdown reports](http://stackoverflow.com/q/18923405/1968) generated with [knitr](/yihui/knitr) or Sweave. Even though such reports can generally live without documentation, having it would still help during writing, and would promote writing better code from the start, which could later be put into a package
- [modules](/klmr/modules), a modern alternative to conventional R packages, which organises reusable code units in a fashion similar to Python and [JavaScript](http://nodejs.org/api/modules.html). The feature most sorely lacking from modules at the moment is support for documentation, and it would not make sense to reinvent the wheel, when there’s a perfectly fine tool out there.

title: markdown doesn't work within template files
description:
Reproducible example:

```R
setwd(tempdir())
devtools::create("roxlate")
setwd("roxlate")

cat(
	"Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE)",
	file = "DESCRIPTION",
	sep = "\n",
	append = TRUE
)

dir.create("man-roxygen")

cat(
	"#' @param x This is a link to [stats::rnorm()].",
	file = "man-roxygen/roxlate-rnorm.R",
	sep = "\n"
)

cat(
	"#' Foo.",
	"#'",
	"#' Description. Link: [stats::runif()]",
	"#' @template roxlate-rnorm",
	"#' @export",
	"foo <- function(x) {}",
	file = "R/foo.R",
	sep = "\n"
)

devtools::document()
writeLines(readLines("man/foo.Rd"))
```

This produces the file:

```
> writeLines(readLines("man/foo.Rd"))
% Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand
% Please edit documentation in R/foo.R
\name{foo}
\alias{foo}
\title{Foo.}
\usage{
foo(x)
}
\arguments{
\item{x}{This is a link to [stats::rnorm()].}
}
\description{
Description. Link: \code{\link[stats:runif]{stats::runif()}}
}
```

Note that the `[stats::rnorm()]` link was not processed, while the `[stats::runif()]` one was.

title: Namespace directive order should honour Collate order
description:
Currently, the namespace roclet sorts the directives, which causes check and loading warnings of the following sort:

```
Found the following significant warnings:
  Warning: replacing previous import ‘Rcpp::prompt’ by ‘utils::prompt’ when loading ‘pkgA’
```

These warnings can be avoided by forcing package import order in the `NAMESPACE` file.
However, this is not possible when this file is generated by roxygen, because of the default sort. 
Users should be able to control order by having the `@import` tags parsed in the correct order, which can be achieved easily if the namespace directives are output directly without sorting.

That is having :
```R
roclet_process.roclet_namespace <- function(x, parsed, base_path,
                                            global_options = list()) {
  ns <- unlist(lapply(parsed$blocks, block_to_ns)) %||% character()
  unique(ns)
}
``` 
instead of
```R
roclet_process.roclet_namespace <- function(x, parsed, base_path,
                                            global_options = list()) {
  ns <- unlist(lapply(parsed$blocks, block_to_ns)) %||% character()
  sort_c(unique(ns))
}
```

title: Bug: @describeIn fails when combined with @rdname
description:
When documenting S4 generics and methods I find that I often want to add several generics to the same documentation file (often setters and getters). In some circumstances it makes sense to change the name of the generated rd file to reflect this multiplicity.

When having @rdname in a generic and then using @describeIn for a method I wish to include in the documentation I get the following error:

```
Error: Failure in roxygen block beginning pgFull.R:118
Don't know how to describe s4method in data.
```

It seems adding @rdname messes up how roxygen infers the type. Removing @rdname and changing @describeIn accordingly removes the error...

``` R
NULL
```

title: WARNING: roxygen2 6.0.0 clears NAMESPACE and deletes man/*.Rd files
description:
**I'd flag this a HIGH-PRIORITY ISSUE, because if someone is not using version control and if someone is just starting to use roxygen2 6.0.0, there seems to be a risk that they loose their files.** (I hope I'm wrong)

Sorry, don't have much time today for more than a quick report: After updating to roxygen2 6.0.0, running `roxygen2::roxygenize()` will clear the `NAMESPACE` file (leaving a single line `# Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand`) and and delete all `man/*.Rd` files.

# Reproducible example
```sh
$ git clone https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson/listenv.git
$ cd listenv
$ Rscript -e "roxygen2::roxygenize()"
Writing NAMESPACE
Deleting as.list.listenv.Rd
Deleting cash-.listenv.Rd
Deleting cash-set-.listenv.Rd
Deleting get_variable.Rd
Deleting length.listenv.Rd
Deleting listenv.Rd
Deleting map.Rd
Deleting names.listenv.Rd
Deleting parse_env_subset.Rd
Deleting undim.Rd
```

As suggested by https://twitter.com/hrbrmstr/status/827476343264780290 and https://twitter.com/M2RUseR/status/827510563282485249, this is due to empty lines in `.Rbuildignore`;
```sh
cat .Rbuildignore 
#----------------------------
# Git and SVN related
#----------------------------
^.svn
^.git
^.make
INSTALL[.]md
OVERVIEW[.]md
README[.]md

#----------------------------
# Travis-CI et al.
#----------------------------
^[.]travis[.]yml$
^travis-tool[.]sh$
^pkg-build[.]sh$
^appveyor[.]yml$
^covr-utils.R$
^[.]covr[.]R$

#----------------------------
# R related
#----------------------------
^cran-comments[.].*$
^vignettes/.*[.](pdf|PDF)$
^vignettes/.*[.](r|R)$
^vignettes/[.]install_extras$
^Makefile$
^incl
^NAMESPACE,.*[.]txt$
^nohup.*$
^[.]R
^[.]benchmark
^[.]devel
^[.]test
^[.]check
^.*[.]tar[.]gz$
```

Commenting out or removing those empty lines in `.Rbuildignore` avoids the problem.

title: wrap_field_if_necessary() does not work with non-native encoding of DESCRIPTION file
description:

```

Error in if (longest.line > wrap.threshold) { :

In addition: Warning message:
In stri_length(string) :
  invalid UTF-8 byte sequence detected. perhaps you should try calling stri_enc_toutf8()
```

I have added a complete test case with a DESCRIPTION file in "latin1" encoding in my roxygen fork (https://github.com/WastlM/roxygen/commit/94ac5375423f91b0c303daa1349c6e0d63d695ac), which currently fails because of the above problem.

It seems to me as if the `value` argument of `wrap_field_if_necessary()` needs to be `iconv()`ed from the "Encoding" set in the DESCRIPTION (if present) to the native encoding, such that `str_length()` does not produce NA's and `str_wrap()` does not fail. 

Additionally, in `cat.description()`, the original encoding of the DESCRIPTION file has to be preserved. This issue has probably been addressed in #277.

title: Proposition: @importExcept tag
description:
A new tag `@importExcept` with the following semantics:
- `@importExcept package` adds an entry `importFrom(package,symbol)` for every symbol that `package` exports
- `@importExcept package exception1 exception2` adds an entry `importFrom(package,symbol)` for every symbol that `package` exports, except for symbols `exception1` and `exception2`

Rationale: If I know I'll be using many functions from a specific package, I'm inclined to simply say `@import package` and get done with it. However, there are drawbacks to this approach:
- If two imported packages have a symbol with the same name, warnings are issued when building or loading such a package
- From [R-exts](http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-devel/R-exts.html#Specifying-imports-and-exports): "Using importFrom selectively rather than import is good practice."

Benefits: Drop-in replacement for `@import` that shows explicitly (at least in the generated `NAMESPACE`) what is imported in the end, and allows safe resolution of collisions.

Drawbacks: Performance impact unclear.

title: devtools::document() error for global variable that uses an external function
description:
Hi,

I am trying to set some constants, i.e. read-only global variables, in a package I am writing. But I have a roxygen2 problem when running devtools::document():

```
> devtools::document()
Updating dummy documentation
Loading dummy
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) (from constants.R#4) : 
  could not find function "as.integer64"
```

The traceback looks like:

```
> traceback()
9: eval(expr, envir, enclos)
8: eval(exprs[i], envir)
7: source_one(file, envir = envir)
6: source_many(paths, env)
5: force(code)
4: withr_with_dir(file.path(pkg$path), source_many(paths, env))
3: load_code(pkg)
2: load_all(pkg)
1: devtools::document()
```

My minimal R example file, "constants.R" looks like this:

``` R
#' @importFrom bit64  as.integer64
NULL

CONSTANT <- as.integer64(123)
```

And the "Imports:" section of my DESCRIPTION file does list the bit64 package, so, there really is no reason that "as.integer64" should not be found.

Fully qualifying the external functions (replacing as.integer64 by bit64::as.integer64 in the code) allows devtools::document() to run through and generate the NAMESPACE file, as expected. From then on, it's possible to revert to "as.integer64" (not fully qualified) and to run devtools::document() again without issues. Try to remove NAMESPACE, do a "clean & rebuild" in RStudio, a devtools::document() and the problem pops up again.

Note that if I use roxygen2::roxygenize() instead of devtools::document(), the problem goes away.

Cheers,

Florent

PS/ R 3.2.5, roxygen2 5.0.1, RStudio 1.0.44

```
#' Calculation of block-wise topological overlaps
#'
#' Calculates topological overlaps in the given (expression) data. If the
#' number of variables (columns) in the input data is too large, the data is
#' first split using pre-clustering, then topological overlaps are calculated
#' in each block.
#'
#' The function starts by optionally filtering out samples that have too many
#' missing entries and genes that have either too many missing entries or zero
#' variance in at least one set. Genes that are filtered out are excluded from
#' the TOM calculations.
#'
#' If \code{blocks} is not given and the number of genes exceeds
#' \code{maxBlockSize}, genes are pre-clustered into blocks using the function
#' \code{\link{consensusProjectiveKMeans}}; otherwise all genes are treated in
#' a single block.
#'
#' For each block of genes, the network is constructed and (if requested)
#' topological overlap is calculated in each set. The topological overlaps can
#' be saved to disk as RData files, or returned directly within the return
#' value (see below). Note that the matrices can be big and returning them
#' within the return value can quickly exhaust the system's memory. In
#' particular, if the block-wise calculation is necessary, it is nearly certain
#' that returning all matrices via the return value will be impossible.
#'
#' @inheritParams adjacency
#' @inheritParams blockwiseModules
#' @param multiExpr expression data in the multi-set format (see
#' \code{\link{checkSets}}). A vector of lists, one per set. Each set must
#' contain a component \code{data} that contains the expression data, with rows
#' corresponding to samples and columns to genes or probes.
#' @param checkPower logical: should basic sanity check be performed on the
#' supplied \code{power}? If you would like to experiment with unusual powers,
#' set the argument to \code{FALSE} and proceed with caution.
#' individual TOMs into. The following tags should be used to make the file
#' names unique for each set and block: \code{%s} will be replaced by the set
#' number; \code{%N} will be replaced by the set name (taken from
#' \code{names(multiExpr)}) if it exists, otherwise by set number; \code{%b}
#' will be replaced by the block number. If the file names turn out to be
#' non-unique, an error will be generated.
#' @param individualTOMFileNames character string giving the file names to save
#' individual TOMs into. The following tags should be used to make the file
#' names unique for each set and block: \code{%s} will be replaced by the set
#' number; \code{%N} will be replaced by the set name (taken from
#' \code{names(multiExpr)}) if it exists, otherwise by set number; \code{%b}
#' will be replaced by the block number. If the file names turn out to be
#' non-unique, an error will be generated.
#' @return A list with the following components:
#'
#' \item{actualTOMFileNames}{Only returned if input \code{saveTOMs} is
#' \code{TRUE}. A matrix of character strings giving the file names in which
#' each block TOM is saved. Rows correspond to data sets and columns to
#' blocks.}
#'
#' \item{TOMSimilarities}{Only returned if input \code{saveTOMs} is
#' \code{FALSE}. A list in which each component corresponds to one block. Each
#' component is a matrix of dimensions (N times (number of sets)), where N is
#' the length of a distance structure corresponding to the block. That is, if
#' the block contains n genes, N=n*(n-1)/2. Each column of the matrix contains
#' the topological overlap of variables in the corresponding set ( and the
#' corresponding block), arranged as a distance structure. Do note however that
#' the topological overlap is a similarity (not a distance). }
#'
#' \item{blocks}{if input \code{blocks} was given, its copy; otherwise a vector
#' of length equal number of genes giving the block label for each gene. Note
#' that block labels are not necessarilly sorted in the order in which the
#' blocks were processed (since we do not require this for the input
#' \code{blocks}). See \code{blockOrder} below. }
#'
#' \item{blockGenes}{a list with one component for each block of genes. Each
#' component is a vector giving the indices (relative to the input
#' \code{multiExpr}) of genes in the corresponding block. }
#'
#' \item{goodSamplesAndGenes}{if input \code{checkMissingData} is \code{TRUE},
#' the output of the function \code{\link{goodSamplesGenesMS}}.  A list with
#' components \code{goodGenes} (logical vector indicating which genes passed
#' the missing data filters), \code{goodSamples} (a list of logical vectors
#' indicating which samples passed the missing data filters in each set), and
#' \code{allOK} (a logical indicating whether all genes and all samples passed
#' the filters). See \code{\link{goodSamplesGenesMS}} for more details. If
#' \code{checkMissingData} is \code{FALSE}, \code{goodSamplesAndGenes} contains
#' a list of the same type but indicating that all genes and all samples passed
#' the missing data filters.}
#'
#' The following components are present mostly to streamline the interaction of
#' this function with \code{\link{blockwiseConsensusModules}}.
#'
#' \item{nGGenes}{ Number of genes that passed missing data filters (if input
#' \code{checkMissingData} is \code{TRUE}), or the number of all genes (if

#'

#'
#' \item{nThreads}{ number of threads used to calculate correlation and TOM

#'
#' \item{saveTOMs}{ logical: were calculated matrices saved in files
```

description:
Per a brief convo on twitter with @hadley, I posit the creation of an `@figure` tag. Something like:

```
#' @figure stat_ash_01.png options: width="100\%" alt="Figure: stat_ash_01.png"
#' A sample of the output from \code{stat_ash()}:
#'
#' @figure statash01.pdf options: width=10cm

```

That makes:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/509878/12072831/d2f9578e-b0c4-11e5-8591-41672bb98aa9.png)

in the HTML docs and:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/509878/12072833/e9eeccee-b0c4-11e5-9fde-e9f104f714e7.png)

in the PDF/latex doc.

The current code - https://github.com/hrbrmstr/roxygen/blob/master/R/rd-tag-api.R#L204-L226 - uses the file type to determine the output target (i.e. `.png` => `\if{html}{…}`.

Anyone will quickly see that I based it off of the way `@param` works. Yes, this means the figures will be combined into one and the way I've got it implemented it makes a new `Figures` section (also obvious by the examples above), but that was the easiest way to at least make a start for this (and it took be a bit to grok how the tag processing is done today).

I'm open to suggestions and would be glad to take this on. Adding in checks to make sure that the files actually exist would be a next add for this. Also, the PDF/latex output is "meh" at best with this method so I need to poke at that a bit more. And, defaults for `options:` would be good to add as well. It also looks like I messed up something in the latex/PDF processing but this is just proof-of-concept. 

If this doesn't follow the `@param` idiom, then can I get a pointer as to how to do in-line `@` tag processing (if that functionality exists now).

title: FR: A robust way for defining collation order
description:
Collation order is given implicitly by topologically sorting the graph defined by `@include` relationships. The only way to ensure that a certain order is maintained is to add explicit links to the immediate parent. This "linear list" data structure is difficult to maintain, because each insertion/deletion requires a nontrivial update in two files.

Example: Assume three files D.R, B.R, A.R, and I want the files to be collated in that order. I can add `@include D.R` to B.R, and `@include B.R` to A.R, but if I add a new file C.R to appear between B.R and D.R, I need to update B.R to ensure the collation order.

I'm working around this by defining a parent for all source files which `@include`-s them. This parent contains.

``` r
#' @include A.R
#' @include B.R
#' @include C.R
#' @include D.R
NULL
```

The includes must appear _in reverse order_ with the current implementation, see also a [real example](https://github.com/rstats-db/DBItest/blob/a41829808022aceaa74e01b9c6ea4f69f92730bf/R/spec-.R).

How about a new `@collate` tag that define include-like dependencies in order of appearance? The entry `@collate D.R C.R B.R A.R` would be equivalent to `@include D.R` in C.R, `@include C.R` in B.R and `@include B.R` in A.R . Only tags defined in the same source file (or the same roxygen block?) would be considered jointly.

description:
A package that uses `#' @import` or `#' @importFrom` should declare these packages in the `Imports:` (or `Depends:`) section. title: Roxygen doesn't understand UseMethod("generic", x)
description:
Having battled through the R documentation, I don't see any objection to using `UseMethod` within an S3 method to dispatch again, but doing this breaks `roxygen2:::calls_use_method` which simply looks for whether `UseMethod` exists.

I want to do something like:

```
#' my method
#' @export
my_method <- function(x)
  UseMethod(x)

#' @describeIn my_method a class stuff
#' @export
my_method.a_class <- function(x)
 return("something")

#' @describeIn my_method determine class and re-dispatch
#' @export
my_method.default <- function(x)
  class(x) <- "a_class"
  UseMethod("my_method", x)
```

This works from an R point of view, and, although it is not a common use of UseMethod, it is the simplest way I can see to solve a more complicated problem in my package (https://github.com/jackwasey/icd9). Unfortunately, roxygen2 gives:
`Error: Don't know how to describe s3generic in s3generic.`
Commenting the second `UseMethod` lets roxygen run okay.

Incidentally, `NextMethod` is not the solution to this for multiple reasons, not least that you can't update the class passed to NextMethod.

title: Documenting a return function
description:
Hi,

I would like to document a function that is generated by my function.

For example:

``` R
#' Load a file, prefetch version
#'
#' @param path the root directory to save into
#' @param pattern The pattern to use to locate the files
#' @return A function that can be called with vds and year to get the
#' appropriate file from the precached list of files
#'
#' The closure function that will use the prefeched directory reading results
#'
#' The closure function has two parameters:
#'    vds =  the vds ids, as a list or vector; and
#'    year = the year of the data
#'
#' The closure function will return the file it finds as a dataframe
#'
#' @export
load.prefetch <- function(path,pattern='wim.*reduced.*vds.*imputed.*RData') {

    existing.files <- dir(path,
                          pattern=pattern,
                          full.names=TRUE,
                          ignore.case=TRUE,
                          recursive=TRUE,
                          all.files=TRUE)

    ## return a function that can be called that searches from this list

    callback <- function(vds,year){

        alldata <- data.frame()

        ## blah blah
        ## turn the file or files into a data frame

        ## vds could be an array, or it might not, collapse handles that
        for (vdsi in 1:length(vds)){
            ...
        }
        alldata
    }
    return (callback)
}
```

What I _want_ to do is something like http://usejsdoc.org/tags-callback.html, where I can "officially" document the parameters and return type of the function I return.  While I'm certainly no expert with jsdoc or with roxygen2, it looks like with jsdoc one can define a function's documentation separately, then use that definition inside other documentation blocks.

So above, I would write something like:

``` R
#' Load a file, prefetch version
#'
#' @param path the root directory to save into
#' @param pattern The pattern to use to locate the files
#' @return {my_generated_function} function
#' @export
load.prefetch <- function(path,pattern='wim.*reduced.*vds.*imputed.*RData') {

    existing.files <- dir(path,
                          pattern=pattern,
                          full.names=TRUE,
                          ignore.case=TRUE,
                          recursive=TRUE,
                          all.files=TRUE)

    ## return a function that can be called that searches from this list

    callback <- function(vds,year){

        alldata <- data.frame()

        ## blah blah
        ## turn the file or files into a data frame

        ## vds could be an array, or it might not, collapse handles that
        for (vdsi in 1:length(vds)){
            ...
        }
        alldata
    }
    return (callback)
}

#' A function to get the file(s) from the precached list of files
#'
#' @function my_generated_function
#'
#' This closure function will use the prefeched directory reading
#' results, so if the underlying directory contents changes, this
#' function will not reflect that case.  Use with caution
#'
#' @param vds the vds ids, as a list or vector; and
#' @param year = the year of the data
#'
#' @return a single data frame containing the contents of the file or
#'     files defined by the passed in vdsid(s) and year
#'
```

Here I mimicked the jsdoc use of parameters for the @ tags, which doesn't seem to be a feature of roxygen2.  The idea is to define the function documentation, and then be able to refer to that documentation block from within the main function block.  Otherwise it just floats around disconnected and the developer/user won't see it. 

I can also use a link tag, I guess.  Any advice would be appreciated (and then I can maybe write up an example for the R Packages document).

title: Tab vs space between #' and @

I'm using R version 3.3.0 on Rstudio 0.99.902 on Mac OS 10.11.6 (15G31).

I had the following in the preamble to one of my functions

```
#'  @title myFunction
#'  @param my.parameter.description

```

Note that there are two spaces between `#'` and `@`.  This is what Rstudio puts there if I type pound-singlequote-tab-atsign.  On `roxygenise()`, myFunction wasn't getting added to NAMESPACE.  I remembered some problem I had months ago about the spacing before the `@`, so I switched the preamble to this:


Note that now the `@export` line has only one space before the `@`.  
When I used `roxygenise()`, I got this error:

I switched all the lines to have a single space between `#'` and `@` and now `roxygenise()` works as expected.

title: Discrepancy between build_vignettes and document(roclets="vignettes")
description:
(Copy of [devtools:1145](https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/1145) which @hadley requested I file over here.)

If I call `build_vignettes()`, the built vignette files get placed into inst/doc/.

If I call `document(roclets="vignette")`, the built vignette files stay in vignettes/.

There is a discrepancy here. It arises most because in current versions of Rstudio, the only way I can find to build vignettes from the interface (without running a full check or build) is to run Document, with the option for vignette selected (which adds `vignette` to the list of `roclets` in `document`).

title: Roxagyn inserts non-allowed line break in usage-section
description:
A new line is created in the usage section (when not using the `@usage` tag) of the .rd file, when a function name with arguments exceeds a certain line length.
This is what roygen does (new line before "<- value"):

```
\usage{
set_labels(x, labels, force.labels = FALSE, force.values = TRUE, drop.na = TRUE)

set_labels(x, force.labels = FALSE, force.values = TRUE, drop.na = TRUE)
  <- value
}
```

While the CRAN check expects the second usage in one line:

```
\usage{
set_labels(x, labels, force.labels = FALSE, force.values = TRUE, drop.na = TRUE)

set_labels(x, force.labels = FALSE, force.values = TRUE, drop.na = TRUE) <- value
}
```

Using `@usage`, however, works:

```
@usage set_labels(x, force.labels = FALSE, force.values = TRUE, drop.na = TRUE) <- value
```

title: verbose output from roxygenize when needed?
description:
I was getting an error when calling roxygenize because I had some code in a file that wouldn't execute. it would have helped if there were a way to see which file was causing the error. One option would be to allow a verbose flag in roxygenize to change source_package to call this

lapply(paths, function(z) { cat("z=",z,"\n");sys.source(z, envir=env, keep.source=FALSE) })

in place of 

 lapply(paths, sys.source, envir = env, keep.source = FALSE)

a better thing might be to catch the error in sys.source and tell the user which file caused sys.source to throw an error. As it stands now, traceback() doesn't give helpful info about which thing was being sourced so I had act as if I was debugging source_package to figure out which file was causing it.

This is, obviously, an RFE, so I won't complain if you just close it. Now that I have figured out this situation I see that another option would have been to search the R/ folder for the call that I most recognized from traceback() to find what was causing the issue. But I'm not sure how many users would get that far.

Thanks for this amazing package!

title: Error parsing @importFrom statements
description:
Hi,

I have a package documented with Roxygen2. I decided to organize my main R file into several smaller ones. It all went well until I moved one of my @importFrom statements (#' @importFrom lattice trellis.device) to a new file.

A clean&rebuild in RStudio resulted in:

*\* preparing package for lazy loading
Error : object '(for' is not exported by 'namespace:lattice'
ERROR: lazy loading failed for package 'S001'

This is because the devtools::document() step generates a wrong NAMESPACE file, with entries like:

```
importFrom(methods,new)
importFrom(utils,"\\code{simpleError}")
importFrom(utils,"message,")
importFrom(utils,Create)
importFrom(utils,The)
```

The solution was the same as explained here, i.e. inserting a NULL after the @importFrom line:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/26386811/rstudio-roxygen2-importfrom-parsing-function-header

It was also discussed here:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/27364610/create-an-r-package-with-dependencies

Cheers,

Florent

the whole documentation (and build) failed, because of this section:

```
#' @example
#' dataset <- civicon_2014$sorts[,,"before"]
#' diag_forced(dataset = dataset,

```

This is to be expected, of course, but it took me a quite a while to figure out what the problem was, because the error message is not every informative (I think):

```
Loading pensieve
```

title: periods between names in @family attribute
description:
When a package contains only one unique `@family` tag, e.g.

```
@family scope-related functions
```

`roxygen2` mutates the name to

```
scope.related.functions
```

This seems to be caused by the definition of `invert`. A small reproducible example:

```
data <- structure(list(defer.Rd = "scope-related functions", scope_dir.Rd = "scope-related functions", 
    scope_env_vars.Rd = "scope-related functions", scope_options.Rd = "scope-related functions"), .Names = c("defer.Rd", 
"scope_dir.Rd", "scope_env_vars.Rd", "scope_options.Rd"))
roxygen2:::invert(data)
```

This could be fixed by avoiding the use of `stack()`, `unstack()` in `invert`: https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/blob/master/R/family.R#L29-L32

title: is_s3_generic fails on 'predict' method - is S4 method?
description:
I've got a simple class `"foo"` and I want to define some methods like `predict` and `coef`:

```
##' @export
foo <- function(mean, var) {
  fit <- nnls(cbind(mean^2, mean), mean+var)
  class(fit) <- c('foo', class(fit))
  fit
}

## @export
coef.foo <- function(object, ...) {
  co <- NextMethod(object)
  c(a=co[1], b=1+co[2])
}

##' @export
predict.foo <- function(object, newdata, ...) {
  co <- coef(object)
  with(newdata, co[1]*mean^2 + co[2]*mean)
}
```

However, this doesn't always work - sometimes `predict` and `coef` are recognized as methods (so `S3method` is generated in the `NAMESPACE` file), and sometimes not (so I get `export` in the `NAMESPACE`).  I've seen it go back and forth in the same project.

Looking deeper, I notice that `roxygen:::is_s3_generic` fails on, e.g., the generic `predict` method:

```
> roxygen2:::is_s3_generic("predict")
[1] FALSE
> roxygen2:::is_s3_generic("print")
[1] TRUE
```

I think this is probably because `predict` calls `standardGeneric("predict")` rather than `UseMethod`, right?  Does that make it an S4 method?  If so, what's the right way to document `predict` / `coef` methods with roxygen?

title: Clarify overwrite prevention.
description:
I just spent 10 minutes trying to workout what "NAMESPACE not generated by roxygen2. Skipped." actually meant.

I had interpreted it as "roxygen2 is not configured to write a NAMESPACE file" and I then spent some time trying to tweak rstudio/project options.

After a bit I realised it was trying to say: "The existing NAMESPACE file was not generated by roxygen2. Not going to overwrite it."

Could this warning text be adjusted to clarify the meaning?  e.g. "The existing NAMESPACE file was not generated by roxygen2, and will not be overwritten."

It's probably getting a bit verbose, but since Rstudio -> new project -> new package  automatically creates a NAMESPACE file, this is going to be a trip hazard.

title: Collision between function and S4 generic of same name
Proposal : could roxygen2 parse the R files in collate order, to improve @describeIn and @rdname
description:
#### Synopsis

Could 3 lines of code in roxygen2 be changed so that it **parses** the R files in collate order, when it is generating  documentation?  This would improve the readability of the generated documentation when using `@describeIn` and/or `@rdname` split across several .R files, as may happen when working with S4 classes, generic functions and methods. 
#### Background

The present version of roxygen2, 4.1.0, reads the R code files for a package in alphabetical order when it _parses_  them --- inside `roxygen2:::parse_package()` there is a line of code which says :  

`parsed <- lapply(r_files(base_path), parse_file, env = env)`  

`r_files(base-path)` returns a list of .r filenames in alphabetical order.

In contrast, both `roxygen2::roxygenise()` and `devtools::document()` _source_ the files in collate order.
#### Motivation

The consequence is that although the sourced code itself has been loaded in the correct (collate) order, the documentation that roxygen2 generates appears in the alphabetical order of the R files.  This doesn't matter most of the time, because often the contents of a single Rd file come from a single .r file.  

However when `@rdname <some-name>`, or `@describeIn <some-other-name>` have been used in more than one R file, and the _correct_ (i.e. collate order) is not alphabetical, it leads to the generated documentation appearing in the _wrong_ order.  This typically might happen when using S4 classes, or generic functions and methods.  For example if the method appears in a file which alphabetically precedes the file in which the generic function is created, the generated documentation describes the method first, and the generic function second, _even_ if `#' @include ...` has been used to specify the correct collate order for the files.  See the example below.
#### Proposed change

It requires changes to only 3 lines of code inside roxygen2 to have it parse the code files for a package in collate order.  

Two of those lines are in the `roxygen2:::package_files` function (in source.r) and also have the effect of making that function, which is currently only used by `roxygen2:::source_package`, behave more as I suspect is actually intended. At the moment `roxygen2:::package_files`  fails to deduplicate the list of file names that it returns, which means that `roxygen2:::source_package` will source the code files more than once. See the addendum to this example below for an illustration of this.

The third line to be changed is in  `roxygen2:::parse_package` itself.

If you are amenable to considering this change, I can easily submit a pull request. I have written a branched version of roxygen2 already while I was investigating why my documentation didn't look like I expected.
#### Example to illustrate the issue
##### File b.r is logically the first file, but alphabetically second.

It creates and documents a generic function, `f_gen`

``` r
#' @rdname Explanation
#'
#' @name Explanation
#'
#' @title First file in code logic order, but second file alphabetically.
#'
#' @details Alphabetically b.r is the second file, but in collate order it is the first.
#'
NULL

a <- 1

#' @title f_gen
#'
#' @description f_gen is a generic function
#'
#' @details The default f_gen just emits a simple message
#'
#' @param x The compulsory parameter
#'
setGeneric('f_gen', def = function(x) {message('I am f_gen, x was ', x)})

```
##### File a.r is logically the second file, but alphabetically first.

It creates and documents a method for `f_gen`

``` r
#' @include b.r
#'
#' @rdname Explanation
#'
#' @name Explanation
#'
#' @title Second file in code logic order, but first alphabetically.
#'
#' @details Alphabetically a.r is the first file, but in collate order it is the second.
#'
NULL

a <- 2

#' @describeIn f_gen
#'
#' @title f_gen_logical
#'
#' @description f_gen_logical is the method for f_gen when x is logical
#'
#' @details f_gen_logical is just a pseudo name for documentation purposes.  This is really an f_gen method with signature "logical".  It emits a different message to the f_gen default method.
#'
setMethod('f_gen', signature = "logical", def = function(x) {
  message('I am the f_gen method for a logical signature, x was ', x)
})
```
##### Rd for `f_gen` using current CRAN version of roxygen2

Using the a very recent github version of devtools with the CRAN release version of roxygen2 produces an .Rd file for `f_gen` which looks as follows.  The key point to note is that the documented description and details for the method come **before** the corresponding information about the generic.

```
% Generated by roxygen2 (4.1.0): do not edit by hand
% Please edit documentation in R/a.r, R/b.r
\docType{methods}
\name{f_gen,logical-method}
\alias{f_gen}
\alias{f_gen,logical-method}
\title{f_gen_logical}
\usage{
\S4method{f_gen}{logical}(x)

f_gen(x)
}
\arguments{
\item{x}{The compulsory parameter}
}
\description{
f_gen_logical is the method for f_gen when x is logical

f_gen is a generic function
}
\details{
f_gen_logical is just a pseudo name for documentation purposes.  This is really an f_gen method with signature "logical".  It emits a different message to the f_gen default method.

The default f_gen just emits a simple message
}
\section{Methods (by class)}{
\itemize{
\item \code{logical}: 
}}
```
##### Rd for `f_gen` generated using a branched version of roxygen2 with the proposed alterations

The key point to note is that the generic `f_gen` is described **before** the method in the documentation (which makes more sense to me). 

```
% Generated by roxygen2 (4.1.0.9001): do not edit by hand
% Please edit documentation in R/b.r, R/a.r
\docType{methods}
\name{f_gen}
\alias{f_gen}
\alias{f_gen,logical-method}
\title{f_gen}
\usage{
f_gen(x)

\S4method{f_gen}{logical}(x)
}
\arguments{
\item{x}{The compulsory parameter}
}
\description{
f_gen is a generic function

f_gen_logical is the method for f_gen when x is logical
}
\details{
The default f_gen just emits a simple message

f_gen_logical is just a pseudo name for documentation purposes.  This is really an f_gen method with signature "logical".  It emits a different message to the f_gen default method.
}
\section{Methods (by class)}{
\itemize{
\item \code{logical}: 
}}

```

title: roxygen2 doesn't respect collate order
description:
Suppose you have two files, `a.R` and `b.R`:

``` R
## a.R ##
#' @include b.R
NULL

#' Function a
#' @rdname funb
funa <- function() NULL
```

``` R
## b.R ##
#' Function b
funb <- function() NULL
```

Then the resulting .Rd file should have `funb` in the header, and `funb` should be listed first. But instead, `funa` is in the header and is listed first.

Here are the contents of `funb.Rd`:

``` R
% Generated by roxygen2 (4.1.1): do not edit by hand
% Please edit documentation in R/a.R, R/b.R
\name{funa}
\alias{funa}
\alias{funb}
\title{Function a}

funa()

funb()
}

Function a

Function b
}
```

title: Formatting of multiple args in help file
description:
This was reported to me by a student, so I'm not sure there isn't some other way to do this.

He had a function definition like this:

```
#' Show all relevant data on a student.
#' 
#' @param totalWeighting,cpWeighting,attendanceMethod,questionMethod See \code{\link{IDToCurrentGrade}}
#' @return A list with outputs from IDToName(), AssignmentMarks(), TestMarks(), IDToNotes(), and (if testWeighting is given) IDToCurrentGrade().
#' @export
foo <- function(totalWeighting, cpWeighting, attendanceMethod, questionMethod) {
      # content deleted  
}

```

The .Rd file ends up with a parameter entry like this:

```
\arguments{
\item{totalWeighting,cpWeighting,attendanceMethod,questionMethod}{See \code{\link{IDToCurrentGrade}}}
}
```

The problem is that without spaces after the commas, Rd2HTML forces the whole list of parameter names onto one line.  This makes the display really wide, pushing the descriptive text off screen.  The browser handles the wrapping nicely if there are spaces after the commas, but you can't put those into the .R file, because Roxygen treats spaces as the marker of the beginning of the descriptive text.

So I'd suggest that Roxygen should add a space after each comma when it produces the .Rd file.  Possibly this should require different input (e.g. \,) to allow the .Rd to be produced without spaces, but I don't really know any good reasons to do that.

title: feature request: Support for conditional @importFrom
description:
Some base-R functions are not available under all OSes.  If you want to use these functions in a cross-platform way, then you need to conditionally import the function.

Full discussion on [r-package-devel](https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-package-devel/2015q3/000478.html).

For example, `utils::win.version` is only available under Windows.  If your package includes a function that calls this, the NAMESPACE file should contain a conditional importFrom:

``` r
if(.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
importFrom(utils, win.version)
}
```

The way I'd typically write such a function would be this:

``` r
#' An OS-specific fn
#' 
#' This  fn uses win.version
#' @return The value of win.version, or NULL.
#' @importFrom utils win.version
#' #export
f <- function()
{
  if(.Platform$OS.type == "windows")
  {
    win.version()
  }
}
```

AFAIK, there currently isn't a way to specify the `@importFrom` line to make it conditional.  This would be a nice feature.

Possible syntax would be `#' @importFrom utils win.version .Platform$OS.type == "windows"`.  That is, anything after the function name up to a newline would be considered as a condition to go in an if block.

title: @export doesn't export S3methods correctly
description:
I am having a similar issue to the comments made on @hadley 's answer in this SO thread: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7198758/roxygen2-how-to-properly-document-s3-methods

If we take the SO example:

```
#' A description of MyHappyFunction
#'
#' A details of MyHappyFunction
#'
#' @title MyHappyFunction: The my happy function
#' @param x numeric number
#' @param ... other arguments
#' @examples
#' a <- 1
#' class(a) <- "lm"
#' MyHappyFunction(a)
#' @export
MyHappyFunction <- function(x, ...){
  UseMethod("MyHappyFunction")
}

#' @export
MyHappyFunction.lm = function(x, ...) {
```

title: Roxygen2 is not case sensetive
description:

title: Chaining @inheritParams together
description:
It was not clear to me in reading the documentation that one could not chain `@inheritParams` together. For example, the following does not work:

```
#' @title Foo
#' 
#' @inheritParams bar
foo <- function(value){ bar(value) } ;

#' @title Bar
#' 
#' @inheritParams baz
bar <- function(value){ baz(value) } ;

#' @title Baz
#' 
#' @param value A scalar
baz <- function(value){ value } ;
```

You get an error of `Error in rep.int(params, reps) : unimplemented type 'NULL' in 'rep2'`.

However, linking everything back to the original function does work, i.e., changing `#' @inheritParams bar` to `#' @inheritParams baz`.

My preference would be to add the functionality to chain the depths. In my real code, there are times where it makes sense to have depths of pass-through. From an architecture perspective, I like the idea of only having to worry about inheriting from the functions that are called inside of the each function, rather than tracking the tree all the way down to the node. 

If adding this functionality is not possible, perhaps we can update the documentation to notify that this is not possible and provide an error message that is a little more obvious.

title: update_collate removes existing Collate field whenever there are no @include directives
description:
This issue manifested itself while I was trying to use devtools on a package with S4 classes defined in different files.  To get `devtools::load_all`  to work on the package, it needed to know the collate order, which I specified by using `@include` directives.  But I needed to run `roxygen2::update_collate` to have those `@include` directives processed and placed into the Collate entry in the DESCRIPTION file, before `devtools::load_all` would succeed.

While trying to add a call to `roxygen2::update_collate` into (a forked development copy of) `load_all`, it emerged that some of the testthats in devtools had become unhappy.  I tracked it down to the disappearance of Collate entries in the DESCRIPTION files of templates for testthat.  The templates in question do not have `@include` directives, but did have manually entered Collate fields.  My modified copy of `load_all` with a call to `roxygen2::update_collate` that had been called while running the devtools tests, wiped out the Collate entries that previously were there.

@hadley advised that this was probably a bug in update_collate - hence this issue.

See devtools/#623 for a minimal example ->  \link{https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/623}

The sessionInfo from the test case demonstrating this behaviour was 

```
> sessionInfo()
R version 3.1.1 (2014-07-10)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)

locale:
[1] LC_COLLATE=English_Australia.1252  LC_CTYPE=English_Australia.1252   
[3] LC_MONETARY=English_Australia.1252 LC_NUMERIC=C                      
[5] LC_TIME=English_Australia.1252    

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] roxygen2_4.0.2

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] Rcpp_0.11.2   stringr_0.6.2 tools_3.1.1 
```

PS It's not as simple as not changing the collate entry if one already exists:  
1. If the user **is** using `@include` directives, there might be an outdated Collate field that ought to be refreshed.  
2. But if the user is entering the Collate field manually (which you might be able to _guess_ if there are no `@include` directives found in the package code) then you should leave it alone.

title: "@concept" slot instead of "@concepts" as in vignette, Rstudio and official doc
description:
## Problem

The `@concepts` tag [don't seems to exists](https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/search?q=concepts&ref=cmdform&type=Code) in _roxygen_. But there is a `@concept` one without the final _s_  that work.

The problem is :  
- `@concepts` is describe in [vignette "usage"](https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/blob/3c1608540458bb94117a19b189341769594a8dde/vignettes/rd.Rmd), line 129

> `@concepts` to add extra keywords that will be found with `help.search()`
- `@concepts` is autocompleted in RStudio 0.98.983 when writing `@conc` then tab
- The keyword described in the [official documentation](http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Indices) is `concepts`
## Possible solutions
- rename `@concept` to `@concepts` this way it's consistent with official doc but it will be confusing because people will want to put serveral concepts in a same line.
- rename `@concepts` to `@concept` in vignette and in RStudio autocompletion. I believe that's the more relevant way.

`concepts` is not a critical part for R documentation to my mind (I almost never use `help.search()`) then this bug is not important but may be confusing.

title: failed to catch unclosed brace
description:
In a package that I am developing, roxygenize() and devtools::document() failed to find a unclosed brace in a file that defined an S4 object (line 13 in lcens-class.R). It did generate an error in a subsequent file that defined functions that created the object (as.lcens.R). I have included the original version of the files so that you can see the error.

I was able to fix the error in the full package and it documented just fine with roxygenize(). But, I did spend a lot of wasted effort in looking at the wrong file.

Thanks. I do like the new version of roxygen as it makes documenting S4 objects and methods a lot easier.

```

#'

#'
#' @name as.lcens

#'are permitted.

#'are permitted. Detection limits are required for each non-missing value in \code{values};
#'they will be imputed if missing. The imputation scheme is fairly sophisticated, see
#'Lorenz (in preparation) for details, so it is better to set to missing, rather than
#'provide an arbitrary detection limit.
#' @param censor.codes optional codes indicating a left-censored value. If class
#'"logical," then \code{TRUE} indicates left-censored. If class "character,"
#'then "<" indicates left-censored and anything other than "" or " " generates

#'analysis of left-censored data.

#'\code{detlim}. All \code{values} that are less than \code{detlim} are treated
#'as left-censored values at \code{detlim}. This ensures unbiased analytical results.
#' @references Lorenz, D.L., in preparation

#' @examples
#'
#'## The first value is censored at 2
#'as.lcens(c(1,3), 2)
#'## Set the first value to censored at that level and the detection limit is
#'# carried forward
#'as.lcens(c(1,3), censor.codes=c("<", ""))
#'
setGeneric("as.lcens", function(values, detlim, censor.codes) standardGeneric("as.lcens")
           ## Coding history:
           ##    2012Mar01 DLLorenz Conversion to R/new style
           ##    2012Mar22 DLLorenz Conversion to S4
           ##    2012Jul24 DLLorenz Modified dfns to produce typeof = "numeric"
           ##    2012Aug03 DLLorenz Added detlim="missing" signatures to as.lcens.
           ##    2012Sep17 DLLorenz Added values="qw" signature to as.lcens
           ##    2013Jan13 DLLorenz Roxygenized
           ##    2013Jan13          This version
)


lcens-class.R:
#' @title Left-censored Data
#'
#' @description Class "lcens" describes left-censored data.
#'
```

title: `roxygenise` clobbers .Rd files for functions with the same name, but different case
description:
Consider the following trivial example.

``` R
#' This is a test function
#' 
#' Hello world!
#' 
#' @param x any object
#' @return \code{x}
#' @export
test <- function(x) {
  x
}

#' Test function 2
#' 
#' This is another function with different case and signature to \code{test}.
#' @param x any object
#' @param y any object
#' @return A \code{list} of \code{x} and \code{y}
Test <- function(x, y) {
  list(x, y)
}
```

If I call `roxygenise` on my package (either manually or through RStudio), Its output clearly tells me that both `test.Rd` and `Test.Rd` are written. However looking in the `man/` directory, only `test.Rd` exists, and it contains the documentation for `Test` not `test`.

So there are two issues here:
1. If two functions have the same name, but a different case, the files and documentation are clobbered.
2. If the two functions are in the same file:
   - The filename for the .Rd file is the first occurring function.
   - But the contents of the .Rd file is for the last occurring function.
3. If the two functions are in different files:
   - The name and contents of the .Rd is for the function in the first file (alphabetically sorted).
### The use case I have that makes this naming convention a non-terrible design choice

I am implementing some functions in `Rcpp`. These functions are not exported to the namespace of my package (but I've documented them anyway), and I've provided wrapper functions, which are exported to the namespace. The exported wrapper functions I've written are in camelCase (e.g. someFunction), while the wrapper functions generated by Rcpp start with an uppercase letter (e.g. SomeFunction). This clobbering will be problematic for any functions starting with a letter > R (i.e. the file occurs after RcppExports.R)

title: Arguments order with @inheritParams
description:
When using @inheritParams, the arguments are not necessarily listed in the right order in the .Rd file created. By right order, I mean the argument order in the usage section.

Here is an example. Let's say I have two functions:

fct1 <- function(r, K){...}
fct2 <- function(r, p, K){...}

In the roxygen2 documentation of the first function I use the following tags:
# ' @param r description of argument r
# ' @param K description of argument K

For the second function, I use the following tags:
# ' @param p description of argument p
# ' @inheritParams fct1

After processing my code with roxygenize, the .Rd file for the function fct2 presents the arguments in the following order: p, r, K (not r, p, K as I would have expected).

title: Please provide option to forgo automated deduction that function containing a "." is a S3Method

A couple remarks:
1. Seems like when dropping `@docType`, `@rdname` and `@aliases` you now **must** provide a `title` to the methods (which previously you didn't need to) as otherwise you'll see the following [error](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/13137912/rd-file-name-conflict-when-extending-a-s4-method-of-some-other-package). I couldn't find anything about this in the documentation so far.
2. If for `foo()` you still **do** use `@rdname foo-method` to combine help for method(s) and generic to _one_ help file then this seems to "override" the `@family` functionality. This might be intended as when using `@rdname foo-method` there are no explicit help files for the methods anymore and thus linking via `@family` doesn't really make sense; maybe still worth a note in some documentation file, though.

Related SO posts: 
- http://stackoverflow.com/q/7356120/989691
- http://stackoverflow.com/q/13137912/989691

title: Ability to add class-specific alias without generic alias
description:
This is clearly an issue with S4 methods, but may also apply to S3 generics.

The following roxygen-header for a class-specific method extension to the base S4 generic, `show`, should add just a specific alias to the Rd file (here it would be `myPkgSpClass-class.Rd`). However, it also adds the generic alias (`\alias{show}`) to the documentation as well. This causes a conflict with the base documentation for `show`, and is a problem that could result in lots of disambiguation-forks in the doc-UI of a package that has lots of specific extensions to already-available methods:

``` R

#' @export
#' @aliases show,myPkgSpClass-method
#' @rdname myPkgSpClass-class
setMethod("show", "myPkgSpClass", function(object){ show(NA) })

```

In fact there should be no conflict, and the `myPkgSpClass`-specific alias of `show` should point to the `myPkgSpClass-class` documentation instead. 

This issue was first described as a question on StackOverflow, and further details can be found there:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/8947483/how-to-add-class-specific-alias-without-generic-alias-using-roxygen2

title: @importFrom pkg fn != just calling pkg::fn()
description:
The 'namespace' vignette says:

> If you are using just a few functions from another package, call them explicitly with `pkg::fun()`.  I no longer recommend using `@importFrom`.

As far as I can find, this is the only mention of `@importFrom` in all of the roxygen2 documentation. However, as far as I can tell, these two things are not quite equivalent. For example, if I have an S3 function `foo()` in a package `pkgA` and wish to add a `foo.bar()` method in a package `pkgB`, I can write

``` splus
#' @importFrom pkgA foo
#' @method foo bar
#' @export
foo.bar <- function(x) {
  message("Hello world!")
}
```

and everything works fine. However, if I instead write

``` splus
#' @method foo bar
#' @export
foo.bar <- function(x) {
  pkgA::message("Hello world!")
}
```

I receive the error

> object 'foo' not found whilst loading namespace 'pkgB'

when running `document(clean=TRUE)` (as an aside, I still receive this error even when I go back to the first option, unless I completely delete the `NAMESPACE` file), which goes against the suggestion that the two methods are equivalent.

title: Errors caused by `load_all` in `document`
description:
This is basically reopening issue https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/407 in the sense that I am able to reproduce the example with an MWE where I do the following with two skeleton packages:
package `foo` exports `f`. package `bar` has `@importsFrom foo f` so it can use it in a function `b`. I `document` and `install` both packages and everything is fine. I then change the name of `f` to `ff` and change to `@importsFrom foo ff`. Now when I `document` and `install` `foo` things are fine, but I get an error when I do it for `bar` because `f` is not exported by `foo`. 

I think it comes back to @hadley 's comment that "`document()` first needs to run `load_all()` to load the package." In other words, my understanding is that `document` requires that the `NAMESPACE` file is perfectly correct (and valid, which was addressed a bit in https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/pull/220). Is my understanding correct? If so, why make that assumption? The point of me running `document` is that I want `roxygen` to create the `NAMESPACE` file for me. Why should `document` assume that it is correct to begin with? In my opinion, one of the first lines of `document` should be to delete the `NAMESPACE` file (if it exists), and write it from scratch. What am I missing here?

I currently read `NAMESPACE` files because the index is generally clustered with all functions, not just exported, in a package. However, I never realized one could use `@keywords internal` to change that, which I just learned by reading the vignette. 

My question is, would it make sense to have anything not exported via `@export` have a `@keywords internal` automatically attached to it (similar to what you do if `@description` is missing)? I am just thinking that having a default perspective of "everything is internal unless explicitly stated otherwise via `@export`" makes a lot of sense. Plus I don't want to go back and edit hundreds of little functions through all of my packages ;)

title: `roxygenize` does not seem to respect `@importFrom`
description:
When I use `roxygenize` on packages I write, I continue to get warning messages about function names overwriting each other even though I have intentionally used `@importFrom` to avoid such conflicts.

I have been able to create a MWE that produces this error. I constructed a skeleton package with barebones files and only edited the `help.R` file, which is very simple:

```
#' @docType package
#'
#' @import lubridate
#' @importFrom plyr ddply
NULL
```

I have chosen `lubridate` and `plyr` because I know these packages have a common function, `here`.

When I call `roxygenize(package_directory)` (where package_directory is a variable holding the path to the package), I get the following output:

```
Loading required package: plyr
Loading required package: lubridate

Attaching package: ‘lubridate’

The following object is masked from ‘package:plyr’:

    here
```

But why would `plyr`'s `here` mask `lubridate`'s even though I explicitly told it not to? What is also odd to me is that the `NAMESPACE` file is generated correctly even though the text shown on screen earlier would lead me to believe it wouldn't:

```
import(lubridate)
importFrom(plyr,ddply)
```

I wrote a function in the package that simply returns the value of `here` to find out which version of the function is being used and it is the `lubridate` version, which is counter to the output to the `roxygenize` call. 

So, what is happening with the text output from `roxygenize`? Is it wrong, in that `plyr`'s `here` is never actually used? Or is it used somewhere that is not clear? 

On a side note, when I use `document` instead of `roxygenize`, I don't see the notification that the function has been masked and the `NAMESPACE` file generates correctly. 

So, why does `roxygenize` not work here but `document` does? And when should each be used?

As for versions, I am up to date:

title: roxygen2 generates non-passing Rd syntax for S4 methods dispatching on <-
description:
This is pretty much of an edge case so it might be lower priority, but I am the author of the `formula.tools` package.  In this package, I define an S4 method on the `<-` class.  For example, to get the right-hand side of an assignment expression, I define the following:

``` r
#' @rdname formula.parts

setMethod( 'rhs', '<-', function(x) x[[3]] )
```

title: ReferenceClass method documentation generates error for parameterised methods
description:
I have a reference class, say `Blob`, that has some methods defined by a function elsewhere. This function has one argument, say `type`. 

```
draw.Blob <- function (type = 'small') 
{
   type <<- 'small'
}

Blob <- setRefClass (
  Class = "Blob", 
  fields = list(type = 'character'),
  methods = list(draw = draw.Blob)
)
```

When running `document(clean=TRUE)` and then `check_doc()`, I get the following error:

```
> check_doc()
Updating packageName documentation
Checking documentation
Blob-class.Rd: non-ASCII input and no declared encoding
problem found in ‘Blob-class.Rd’
```

When I delete the `type` parameter from `draw.Blob`, the error message goes away. There are no obvious issues with the Rd file that was generated - and certainly no obvious (visible) non ASCII characters in the Rd file.

Perhaps a separate issue is that when I change the `draw.Blob` docstring or even remove the function's parameter, and run `document()`, it doesn't pick up the change. When I run `document(clean=TRUE)` the change is picked up (unsurprisingly).

title: @templateVar doesn't work properly
description:
Using @templateVar doesn't assign to a variable named by the specified name; it assigns to a variable named templateVar (because the names in partitum are tag names and propagate through).

The solution is simple: set the names to the names they should be in template.R:

```
  var_tags <- partitum[names(partitum) == "templateVar"]
  vars <- lapply(var_tags, "[[", "description")
+  names(vars) <- sapply(var_tags, "[[", "name")
  vars <- lapply(vars, type.convert, as.is = TRUE)
```

```
##'  @rdname foo
fun_bla <- function(...)
```

And the second has 

```
##' 
##'
##'  gula gula
##'  @rdname foo
fun_gula <- function(...)
```

The resulting file will end up with 

```
\description{General description
gula gula}
```

And I want `gula gula` to end up into \details section. This was working fine in older roxygen. 

Second issue is with merging different roxygen entries without specifying which function it refers to. So, with the above example the end Rd entry is simply:

```
bla bla
gula gula 
```

Instead of the more useful:

```
\describe{
\item{fun_bla}{
   bla bla
}
\item{fun_gula}{
    gula gula
}}
```

It applies to \description as well as \details Rd secsions. 

This is how multiple roxygen entries were merged in old version of roxygen2.

Any ideas?

Thanks.

title: @slot not being processed correctly
spurious Warnings: @inheritParams: can't find topic XXX
description:
Dear Hadley,

I encounter spurious warnings that topics are not found for S4 methods where no "normal" function of that name exists. 
I set up a minimal example package at  cbeleites / roxygenize-inheritparams .

I think the problem is the inheritParam checking in https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/blob/s4/R/roclet-rd.R l. 257

``` R
       rd_name <- names(Filter(function(x) inheritor %in% x, name_lookup))
```

name_lookup contains the full aliases, e.g.  "mean_sd,numeric-method", but inheritor is "mean_sd" only. As there is no "normal" function mean_sd, the matching doesn't succeed.

``` R
       rd_name <- names(Filter(function(x) inheritor %in% sub (",.*$", "", x), name_lookup))
```

seems to fix it.

I'll send you a pull request (hoping I don't mix it up again...)

Best,

Claudia

title: cannot @inheritParams when params are multiply defined?
description:
It seems that if a param is doubled, like so:

```
#' ...
#' @param log,log.p logical; if TRUE, probabilities p are given as log(p)
#' ...
```

later on you cannot inherit, via `@inheritParams`, either of `log` or `log.p`.

Here is a MWE that I cooked up (I originally thought using aliases was the problem):

```
#' @title a minimum working example, first part.
#'
#' @usage
#'
#' foo.func(x,y,z)
#'
#' bar.func(a,b,c)
#'
#' baz.func(m,n)
#'
#' @param x,y some parameters of foo
#' @param z some parameter of foo
#' @param a,b some parameters of bar
#' @param c some parameter of bar
#' @param m some parameter of baz
#' @param n some parameter of baz
#' @return typically return the first input.
#' @aliases bar.func baz.func
#' @export 
foo.func <- function(x,y,z) {
    return(x)
}
#' @export 
bar.func <- function(a,b,c) {
    return(b)
}
#' @export 
baz.func <- function(m,n) {
    return(m)
}
#' @title a minimum working example, second part.
#'
#' @usage
#'
#' dep.func(x,z,a,m,alpha)
#'
#' @param alpha some parameter of dep
#' @inheritParams foo.func
#' @inheritParams bar.func
#' @inheritParams baz.func
#' @return just returns \code{a}
#' @export 
dep.func <- function(x,z,a,m,alpha) {
    return(x+z+a+m+alpha)
}
```

When I roxygenize this, I get the warnings:

```
Warning: @inheritParams: can't find topic bar.func
Warning: @inheritParams: can't find topic baz.func
...
snip
...
* checking Rd \usage sections ... WARNING
Undocumented arguments in documentation object 'dep.func'
  ‘x’ ‘a’

Functions with \usage entries need to have the appropriate \alias entries, and all their arguments documented.
The \usage entries must correspond to syntactically valid R code.
See the chapter ‘Writing R documentation files’ in the ‘Writing R Extensions’ manual.
```

The first warning, about unfound topic, is probably somewhere else in the issue tracker; the latter, however, is earnest: the `x` and `a` end up undocumented.

title: Wrapping of `\preformatted`
description:
I've been trying to insert some instances of `\preformatted` into my roxygen markup, each line less than 60 characters.

Since roxygen2 seems to ignore newlines in markup (that aren't double newlines) and wrap at 60 characters, the text within my `\preformatted` all gets mashed into one line and wrapped at 60 characters.

That makes my 'preformatted' appear all distorted in the Rd/text help.

Is there a workaround for this? A `@verbatim` tag that tells roxygen to respect newlines within markup?

Example replicating my problem:

```
#' test documentation
#' @details
#' \preformatted{
#'                     /a\\                                 
#'                     |b|                                  
#'   /x y 0 0 -ux -uy\\|d| = /u\
#'   \\0 0 x y -vx -vy/|e| = \\v/                          
#'                     |g|                                  
#'                    \\h/                                  
#' }
#
f <- function()
{
    return(NULL)
}
```

(I put in the double backslashes just in case. And just for interest, in reality, this will be nested in an `\ifelse{latex}{ ...latex version of the equation... }{ ASCII version for the text help file }`).

This shows up in the .Rd (and text help) as :

```
Details:
      /a\ |b| /x y 0 0 -ux -uy\|d| = /u\ \0 0
       x y -vx -vy/|e| = \v/ |g| \h/ 
```

This is a result of all the lines being formed into one and then wrapped at 60.

title: @imports should also modify DESCRIPTION
Handle names<- and $<- and [
description:
In version `roxygen2_2.2.2` it is not possible to document methods for:
- `names<-`
- `$<-`
- `[`

Here is some reproducible documentation code:

```
#' Updates names and variable.labels attribute of surveydata.
#' 
#' @param x surveydata object
#' @param value New names
#' @method names<- surveydata
#' @export 
  NULL
}


#' Extract or replace subsets of surveydata.
#' 
#' Extract or replace subsets of surveydata, ensuring that the varlabels stay in synch.
#'
#' @param x surveydata object
#' @param name Names of columns
#' @param value New value
#' @method $<- surveydata
#' @export 
"$<-.surveydata" <- function(x, name, value){
  NULL
 }

#' Extract a subset of surveydata.
#' 
#' @param i row index
#' @param j column index
#' @param drop logical. Passed to \code{\link{[.data.frame}}. Note that the default is FALSE.
#' @param ... Other arguments passed to \code{[.data.frame}
#' @export 
#' @method [ surveydata
"[.surveydata" <- function(x, i, j, drop=FALSE){
  NULL
}
```

---

Using the examples as they stand, `roxygen2` doesn't produce a valid filename:

```
> {document(pkg); check_doc(pkg)}
Updating surveydata documentation
Skipping invalid filename:  -cash-set.surveydata.Rd 
Skipping invalid filename:  -open-brace.surveydata.Rd 
NULL
```

So, I add:

```
#' @name extract 
```

and

```
#' @name names<-
```

Now a valid file is produced, but new `R CMD check` warnings:

```
> {document(pkg); check_doc(pkg)}
Updating surveydata documentation
Writing extract.Rd
NULL
Objects in \usage without \alias in documentation object 'extract':
  '$<-.surveydata'

Objects in \usage without \alias in documentation object 'names<-':
  'names<-.surveydata'
```

---

At the moment, one needs to use a workaround to produce valid documentation:

```
#' @usage \\method{names}{surveydata}(x) <- value

#' @usage \\method{$}{surveydata}(x, name) <- value
```

title: Roxygen should add @importFrom automatically
description:
Allowing you to override with `@importFrom` if it guesses wrong.

``` R

library(codetools)

#' Scans a function and determines what functions it uses from other packages.
#' 
#' @param f function to process
#' @param imported list of functions that are already imported
auto_imports <- function(f_name, imported = NULL) {
  f <- get(f_name)
  globals <- findGlobals(f, merge = FALSE)$functions
  this_pkg <- environmentName(environment(f))

  loaded <- loaded_funs(this_pkg)
  matches <- setdiff(intersect(names(loaded), globals), imported)
  source <- loaded[matches]

  source_length <- vapply(source, length, integer(1))
  ambiguous <- source_length > 1
  if (any(ambiguous)) {
    pkgs <- lapply(source[ambiguous], paste, collapse = ", ")

    message("In ", f_name, ", multiple possible sources for: \n", 
      paste("  ", names(pkgs), ": ", pkgs, collapse = "\n", sep = ""))
  }

  vapply(source, "[", 1, FUN.VALUE = character(1))
}

loaded_funs <- function(exclude = NULL) {
  base <- c("stats", "graphics", "grDevices", "utils", "datasets", 
    "methods", "base", exclude)
  pkgs <- setdiff(loadedNamespaces(), base)
  envs <- setNames(lapply(pkgs, asNamespace), pkgs)

  invert(lapply(envs, ls))
}

invert <- function(L) {
  t1 <- unlist(L)
  names(t1) <- rep(names(L), lapply(L, length))
  tapply(names(t1), t1, c)
}
```

title: Generate file pkg-internal.Rd based on @keyword internal
description:
This is an idea of new feature.

R documentation says:

```
The special keyword ‘internal’ marks a page of internal objects that are not 
part of the package's API. If the help page for object foo has keyword ‘internal’, 
then help(foo) gives this help page, but foo is excluded 
from several object indices, including the alphabetical list of objects in 
the HTML help system.
```

There is also file pkg-internal.Rd dedicated for documenting internal stuff:

```
if a package pkg contains user-level objects which are for “internal” use only, 
it should provide a file pkg-internal.Rd which documents all such objects, and
 clearly states that these are not meant to be called by the user
```

It would be nice to generate the file pkg-internal.Rd based on chunks that are flagged with `@keyword internal`.
It could simply contain a list of short descriptions and links for each separate topic.

In fact, one may argue that chunks that have no tag `@export` should be considered documenting internal objects and automatically get a keyword 'internal' if it is relevant, with some exceptions for chunks with e.g. `@doctype package` or S4 and S3 methods for exported generics.

title: roxygenize modifies author text in the package DESCRIPTION
description:
## Background

I currently don't expect roxygen to write out the "Author"  field of my package DESCRIPTION. And, back in April @Hadley explained that [**roxygen only writes the collate directive of a DESCRIPTION file**](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/5757855/why-doesnt-roxygen-write-package-info-to-description#comment-6604975). 

But I'm running [roxygen 2.1](http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/roxygen2/) (from CRAN), and as far as I can tell it's re-writing my author field. Below, I've included steps to reproduce the problem, as well as a screenshot of the diff that results. I apologize that reproducing the problem requires cloning down my git repository. 
## Steps to reproduce the problem
1. clone down the granovaGG github repository. At a terminal, type:
   
   ```
   git clone git@github.com:briandk/granovaGG.git
   ```
2. Navigate into your local granovaGG repository and check out [this commit](https://github.com/briandk/granovaGG/commit/80f8f0022ea1a445d434f7211a5c5e249bbed201) (again at a terminal)
   
   ```
   git checkout 80f8f0022ea1a445d434f7211a5c5e249bbed201
   ```
3. From a clean R session, run the following commands, replacing `path/to/local/repository` with the actual path to your local granovaGG repository:
   
   ```
   library(roxygen2)
   roxygenize("path/to/local/repository")
   ```
## Expected Behavior

Nothing. The package has already been run through `roxygenize`, and the author list is formatted as I'd like it. Nothing should change.
## Actual Behavior

`roxygenize` seems to rewrite the DESCRIPTION file. Running step 3 above produces this output in an R session:

``` r
> roxygenize("granovaGG")
Updating collate directive in  [redacted]/granovaGG/DESCRIPTION 
```

And examining the diff in files shows:

![Reformatted authorship output in DESCRIPTION file](http://briandk.com/screenshots/roxygenizeDiff-20110830-102539.png)

title: Unwanted quotation marks around aliases with commas
description:
This affects especially S4 method documentation, which has an alias naming convention that builds on the generic using no-space commas as delimiter to indicate the signature, and ending with "-method" without the quotes. (http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#Documenting-S4-classes-and-methods)

The quotes are probably necessary during internal text-handling, but need to be removed from the final \alias{ } tag in the Rd file.

The following example S4 extension of the "show" method illustrates the problem:
# ' @name show
# ' @aliases show show,helloworld-method
# ' @docType methods
# ' @rdname show-methods
# ' @export

setMethod("show", "helloworld", function(object){
    cat("Hello World!")
    cat("\n")
})

Is translated by the latest version of roxygen2 to the following Rd file:

\docType{methods}
\name{show}
\alias{"show,helloworld-method"}
\alias{show}
\title{Show the helloworld class to standard output.}
\arguments{
  \item{object}{A \code{helloworld} object.}
}

I have also created an example package and put on github: ( https://github.com/joey711/testpkg ) . It builds and loads fine, but throws the following errors during <R CMD check testpkg> because the S4 methods appear undocumented (even though they are):
- checking for missing documentation entries ... WARNING
  Undocumented S4 methods:
  generic 'helloworld' and siglist 'array'
  generic 'helloworld' and siglist 'character'
  generic 'helloworld' and siglist 'function'
  generic 'helloworld' and siglist 'helloworld'
  generic 'helloworld' and siglist 'integer'
  generic 'helloworld' and siglist 'list'
  generic 'helloworld' and siglist 'logical'
  generic 'helloworld' and siglist 'matrix'
  generic 'helloworld' and siglist 'numeric'
  generic 'print' and siglist 'helloworld'
  generic 'show' and siglist 'helloworld'
  All user-level objects in a package (including S4 classes and methods)
  should have documentation entries.
